about_text.value: A law-bound age of knights where Camelot is both court, relic-shrine, and civic constitution. Power is not simply land but visible legitimacy: oaths to the Round Table, the defense of widows and exiles, the maintenance of the Grail, and the balancing of four forces - Arthur's peace, Lancelot's divided loyalty, Mordred's claim, and the old magic held by Merlin and Morgan. Stakes include the stability of succession, the survival of ordinary people outside court, the return or disappearance of sacred objects, and whether Camelot remains a just republic, a doomed chivalric ideal, a broken throne, or a different kingdom born from ruin. Every scene asks what the player values when honor, love, duty, and law point in different directions.

encounters.title: Arthur, Merlin, and Gawain face a succession crisis in which Camelot's peace, th

text_script.value: At the relic-shrine before dawn, Arthur sets the empty thrones of the Round Table in a crescent while Merlin traces the succession line in candle-ash. Gawain stands at the threshold, half knight and half judge, and names the three tensions aloud: Arthur's peace, Lancelot's divided loyalty, and the Grail's silence. 'If the old oath binds us to a peace that starves the exiles,' Merlin murmurs, 'then the oath has become a cage.' Gawain answers that law without honor is only fear wearing a crown, and the shrine seems to hold its breath.
Hold the oath of the Round Table
Arthur recommits the court to the oath, forcing Gawain to mediate with the exiles and pushing Mordred's challenge toward the succession crisis later.
Negotiate the oath with the excluded
Merlin drafts a conditional pact that broadens legitimacy but risks breaking the old solemnity and inviting Lancelot's divided loyalty into the open.
Send Gawain toward the Grail
Gawain departs toward the Grail, removing one judge from the council and shifting the succession question onto Merlin and Arthur alone.

encounters.title: Arthur, Merlin, Mordred and Lancelot confront an empty seat; Gawain's absence an

text_script.value: At dawn the oathhall empties of ceremony and fills with hunger: outside the walls, widows and exiled craftsmen crowd the gate, while inside Arthur stands beside an empty throne and a sealed shrine whose basin does not reflect the candles. Mordred does not shout; he sets a worn ring on the stone, smiling like a law with teeth, and asks whether legitimacy may be inherited, bought, or rescued from the dead. Lancelot stays one pace behind the king, neither naming Guinevere nor renouncing her, while Merlin traces a broken seventh line in ash and says the Round Table has only two true rooms: oath and necessity.
Hold a public oath-feast
Arthur forces Mordred to answer openly before knights and exiles, exposing peace to public judgment but making Lancelot's divided loyalty break open rather than remain a private doubt.
Admit exiles to judge the seat
The court widens legitimacy beyond birthright, yet Mordred claims the shrine was built to crown him and turns the question from succession into a contest of who is allowed to speak.
Ask Merlin to read the Grail first
Merlin reaches for the sealed basin and the succession becomes a revelation rather than a settlement, stripping Arthur of sole control and letting Lancelot choose whether to follow law or love.

encounters.title: Arthur, Mordred, Lancelot, Guinevere, Merlin and the Lady of the Lake face a Gra

text_script.value: On the threshold of the relic-shrine, the empty basin reflects not candles but a drowning star, and the Lady of the Lake steps down from the mist with a shard of silver on her tongue. Arthur says the peace cannot be rebuilt by kings alone, while Mordred answers that the shard is proof a new inheritance already moves beneath the oath; Lancelot, nearer to Guinevere than to the throne, hears her name as both sin and law. Merlin turns the shard over and warns that whoever claims the Grail must carry the exiles' grief with it.
Bind the Grail to the exiles

Arthur and the Lady of the Lake pledge that no claimant may touch the shard until the excluded are fed, judged and admitted as witnesses, sharpening legitimacy but provoking Mordred to contest the seat directly.
Let Lancelot name love or law
Lancelot speaks openly before the court, exposing Guinevere and forcing Arthur and Merlin to answer whether honor can survive outside the oath or must be surrendered to it.
Remake the seat as a common hall
Arthur turns the empty throne into a seat of judgment for widows and exiles, winning public support but ceding kingship's simple claim and inviting Mordred and Lancelot to dispute the new order.

encounters.title: Gawain returns wounded and searching, Morgan forces Camelot to answer need rathe

text_script.value: At the third hour of the relic-hall, Gawain comes back through the black door with his hand still wrapped in linen and refuses to call the breach a wound; he says the Round Table's peace is now a debt owed to the people who were already outside it. Morgan steps out of the narrow passage that no knight can open, not to crown Arthur or accuse him, but to ask who will carry succession, Grail, exile and peace when the King says he cannot. Mordred keeps his ring in his pocket and asks whether a crown should be judged by its blood or by the number of bellies it keeps alive, while Bedivere sets the shard-key on the table and the candle-wicks lean toward it as if listening.
Swear a bridge oath with Gawain

Arthur and Gawain turn the throne into a visible pledge to judge widows, exiles and broken oaths, winning public support but forcing Mordred and Morgan to argue whether rank may serve need or must break.
Let exiles choose the seat of judgment
The law widens beyond birthright and begins to survive the war, but Mordred claims the shrine built for him while Morgan invokes an older compact older than the Round Table.
Read the shard as judge of the table
Merlin opens the old binding and the Grail becomes the examiner of Arthur's rule, stripping the King of sole control and showing exiles that legitimacy is a sacred burden rather than a title.

encounters.title: Camelot's throne is being tested by an exile line, a wounded Gawain, the shard-k

text_script.value: Outside the black-door stair, the exile line has stopped at the shrine edge, hunger kept visible as children lean on staffs and widows carry empty bowls into the candlelight. Morgan lets the silence harden and says that a crown that cannot answer bread is only a claim with a candle behind it. Gawain holds his wrapped hand out toward Arthur rather than the shard, telling him the wound must be made answerable or the oath is a fiction. Merlin lifts the small silver key, while the Lady of the Lake opens the mist around the threshold and names the thing they are afraid to say: legitimacy now lives in who is admitted to be wounded, fed, and judged.
Pledge bread before crown
Arthur makes the first public pledge feed and judge the exiles, winning the gate but inviting Mordred and Morgan to argue that the seat has been emptied by its own justice.
Bind the shard to Gawain's wound
The Round Table accepts a healing quest tied to the shard, turning Grail, wound, and Round Table into one oath but risking a pilgrimage that can be called piety or debt by either side.
Admit exiles as witnesses of the table

The table gains an unstable new legitimacy because the excluded can speak, judge, and remember, while Arthur, Mordred, and Morgan are forced to choose whether the Round Table survives as a court, a commons, or a contested chapel.

encounters.title: Exiles admitted at the shrine, Lancelot and Guinevere standing at the threshold

text_script.value: The morning after the pledge, the exile line has not left the shrine threshold: children sleep against staffs, widows carry empty bowls, and the shard-key on the table has begun to glow a shade warmer than the candlelight. Lancelot crosses the hall at a measured pace with Guinevere at his shoulder â€” the first time either has faced the table in this crisis â€” and says that the oath he swore to Arthur cannot feed a child, yet the vow he keeps for the Grail will not sit quietly beside one. Merlin lifts his wrist, and the old binding answers in a thin, strained shimmer, holding only what is chosen rather than what is hoped. Mordred does not deny the bread; he asks whether a table that feeds its enemies is still a Round Table, or a different thing wearing its shape.
Bind the table to the fed exiles

Arthur anchors the Round Table to visible justice, winning the exiles' standing but forcing Mordred and Morgan to argue that the shrine has emptied itself of its sacred power and that the oath now belongs to whoever is hungry.
Let Lancelot carry both oaths
Lancelot is given a public double charge and the court gains an uneasy keeper of both peace and Grail, while Arthur's trust in the table splits along the very line Guinevere and Lancelot draw.
Carry the shard to the exiles

The Grail becomes visible and audible to the excluded, deepening the peace among the people but stripping Arthur of sole control of the sacred object and warning Merlin that the old binding may splinter.

encounters.title: The noon council has stalled at the shrine: exiles are fed and present, the shar

text_script.value: The noon bell is still sounding when the shrine threshold fills with a line of cloaks, staffs, widows, and children, and Arthur sets the warm shard-key down on the black altar rather than around his neck. Lancelot says, in a voice meant to be heard by the table and not only by Guinevere, that an oath carried alone is a knife carried alone; Guinevere adds that she will not be made an unseen wall between two promises. Morgan looks from Mordred to Merlin and names the coming cost aloud: if the exiles are fed and judged, the Round Table stops being only a court and becomes a commons that has to survive its own conscience.
Make the Round Table a commons

Arthur gives the exiles standing to judge and be judged, winning lasting legitimacy for the poor but turning the Round Table into a public assembly where Mordred can argue that oath, bread, and crown have been deliberately fused.
Let Lancelot witness both oaths
Lancelot and Guinevere take the peace and the Grail into one shared visible office, gaining trust but forcing the court to choose between personal loyalty and an oath that cannot be wholly kept.
Let the shard judge the claim

The shard is placed in the disputed throne space as a witness, allowing Arthur, Mordred, and Morgan to make their claim under sacred judgment but risking that the old binding reads the choice as a verdict rather than a question.

encounters.title: The shrine stands as a contested border: exiles have entered but are not fully j

text_script.value: The noon bell has faded into a low ring, and the shrine threshold no longer looks like a line between insiders and outsiders: the exiles have crossed it, but their children still face away from the table and toward the roads. Merlin, standing at the binding, says the old vow cannot be asked to govern two wills at once, and that if both Arthur and Mordred keep naming themselves its keeper it will answer the louder voice. Lancelot and Guinevere stand shoulder to shoulder at the edge of the court and argue, quietly but unmistakably, whether witnessing an oath means keeping it or being the proof it fails. Mordred does not shout; he asks what the shrine is for if its light can no longer decide whose claim is honest.
Bind the Round Table to the sworn exiles

Arthur makes the shrine a public commons where exiles may judge and be judged, buying lasting legitimacy for the poor while Mordred and Morgan argue that the sacred oath has been dissolved into politics.
Send the shard outward with the excluded

The Lady of the Lake carries the sacred light toward the roads, strengthening trust among the excluded but stripping Arthur of sole control and warning Merlin that the old binding may splinter under wider sight.
Give Mordred a public office under the table

Mordred becomes guardian of the roads, widows, and exile claims rather than rival king, dividing succession into competing oaths and forcing Lancelot, Guinevere, and Arthur to decide whether divided loyalty can be governed.

encounters.title: The shrine is split by dusk: exiles sit at the table unjudged, the shard-key coo

text_script.value: By dusk the shrine's light has stopped choosing. Arthur stands at the black altar with the shard-key cooling in his hand, and around the table the exiles have taken their places, some weeping and some laughing too loudly, while Mordred, seated at the empty west chair, says that an oath built to be only one thing has already been killed. Merlin, hands pressed to the binding, warns that whatever the court does next, the old law will answer the clearest voice, and that both men are shouting. Guinevere tells Arthur that she would rather be unjudged by the oath than judged by it, and Lancelot answers that witnessing without bearing weight is only another way of carrying nothing.
Split the Round Table into two sworn offices
Arthur keeps the peace while Mordred swears to the exiles' road, making legitimacy negotiable and survivable but forcing Lancelot and Guinevere to choose between loyalty and love.
Carry the Grail vessel past the threshold
Lancelot carries the sacred light into the exiles' camp, turning it from crown-sign into common trust but inviting Morgan to call the act a theft.
Let the binding judge Arthur and Mordred separately
Merlin asks the old law to answer each claimant in turn, risking a sacred verdict that may divide the Round Table in two rather than settle the succession.

encounters.title: The shrine stands grey and contested: the shard-key hovers over the altar, exile

text_script.value: By the third bell the shrine has gone grey, and Merlin lifts the shard-key above the black altar as if it weighed more than the crown it was meant to choose. Morgan, dust still on her hem, says the old magic never promised one table, only one law, and asks whether the Round Table can serve two claims without ceasing to be itself. Mordred rises and names the roads, the widows, and the exiles as the only witnesses the oath has ever truly kept, while Lancelot says the Grail must never be made a bargaining chipâ€”and Guinevere answers that it never was.
Let Guinevere swear openly beside Arthur
The love becomes a public oath rather than a secret, forcing Lancelot to choose between keeping silent and breaking with Arthur, while Arthur's peace is visibly made conditional.
Let the exiles hold the shard-key
The excluded are asked to set the terms of succession, but Mordred and Morgan argue that the sacred oath cannot be handed to those the crown cast out.
Let the binding answer both claimants
The old law gives a sacred verdict that divides the Round Table rather than settles succession, and Morgan uses the split to demand that the magic be governed, not merely invoked.

encounters.title: The shrine is split by the shard-key's unsettled verdict; the Lady of the Lake h

text_script.value: Morning comes back grey, and the shrine stands split down the middle: the east pillar still holds its candle, the west is dark, and the shard-key hangs between them, not settling. The Lady of the Lake comes through the east gate carrying the Grail wrapped in grey wool and says that it was never stolen; it has waited three leagues east, and it answers whoever carries it least easily. Lancelot answers that a relic treated as a prize is only a treasure with ceremony, while Mordred says that the road has no chairs at all, only witnesses, and that the exiles outside the broken threshold have already kept one oath better than any of them. Morgan, dust still on her hem, asks what the old law will say when it is asked to choose between a crown and a road, and Arthur does not know which half of the shrine he wants to light.
Send a party east to find the Grail
Lancelot leads a small party under his own oath, turning Arthur's peace into a journey and leaving the shrine open to Mordred's claim while the exiles watch the road open for them.
Seal the shrine and guard the Grail in place

Arthur swears the Grail to the shrine as a common trust, but Mordred and Morgan argue that a sealed sacred object is a closed door, and the exiles must decide whether to remain witnesses or walk away.
Let the exiles set the terms of the Grail's return

The excluded are asked to speak first at the shrine, forcing Arthur to choose between letting them set the terms or refusing them the table, with Lancelot and Guinevere forced into public agreement or public rupture.

encounters.title: The shard-key has chosen the threshold over the crown, the grey-wrapped Grail br

text_script.value: At the second dusk the shard-key chooses a voice, but not a person: it flares under the exile beside the threshold and dims under the crown. The Lady of the Lake unwraps one grey corner and lets the Grail catch only the east wind; Lancelot says a thing too heavy to carry is not sacred enough to rule, while Morgan replies that a crown fearing the wind has already lost the argument. Mordred names the roads, the widows and the exiles as the only living law, and Arthur, with the oath still warm on his tongue, asks who may carry both the crown and the threshold.
Set the threshold before the crown
The exiles are seated inside the broken shrine and the oath becomes a negotiated commonwealth, but Mordred gains legal claim over the roads and Morgan forces the bargain into writing.
Open the east road to the Grail
A small party takes the Grail three leagues east, Arthur's peace becomes a journey, and Lancelot must choose between public vow, secret protection, or leaving the shrine undefended.
Name the Grail a trust, not a prize
Merlin and Morgan force the oath into a written trust with the exiles, denying Mordred possession but winning him a legal opening, while Arthur must either rule openly or lose the shrine's authority.

encounters.title: The written terms stand unsettled, the exiles hold the threshold but no one has

text_script.value: The bargain was written but the ink had not settled. The exiles at the threshold named the terms they would guard â€” the widows' alms, the return of the graves, the toll at the broken gate â€” and asked who would answer if any of them failed. Lancelot, kneeling before the shrine, said that a trust with no answerer is only a wish wearing paper, and Guinevere answered that an answerer who cannot be blamed is no better than a crown with no law. Morgan demanded that the crown itself swear, while Mordred stood apart and said the road's own law was no chair at all, only witnesses. The shard-key woke and trembled above the written words, and Arthur, with the grey Grail still breathing east, found himself saying that someone would answer, and not naming himself. The Lady of the Lake watched the key, and smiled once: it answers whoever carries it least easily, and she had begun to think that the easy carriers were the ones who needed to be tested.
Arthur swears as answerer

Arthur binds his own name to the written terms, the crown gains weight but Guinevere and Lancelot feel the oath swallow the exiles' claim, and Mordred presses the crown as hostage to a road it no longer governs.
Share the answer between knight and exile
Lancelot and the leading exile take paired oaths, the trust gains a human face, but the exiles gain real power over the shrine and Mordred's claim is forced into the open rather than settled.
Let the shard-key choose the answerer
The shard-key answers before any oath is spoken, the trust takes a relic-like life of its own, and Arthur must either accept a shrine that decides for him or break the key's verdict.

encounters.title: The written terms are unsettled, the key is choosing the answerer, the exiles gu

text_script.value: By first grey light the written bargain no longer lay on the altar; it curled like a page trying to leave, while the shard-key stood over it with a faint sound like a bell under water. Lancelot had his hand on the oath-line and the leading exile had her thumbprint beside his, but the key blinked and all three faces changed together, as if the paper itself were listening. Mordred leaned over the threshold and asked whether a road may be owed to its heirs, and Arthur answered that a road owed to its heirs is no longer a road but a captivity dressed as law. Around them the Grail still breathed east through one grey-wrapped seam, and no one trusted the east to stay only a direction.
Let Lancelot and the exile swear paired under the key
A human answerer enters the bargain, the exiles gain real standing inside the shrine, and Mordred receives a legal opening rather than a defeat.
Let the shard-key decide the answerer
The trust takes a relic-like authority over Arthur's court, the exiles are bound by a voice not chosen by knights, and Merlin and Morgan must either consecrate or challenge that choice.
Arthur breaks the key's verdict and swears alone
The crown answers for the bargain, the exiles fear a throne wearing law, and Mordred gains a stronger claim because the shrine's authority is split between oath and ruin.

encounters.title: The key has moved the bargain past words into a living verdict, the exiles hold

text_script.value: The shard-key fell silent the instant the leading exile pressed her thumbprint into the paper, and every line of the bargain burned brighter than the candlelight, as though the words had finally learned to breathe. Lancelot, on one knee, felt the trust pass through him like a draft through a gap in a wall, and the exiles at the threshold shifted their weight in a way that did not match their fear. Mordred did not rage. He said, quietly, that a key that answers for a bargain has already answered for its heirs, and that someone should either tell the court what that means or ask the key to name the man who holds the east. Merlin bent his grey brow toward the Grail's breathing seam and said the old magic would not thank anyone for naming it before the court did. Guinevere watched the two oath-thumbprints and asked whether a trust with one witness and no judge is law, or only a promise that survives its first failure.
Arthur asks the key to name the judge
The key points beyond the court toward the Grail's east, Merlin is forced to argue that the shrine itself must rule, and Mordred's claim becomes a public question of who the shrine answers to.
Guinevere rules that law comes before the relic
The paired oath is hardened into an enforceable court, the shrine is forced to submit to visible judgment, and Merlin and Morgan unite against a law that treats the Grail as an ordinary charge.
Arthur offers Mordred a seat beside the oath-line
Mordred is pulled into the bargain as a witness rather than an enemy, his claim becomes impossible to ignore, and the shrine answers to a divided court that no longer agrees about its own future.

encounters.title: The key has moved from verdict to motion, the shrine is pressing the court towar

text_script.value: The key no longer burned in a circle; it crept, one pale degree at a time, toward the east seam where the Grail breathed. Gawain stepped into the light and asked why the court was still arguing whether the oath was real while the shrine itself had already decided. Merlin answered that a shrine that decides for itself is not a judge, only a hunger wearing a crown, and Mordred murmured that perhaps the heirs should let it eat first. Guinevere looked at Lancelot's thumbprint, still faintly warm, and asked the court what honesty would cost if the answer had to be sworn aloud. The exiles at the threshold did not move, but their stillness had changed from fear into something closer to attention.
Arthur seats the whole Round Table as judge of the bargain

The oath becomes civic constitution under living eyes, Lancelot is sworn in as witness rather than legend, and Merlin and Morgan begin to doubt whether a court of knights can hold a relic-shrine without breaking either.
Lancelot names his divided loyalty aloud
The exiles receive an answer that is honest and unstable, Arthur's peace loosens as the court hears what the Round Table is really owed, and Mordred gains a public question rather than a private one.
Merlin seals the east seam with old magic
The Grail is guarded at the cost of visibility, the court loses its clearest witness, and Mordred sees a door left ajar behind the shrine's calm.

encounters.title: The exiles stand in the open, the shrine answers to no one's crown, and the Roun

text_script.value: The seam in the shrine's eastern wall no longer glowed like a candle; it inhaled, and the exiles at the ashen threshold felt the court lean toward them. Mordred set his sword flat across his knees and said that a claim which waits for permission has already lost, and Arthur answered that the court's oath was not permission but a rule, and a rule that bends is not saved by being honored. Guinevere asked Gawain what it would cost to hold both peace and oath while the shrine itself chose a third thing. Merlin watched the Grail's breathing seam and said that old magic remembers what courts prefer to forget.
Arthur declares the oath binds all, Mordred included

Mordred is forced into public hearing as a claimant rather than an enemy, the exiles gain standing before the court, and Merlin and Morgan openly question whether a rule that ignores power can survive.
Guinevere assigns a judge to the bargain

Law enters the shrine's circle and the oath becomes enforceable in public, but the relic is forced into the role of a witnessed charge, and the Round Table splits over whether that is justice or capture.
Lancelot steps forward to absorb the cost

Lancelot accepts the burden of the divided oath as his own, Arthur's peace is bought at the price of Lancelot's remaining in the court, and Mordred gains a public question rather than a private answer.

encounters.title: The exiles have entered the consecrated hall, the oath-cloth is slipping toward

text_script.value: At the threshold, Bedivere spread the oath-cloth across the Grail hollow and felt it slide toward the dark east seam, as if the shrine were no longer listening to the court. Morgan asked whether law could still be carried in a pocket, and Mordred answered that heirs who wait for permission are heirs in waiting. Arthur did not answer; he lifted the exile-gate, and the people beyond the ash-field entered the hall as one held breath, still, watching the circle of sworn knights. Guinevere set her hand upon the first exile's shoulder and named the bargain: peace, oath, or relic would no longer be separate answers.
Arthur seats the exiles as witnesses to succession
Exiles gain public standing and Mordred must answer before them, Arthur's peace weakens, and the oath becomes a civic act rather than a shrine command.
Lancelot refuses to choose between peace and loyalty
Lancelot names the price of divided loyalty aloud, Gawain and Guinevere move toward the shrine as witnesses, and Mordred receives an unresolved question instead of a private verdict.
Morgan asks Merlin what the old magic would do now
Merlin reframes the Grail as a negotiation rather than a verdict, and Morgan presses the court to decide whether the relic should be kept, returned, or released to the exiles.

encounters.title: The oath has become a live civic boundary, Merlin and Morgan press the Grail as

text_script.value: The oath-cloth did not reach the seam; it pooled at Arthur's feet like mercury remembering a river. Merlin bent close and said the Grail was not a bowl to be kept but a boundary wearing a bowl's shape, and the exiles beyond the ash-field had not yet agreed which side of that boundary they stood on. Mordred raised one hand and asked whether the crown of Camelot was the same thing as the table, and Guinevere answered that if it was, then its only true heir would be the law that could let Mordred, Lancelot, and the exiles remain in it together. Arthur did not deny it; he touched the edge of the cloth and felt the shrine inhale once, toward the light outside the hall.
Arthur reads the covenant aloud
The court reframes peace as a public civic oath with the exiles as signatories, giving Mordred standing but making Arthur's peace depend on whether the Round Table can trust ordinary people.
Lancelot binds himself to the seam
Lancelot accepts the Grail as his divided oath, the court splits between guarding peace and following the relic, and Gawain is left to choose whether to witness or refuse that choice.
Morgan opens the old magic
Morgan and Merlin let the old power answer the exiles' need, but the threshold becomes ungovernable and Arthur's crown and the Round Table are pulled toward a different kingdom.

encounters.title: The covenant is read and Mordred has accepted the question of succession rather

text_script.value: Arthur spoke the covenant until the exiles heard it as one sentence: no exile would be turned back, no knight would keep the relic for himself, and no heir would inherit by birth alone. Mordred rose slowly, then seated himself at the table's edge, and when Arthur asked whether he accepted, Mordred answered that he accepted the question. Guinevere turned to Lancelot and said quietly that the oath was not a wall around love but a road through it, and Lancelot gripped his own wrist as though to hold himself to the path. Merlin circled the shrine, reading the seam the way a scribe reads a wound, while Morgan murmured that the old magic had been a ledger once and was being asked to settle it all at once.
Arthur seats Mordred beside him

Mordred gains public standing and peace is founded on inclusion, but Gawain, Lancelot, and Morgan must each decide what the oath now binds to them, and the succession question becomes a living threat rather than a sealed door.
Lancelot walks to the seam and binds the oath
Lancelot commits his loyalty to the relic itself, the court splits between those who guard the Grail and those who guard the peace, and Arthur must choose between his kingdom and his conscience.
Morgan invokes the old magic over the threshold
The threshold opens into a different kingdom's logic, the Round Table is pulled toward release and transformation, and the oath becomes something older and stranger than law.

encounters.title: The oath-cloth now lies across the threshold before the exiles' door, the court

text_script.value: Dawn found the oath-cloth no longer on the altar stones but spread thin across the threshold, rippling like light on still water, and the exiles outside stood in the doorway without waiting to be bidden. Mordred crouched beside it and said it was not a map of where Camelot was but a question of where it could still be, and Arthur answered that a question he could not close was not yet a peace. Lancelot watched the cloth with the devotion of a man who had already chosen, while Merlin traced its edge with one finger and Morgan murmured that the old magic did not hold things still; it only kept the question honest. Gawain stepped between the shrine and the door and asked plainly who among them was willing to be answerable to ordinary people.
Arthur opens the door to the exiles

The court becomes a public covenant with the exiles as bearers of the oath, peace is founded in inclusion but the Round Table must face that its relic, crown, and table now serve the whole kingdom rather than the court alone.
Lancelot lifts the cloth toward the exiles

Lancelot carries the oath itself outward to the exiles, the Grail moves beyond the shrine's stone, and the court must decide whether the relic belongs to the people or to the thing that was worshipped.
Morgan bridges the threshold with old magic
Morgan and Merlin weave the threshold into a living passage, the Round Table is pulled toward a new kingdom's logic, and Arthur must weigh the old power's honesty against its ungovernability.

encounters.title: The oath-cloth is torn but still shining, the exiles are inside the hall with or

text_script.value: In the shrine-hall the oath-cloth had torn at one edge and let a narrow band of light fall across the aisle, where the exiles stood in families rather than in ranks: a widow with a cracked cup, a healer with a bundle of herbs, quarry-men whose boots were too heavy for ceremony. Arthur asked them not what they were owed but what Camelot was failing to make whole. Mordred, still seated at the edge, answered that a peace which treated his kin as a symbol of the price had not yet healed anything. Lancelot lifted the seam only enough to read the fault in it, Merlin traced the old veins in the stone, and Morgan said the magic was not lawless so much as older than the word law. Gawain pushed his cloak aside and stepped down beside the exiles, naming the live question plainly: the Round Table could guard its relic, its peace, or its self-image, but it could not keep all three.
Arthur stands down among the exiles
Arthur gives up the raised authority of the throne, peace becomes tied to ordinary survival, and Gawain and Mordred can either make the covenant public or turn it into a claim for heirs.
Lancelot carries the seam outward

The relic-light leaves the shrine and travels with the exiles, splitting the court between those who follow the Grail and those who keep the peace, while Arthur must decide whether conscience or crown comes first.
Morgan binds the torn edge into a road
Morgan and Merlin turn the fault in the oath into a passage between worlds, tempting the Round Table toward transformation while threatening the oath with magic older and stranger than law.

encounters.title: The oath-lamp still burns above a doorway where the exiles stand as neighbors ra

text_script.value: The torn oath-cloth had gathered into a lamp above the threshold, still trembling like a held breath. Along the aisle, the exiles no longer waited to be summoned: a widow with a cracked cup, a healer with bundle of herbs, and quarry-men who said plainly that their children did not know the word covenant. Arthur asked the court what it would become if the Grail were treated as a promise rather than a treasure, and Gawain answered that a promise kept only for its keepers was not yet law. Lancelot turned the seam inward, reading it as a fault line; Morgan said the old magic could hold a road open but could not make the road safe by itself. Mordred rose to say that a peace without a named heir was only a pause, while the Lady of the Lake asked whether Camelot would ask the exiles to be part of the oath or merely tell them the terms.
Arthur names the terms
Arthur invites the exiles to set binding terms of peace, turning the Round Table into an answerable assembly while forcing Mordred and Lancelot to either join the covenant or claim its inheritance.
Lancelot carries the lamp out
Lancelot takes the oath-light past the shrine toward the exiles' villages, splitting the court between those who follow the relic and those who must guard the peace.
Morgan binds the torn edge
Morgan and Merlin weave the seam into a living passage, tempting the Round Table toward transformation while risking that the oath becomes wider than law can govern.

encounters.title: The oath-lamp still burns but leans toward ordinary survival, with the exiles no

text_script.value: Dawn found the oath-lamp low above the threshold, throwing a thin gold path toward the exiles instead of the throne. Arthur asked the widow, the healer and the quarry-men to speak the one term that made peace worth keeping; Mordred answered that the Round Table could not call itself free if it only listened at the door. Lancelot said he could carry the seam outward but not decide who owned its light, while Morgan and Merlin argued that a road open to all was still a boundary, not a doorway. Bedivere read the torn cloth as a list of unfinished obligations, and the Lady of the Lake sent a witness with the exiles to say that their fear was a claim on the peace, not a fact to be managed.
Arthur makes the exiles binding witnesses
The Round Table becomes an answerable assembly, forcing Mordred and Lancelot to either co-sign the covenant or expose their exclusion as a claim on the succession.
Lancelot carries the seam to the villages
The relic-light leaves the shrine and travels with the exiles, splitting the court between those who follow the Grail and those who must guard the peace.
Morgan and Merlin bind the road
The torn oath becomes a passage beyond ordinary law, tempting Camelot toward transformation while risking that the Round Table loses the boundary that makes it a kingdom.

encounters.title: The oath has become a negotiated road among court, exiles, relic and old magic;

text_script.value: At dawn the threshold no longer looked like a door but a road cut through the court, with exile ledgers, a warm lamp of torn oath-cloth, and a narrow seam of violet mist all laid on one table. Arthur asked whether the Round Table could remain a court if the exiles were allowed to name the price of peace; Gawain answered that an oath with no counterparty was only a charm, while Lancelot said the seam could be carried but not owned. Percival held the exiles' ledger against his breast like a shield, the Lady of the Lake refused to call the seam a road until the exiles could walk it, and Morgan asked whether the old magic should hold the road open or keep it honest. Mordred said that if the court refused those terms, then the succession itself was no longer waiting for Arthur but for whoever could carry it.
Arthur makes the exiles binding witnesses
The exiles gain lawful seats and must co-sign the terms, forcing Mordred and Lancelot to either join the covenant or claim publicly that it excludes their right to rule.
Lancelot carries the seam to the villages
The oath-light leaves the shrine and moves with the exiles, splitting the court between those who guard the peace at Camelot and those who follow the relic-road outward.
Merlin and Morgan hold the road open
The torn oath becomes a living passage toward transformation, tempting Camelot beyond ordinary law while risking that the Round Table loses the boundary that makes it a kingdom.

encounters.title: The seam has torn open beyond any oath, the exiles are lost in mist, and Arthur

text_script.value: On the third dawn after the oath was read aloud, the shrine floor split along a single torn seam and the lamp's light pooled in a crack that breathed violet mist. Arthur held the ledger of binding terms and felt it heavy as a stone while Mordred, seated in the seat of the absent, said that the Round Table could admit him to its right or lose the right to call itself a table. Lancelot read his own oath twice and could not find his name in it; Gawain answered that the seam was not a road but a wound, while Morgan asked what would stand at the far side of it. The Lady of the Lake sent her witness back with a message that the exiles had crossed into the mist and no oath on record reached them, and Merlin said that whatever the court decided in an hour, it could never be unmade in a generation.
Arthur answers the exiles' terms
The Round Table becomes an answerable covenant: Mordred is forced to either submit openly or claim the succession by breaking the oath, and Lancelot must declare where his loyalty truly rests.
Lancelot carries the road outward
The seam travels with the exiles and the Grail-light, splitting the court between those who follow it and those who must guard the peace at Camelot.
Morgan and Merlin open the passage
The torn oath becomes a living road toward transformation, tempting Camelot beyond ordinary law while risking that the Round Table loses the boundary that makes it a kingdom.

encounters.title: Arthur faces a cracked kingdom: the exile road is open beyond the oath, the Grai

text_script.value: By torchlight the Round Table looked like a cracked enamel plate around a grail shard no taller than a fist. Arthur read the exile slips aloud and found each one asking the same impossible question: whether the court was still a kingdom or only a place where promises were stored. Mordred said the shard had no lord now that the oath no longer reached the mist, while Gawain answered that a broken table could still keep a promise if someone was willing to be bound by it. Lancelot stared at the shard until it caught his own missing name, and Merlin murmured that the road beyond it had begun to change the direction of Camelot's shadow.
Arthur makes the exiles binding witnesses
The exiles may be heard and named at the table, forcing Mordred to either swear to the terms or publicly claim he stands outside them.
Lancelot carries the shard outward
The Grail-light leaves the shrine with the exiles, splitting the court between those who seek it and those who must keep Camelot from following it into ruin.
Merlin and Morgan ward the road
The passage can be kept from swallowing the Round Table, but the ward is costly and may become the new boundary around a kingdom that no longer needs an oath to survive.

encounters.title: The kingdom is split between a binding road into the mist, a Grail that answers

text_script.value: By the fourth dawn the shrine floor no longer held its old crack but a slow opening, violet at the edges and warm as a banked hearth. Arthur stood where the ledger lay, too heavy to close, and answered Mordred by naming the exile road an oath still owed rather than a place already lost. Lancelot lifted the Grail shard and found his own name written in it backwards, so that when he read it aloud the word was ours; Gawain pressed the seam shut with a blade-edged ring and said that a promise could still hold the shape of a place if someone would carry it into the mist. Morgan asked where the table stood once its light moved, while Merlin, half-turned toward the dark, answered that it stood wherever the kingdom chose to remain answerable.
Arthur answers the road with covenant
The exiles become binding witnesses at the table, forcing Mordred to swear openly or claim the succession by stepping outside the oath.
Lancelot carries the shard and its reversed name
The Grail-light passes through the court, dividing those who seek it from those who must keep the peace from following it into ruin.
Morgan and Merlin make the passage a new boundary
The road is kept from swallowing Camelot, but the ward becomes the kingdom's first living law instead of a wall against law.

encounters.title: The road is held but no longer neutral, the shard answers with reversed truths,

text_script.value: At the threshold the violet road stopped breathing, and Merlin set a ward like a strand of silver across the mist until the exiles outside answered to Arthurâ€™s name instead of the roadâ€™s. Lancelot held the shard in both hands; when it caught the torchlight it read backwards, and his own face appeared in it wearing a different mouth. â€˜Then let us decide what the mouth means,â€™ Arthur said, and Mordred rose with the claim: peace by oath, peace by power, or a kingdom that remakes its promises before the shrine swallows them.
Arthur binds the exiles to a new covenant
The exiles and court swear a written covenant binding the roadâ€™s price, forcing Mordred to either join the terms or open the succession war.
Lancelot speaks the reversed name
The Grail answers a true claim, a false one, or the unborn exileâ€™s claim, turning succession and loyalty into one speaking question.
Morgan and Merlin open the boundary
The ward becomes a gate rather than a wall, preserving Camelot by admitting foreign law, oath, and exile into the Round Table.

encounters.title: The road is again alive, the shard speaks backwards truths, and the court must d

text_script.value: The silver ward flickered like a failing flame, and the violet road beneath the shrine floor began to breathe again. Arthur laid his hand on the ledger, and the words that had been his peace came out as a question instead: "Who is crowned when the oath is also a road?" Lancelot turned the shard until the backwards letters caught the torchlight and read, in effect, both of them; Mordred leaned forward and said that a succession chosen in light might still survive the next dark, and Gawain answered that a succession chosen in darkness might survive nothing. Morgan circled the table, testing the ward's edge with one finger, while Merlin murmured that the kingdom had fought too long to call it a peace. The Lady of the Lake set the exiles' standard against the shard, and Percival closed his eyes and asked whether the dead of the exile road had a voice at all.
Arthur names the succession openly
The court and exiles swear before the shard, forcing Mordred to accept the oath or declare himself outside it, sharpening the succession war into a public test.
Lancelot asks the shard what is ours
The Grail answers the question of the exiles, turning the Grail from a relic into a ruling voice and putting succession, loyalty, and the road into one contested judgment.
Morgan and Merlin reweave the ward as law
The boundary becomes the kingdom's first standing court, admitting exile and foreign oath while binding the Grail's light to a shared obligation.

encounters.title: The ward is at the edge of silence, the exiles are at the gate with unlit lanter

text_script.value: Before the last candle on the shrine altar could drown in its own wax, the exiles came through the road as a line of silhouettes, each carrying a small lantern with no flame inside. Lancelot laid the shard on the threshold and watched the reverse writing harden into a choir of mouths, while Mordred shouted that a table that cannot refuse a successor is already a crown. Arthur knelt by the ledger and asked the court to choose out loud: bind the exiles, hear the Grail, or teach the boundary to breathe again. Morgan let her fingers trail the silver ward; it answered in green, then violet, then a color neither of them had named.
Arthur seals the exile covenant
The exiles swear inside the shrine law, Mordred is forced to enter the oath or declare open war, and the succession becomes a public sentence rather than a private fear.
Lancelot reads the shard as judgment
The Grail speaks a contested verdict over succession, exile, and divided loyalty, turning the shard into a legal witness whose answer can be obeyed, refused, or fought.
Morgan and Merlin teach the boundary to breathe
The ward opens into a shared court and road, admitting foreign oath and exiled power while binding the Grail's light to a living obligation.

encounters.title: The exiles have spoken through the road, the ward is nearly silent, and the cour

text_script.value: The lanterns at the threshold were not lit, but the road behind them glowed the color of a held breath, and the exiles did not speak until Arthur forced them to: "Speak your name and what you carry." A woman from the salt coast answered that she carried a broken coin, a debt owed to her family, and the question of whether Camelot could hold both law and mercy. Lancelot unclasped the shard and read the ward's reply aloud: the oath had not been refused, only made heavier. Mordred said quietly that a crown that cannot carry the unhoused has already been carried away. Merlin touched the silver seam and murmured that Camelot was not dying of weakness but of being asked to be two things at once.
Arthur swears the exiles as members of the oath
The exiles gain standing inside Camelot, Mordred is forced to either accept the covenant or attack it, and the Grail is tied to a promise rather than a possession.
Lancelot asks the Grail to judge the oath
The shard answers with a contested verdict on succession and loyalty, forcing each major claimant to either obey it, refuse it, or die defending the refusal.
Merlin opens the ward into a living border
The boundary becomes a standing court of road and exile, admitting foreign oath while binding the Grail's light to an obligation older than Camelot.

encounters.title: The exiles have ignited blue lanterns inside the ward and carry a name to be jud

text_script.value: The exiles' lanterns woke as one, but their light was no warm candle-glow: each flame burned a deep, smokeless blue, and where the light touched the shrine steps it turned the stone to bruised violet. Arthur found Mordred standing inside the ward line, not guarding it but looking through it, and heard him say, "It has never sealed us in, Arthur. It has only ever been waiting for us to stop asking to be kept safe." Morgan knelt at the silver seam and admitted that the old magic was not refusing to work, only exhausted, and that Merlin's binding sigils were fraying strand by strand. Lancelot held the shard to his chest and felt the Grail's light stutter, and the whole court fell silent while the exiles answered the question of what they carried: not coins or debts, but a name â€” the name of whoever would be judged next when the ward failed.
Lancelot carries the shard through the border
The Grail leaves Camelot for the road, Mordred gains the opening to claim that the law has fled, and the exiles gain a witness rather than a prisoner.
Arthur declares the exiles the second court
The exiles gain oath and office within Camelot, Mordred is forced to contest the charter or accept it, and the Grail is bound to a living promise rather than a sealed shrine.
Morgan and Merlin pay to reweave the ward
The boundary is repaired at a cost that drains Merlin's old gift and binds Morgan's magic to the court, and the exiles must either swear to the new ward or walk into the road it now guards.

encounters.title: The ward is visibly failing and the shard now pulls toward the road; succession

text_script.value: The ward held through the night, but it held the way a wound holds a ribbon together, tighter each hour and thinner each hour. In the grey before dawn, Mordred walked to the shard and held it out to Arthur rather than to the shrine: 'It is not ours to keep,' he said. 'That is the first thing we must admit.' Lancelot, who had not slept, felt the Grail's light shift inside him toward the road, and the Lady of the Lake answered quietly that the exiles had not come for charity but for a verdict. Arthur looked at his heirs, then at the violet seam in the shrine wall that no one dared to touch, and asked the question he had been avoiding.
Arthur names his heir under the Round Table oath

Gawain receives the oath as heir and must either defend Camelot from within or found it beyond the road; Mordred is forced to accept the succession or to break it, and the Round Table gains a second center of gravity.
Lancelot carries the shard out of the ward
The Grail crosses into the road beyond the border, the exiles gain a witness and a promise, Mordred gains a claim that the law has fled, and Camelot's relic becomes a wager that can be kept or lost.
Merlin and Morgan ask the court to pay the ward's price
The court binds itself to the old magic's terms at the cost of one member's freedom, the ward steadies, and the exiles must either stand inside the new boundary or walk out of it forever.

encounters.title: The court faces a choice among staking the succession inside a failing ward, car

text_script.value: The ward held through the night, and held the way a hem holds a tear â€” in the grey hour before dawn, Gawain stood before Arthur and asked whether the court would rule from a shrine that could not keep its own border, while Mordred answered that a law which only works when nothing goes wrong is not law but a promise no one has tried to keep. Morgan knelt at the violet seam and named the cost of the old magic plainly: not gold, but the one who would have to be bound to it. Lancelot lifted the shard and felt the light lean toward the road beyond the border, and the exiles answered from the lantern line with a question no decree could settle â€” what would a court be, if the law had to leave the room first?
Arthur stakes the succession and the ward on the oath

Gawain receives the Round Table oath as heir and must either defend Camelot from within or carry it outward; Mordred must either sign the charter or break it, and the ward steadies on the strength of a public promise.
Lancelot carries the shard beyond the border
The Grail travels past the border with the exiles' witness and a living pledge, Mordred claims that the law has fled, and Camelot's legitimacy becomes a wager that can be kept or lost along the road.
Morgan pays the ward's price and binds the exiles or frees them
The boundary steadies at the cost of Morgan's freedom and a personal debt, the exiles choose to enter the court as bound keepers or walk out as judges, and the ward's terms become permanent.

encounters.title: The court must decide whether Camelot remains a besieged shrine, becomes a road-

text_script.value: Dawn found the court pressed against a violet seam where the ward had begun to fray, and every oath looked less like a roof than a thread held by one tired hand. Mordred said that an oath that only works when nothing goes wrong is not law but a lullaby, while Gawain answered that a promise is not mercy until it can hurt someone fairly. Lancelot lifted the shard and felt the light lean past the lantern line toward the road; the Lady of the Lake answered that the exiles had come not to be saved but to be judged by witnesses, not masters. Arthur looked from the Round Table to the shrine and asked what a king was, if the king could not decide whether the law should stand in Camelot or travel with the Grail.
Arthur convenes the Round Table as a covenant of witnesses
Gawain becomes heir of duty rather than ruler, Mordred is named judge of the exile road, and Camelot steadies as a republic that no longer claims the throne as sacred.
Lancelot carries the shard beyond the border with the exiles
The Grail crosses into the road and the exiles gain a living pledge, while Mordred gains the claim that law has fled and Camelot's legitimacy becomes a wager kept or lost along the road.
Morgan asks the court which wound to keep open
The ward steadies only by binding a visible cost to the boundary, the old magic becomes permanent, and the exiles must either enter as keepers or leave as judges who will not return.

encounters.title: The court must decide whether the shard becomes a road-law carried outward, a co

text_script.value: By the third bell the ward had stopped looking like a wall and started looking like a debt: the shard burned through a seam of violet glass while Mordred stood at the threshold with a charter in one hand and a severed pledge in the other. Guinevere asked whether a court could keep its promises to the dead if it had to make new ones to the walking, and the exiles answered from the lantern line that they would not wait for a king to define them. Arthur lifted the Round Table ring and found it heavy with unpaid hospitality rather than power, while Merlin, half-listening, said that the price had not changed only because no one had named it yet.
Arthur opens the covenant and lets the shard travel with named witnesses
Gawain is made heir of duty, Lancelot and the exiles leave with the shard, and Mordred is forced to judge whether the road has a claim as strong as the crown.
Arthur keeps the shard inside and turns Camelot into a public debt ledger
The ward steadies as a shrine of witnessed bargains, but the court must accept visible exclusion, while Mordred can accuse it of protecting privilege rather than the living.
Morgan asks one named keeper to bind the boundary
The boundary holds, the keeper becomes publicly accountable and partly bound, and the exiles enter as judges or leave as witnesses who will not return.

encounters.title: Camelot must decide whether duty, the shard, or the exiles become the law now, w

text_script.value: At first light the Round Table looked less like a throne than a broken bridge, with an exile token lying across the gold ring and the ward humming above it. Guinevere asked whether Camelot could swear to the living and the dead at once, and Mordred answered that a promise to the dead is only comfort unless it changes the road. Lancelot stood closest to the violet seam, feeling the shard pull toward the exiles, while Merlin kept one hand on the light and Morgan kept one on the price. The Lady of the Lake set the broken token before Arthur and said that the court must answer for the road, not for the crown.
Arthur names Gawain heir of duty
Gawain inherits the Round Table as a witness-court rather than a throne, Mordred is forced to accept the oath or declare open war, and Lancelot may carry the shard outward with witnesses.
Arthur grants the exiles a road-charter
The exiles enter as judges and companions of the shard, Mordred gains a legal claim but loses the throne's sanctity, and Camelot becomes a mobile republic of oaths instead of a guarded shrine.
Merlin and Morgan bind the violet seam
The ward holds and the Grail steadies, but the boundary becomes partly permanent and partly owned by the binders, making Lancelot, Morgan, and Mordred each answer for the cost.

encounters.title: Camelot faces a succession trial: the shard is mobile and dangerous, Mordred has

text_script.value: At grey dawn the Round Table stood cracked like a wax seal while the shard pulsed through its missing rim, and the exiles leaned over the edge of the light without stepping across it. Guinevere asked whether a court could still be a road after it chose, and Mordred answered that any king who stayed was only a good landlord. Lancelot said the shard had taught him that carrying a promise is not the same as owing one, while Merlin warned that a price unnamed until it was paid would simply become Camelot. The Lady of the Lake set a broken cup upon the ring and told them to answer for whoever could no longer hear the answer.
Arthur names Gawain and the exiles joint keepers
Gawain inherits a witness-court with public authority, Lancelot may lead the shard outward with Bedivere as witness, and Mordred must either join the road-oath or seek law outside Camelot.
Arthur shields the Grail inside the ward
The ward stabilizes as a guarded shrine, Mordred gains a public claim to rule its walls, and the exiles must be admitted, bought, or sent away as witnesses.
Morgan and Merlin name the binding price
The boundary holds but becomes partially owned by the binders, Percival and Lancelot are pulled into the cost, and the Round Table must decide whether magic may outvote oath.

encounters.title: The court must now choose whether the shard is guarded, carried, or made a publi

text_script.value: Dusk poured over the broken ring while the shard hung above the oath-stone, too bright to be a treasure and too hollow to be a crown. Guinevere asked if an oath could be spent without dying, and Lancelot answered that he had spent one already and could still feel the cut. Mordred stood at the edge of the light and said the law would either carry him or use him as a wall, while the Lady of the Lake set a guest-token down and told Arthur to say what Camelot was for when no one was listening but the people who must obey. Percival lifted the exile sheaf and called for a sentence short enough to repeat at the far road.
Gawain keeps the road-oath
Gawain becomes the public keeper of the oath and sends Lancelot with Bedivere to carry the shard to named roads, while Mordred must accept the oath or declare open law outside Camelot.
Name a price for binding the seam

Merlin and Morgan bind the seam only after naming the cost: Lancelot carries the shard, Morgan answers for the exiles, Merlin owes magic to the commons, and the Grail steadies but the ward is no longer fully Arthur's.
Let the exiles judge the Grail

The exiles take lawful authority over the shard and the Grail's road, Mordred gains a wall-claim rather than the throne, and Arthur must rule as witness to a republic that answers to those who left it.

encounters.title: The shard is no longer safely within the ward: the court must choose whether to

text_script.value: Arthur kept the council from turning into a theft, and Gawain kept his hand on the broken oath-band while the shard leaned over the threshold as if it had begun to choose. Guinevere said a crown was not a road; Mordred said the law would carry him or swallow him as a stone; Lancelot opened the sheaf of exile names, while Merlin and Morgan argued over what the seam could be bound for. Percival, Bedivere, the Lady of the Lake, and the exiles stayed at the gate to hear whether Camelot was a shrine, a law, or a journey.
Gawain carries the oath outward
Lancelot and Bedivere leave with the shard as a witness road, Gawain holds the oath at the gate, and Mordred must either swear to carry exiles outward or declare law outside Camelot.
Merlin and Morgan name the binding price
The shard settles into a covenant that is no longer wholly Arthur's, Morgan must answer for exiles, Merlin owes magic to the commons, and Lancelot is tied to the cost.
Let the exiles judge the shard and road
The exiles rule the road and Grail, Mordred becomes wall-keeper rather than king, Arthur rules as witness to a republic that answers to those who left it.

encounters.title: The road has carried exiles but the ward is cooling and two roads demand redefin

text_script.value: Frost had not left the eaves when the road-messengers came back through the gate with broken cloaks and tally-sticks. Arthur read the tallies aloud and did not flinch: the road had carried three spears of exiles safely past the thorn-hills, but the ward-stone had grown cold enough to ache, and two of the roads were already asking to be renamed. Gawain held the witness-oath against his chest like a coal. Guinevere said the roads were not the same as the oath, and Lancelot answered that an oath kept on paper meant nothing if it could not feed a family. Mordred stood apart and named his price plainly: let the exiles hold the roads, and the throne can hold the wall, but never the other way around. Percival whispered that the shard had begun humming when the commons listened, and the Lady of the Lake set her guest-token down on the table and asked whether Camelot meant to be a home or a sign.
Arthur holds the ward

Arthur keeps the shard inside the shrine and defends the road by force, Gawain and Bedivere become the ward's shield, Mordred must either yield the wall or rally the exiles, and the Grail stays a symbol of order rather than a road.
Let the Grail walk the roads

Percival leads the shard outward as a living sacrament of the commons, Lancelot carries the burden of division, Morgan and Merlin bind the ward only as a witness, and the exiles gain real lawful authority over it.
Let the exiles write the road

The exiles and the Lady of the Lake set the terms of the road and the Grail, Mordred becomes wall-keeper rather than king, and Arthur must govern as a guest in a republic that answers to those who left it.

encounters.title: The ward-stone has cracked and the exiles have arrived with living claims: Arthu

text_script.value: Dawn found the ward-stone split with a seam of cold light running through the shrine floor, and the exile-convoy stood at the gate with tally-sticks still in their fists. Arthur set the shard on the oath-table and asked the exiles what the road owed them before he asked what it owed Camelot. Lancelot said an oath was only a tally of care, not a stone of obedience; Morgan countered that a binding is a price a town must refuse sometimes, not a spell to be bargained down. Mordred rose and offered the cleanest dividing line anyone had spoken: the wall for his people, the road for the exiles, and the throne for whoever could answer to both.
Arthur holds the ward
Gawain and Bedivere become the shard's shields, the exiles are given road-tolls rather than sovereignty, and Mordred must either rally the wall against the open road or swear to answer to it.
Percival carries the Grail outward

The shard becomes a living road through the thorn-hills, Lancelot carries the cost of division openly, and Morgan and Merlin bind the ward only as a witness to a sacrament that no longer belongs to the court alone.
The exiles write the road
The Lady of the Lake and the exiles set the terms of the road and Grail, Mordred becomes wall-keeper rather than king, and Arthur governs as a guest in a republic that answers to those who left it.

encounters.title: The cracked shrine echoes the council's words and three hard terms are now on th

text_script.value: At the second dawn the cracked ward-stone no longer merely hummed; it answered every spoken word with a faint gold echo, so the council broke into three tables of its own: oath, bread, and witness. Arthur asked the exiles to name the first thing Camelot must return before it could be forgiven; Mordred answered that the first thing was a wall that answered to those who had left it. Lancelot laid his divided loyalty on the table like a torn seal, and Guinevere asked whether a law that fed no one was a promise or a prison. Morgan laughed once and said the old binding still loved them more than it loved the idea of Camelot, while the Lady of the Lake set the shard beside the exile tally and said the shrine had to learn how to leave.
Seal a three-handed bargain
Arthur keeps a crowned office but under exile-appointed road judges, Mordred becomes wall-keeper rather than claimant, and the Grail remains guarded only while the commons keep it honest.
Let the shard leave the shrine
Percival carries the Grail through the commons as a road-sacrament, Morgan and Merlin act only as witnesses, and the ward is no longer Camelot's private power.
Let the exiles write the road
The Lady of the Lake and the exiles set the terms of the road and the Grail, Arthur rules as a guest under their law, and Mordred either submits to that republic or leads the wall into open refusal.

encounters.title: The charter is drafted but unsealed, the shard has gone silent rather than cold,

text_script.value: Three days after the three-table bargain, the shard had gone silent, and the silence was louder than the echo had ever been. Arthur stood at the oath-table with the cracked shard cooling in a bronze basin while the exile-judges read the charter aloud clause by clause, and Mordred watched their faces as though the wall outside were already written in them. Lancelot laid the torn seal on the table between the shrine and the exiles and said that a crown that could not be torn and re-sewn was no kingship at all; Merlin murmured that the silence was not an ending but a threshold, and the Lady of the Lake pressed a single white feather into Guinevere's hand, saying the Grail was no longer waiting where it had always waited.
Arthur names a successor under the charter
Arthur seats Gawain as heir under exile-witnessed law, Mordred must either swear to that succession or refuse it openly, and the shard's silence becomes a wager that the charter can hold a kingship.
Lancelot walks the torn seal to the wall
Lancelot negotiates the wall directly with Mordred, the charter is tested by what is actually said at the gates, and Gawain and Bedivere must choose between shield-duty and exile-facing duty.
Percival and the Lady of the Lake follow the silence

Percival and the Lady of the Lake leave Camelot to trace the Grail's departure, the court splits into those who stay to hold the charter and those who follow, and Merlin must decide whether the silence is a road or a wound.

encounters.title: The charter is drafted but uncrowned, the shard listens toward the road, Mordred

text_script.value: The shard-basin cooled by mid-morning but did not shatter, and its dark center turned toward the east door like a held breath. Arthur told Gawain that the charter could be signed, but not crowned, unless the wall and the exiles knew what they were swearing to; Mordred answered that a charter was a wall with better words, and the wall outside already remembered every exile Camelot called unfinished. Lancelot laid the torn seal on the stone and said both halves of a seal were still useful if they had to be carried separately, while Morgan said the old binding was not confused, only grieved. The Lady of the Lake set the empty white cup beside the tally of names and told Percival that absence had a direction: down the road, toward the shrine, toward whatever the commons had carried away.
Arthur crowns Gawain under exile-witnessed law

Gawain becomes heir by public oath rather than by Arthur's favor, Mordred must either swear to the charter or declare refusal from the wall, and the court is forced to decide whether Camelot survives as law or only as ritual.
Lancelot carries the torn seal to Mordred
Lancelot, Bedivere, and the exile judges carry Arthur's reply into the wall, turning the succession into a negotiation where the cost of agreement and the cost of refusal are both visible.
Percival and the Lady of the Lake take the silence outward
The court splits into those who guard the charter at Camelot and those who follow the Grail road, making the empty cup a map whose first trail is exile, ruin, or refuge.

encounters.title: The charter waits at midday oath while Mordred challenges it from the wall, the

text_script.value: The exile bell came at dawn before the shard ever spoke again, and Mordred stood at the wall with the charter-draft in his fist, saying the shrine had survived one empty table and could survive one more. Lancelot unrolled the torn seal and asked who was left to keep a law, and the Lady of the Lake set the white cup at the foot of the table and said the Grail had not been stolen but answered. Guinevere asked Arthur the question nobody had dared, whether the peace could be kept if the peace itself had vanished; Gawain answered that a throne without a road was a tomb with a king in it; Merlin said the silence was a threshold, not a grave; and Bedivere, watching the east door, asked whether the road was already open behind them. Arthur answered only that the oath would be spoken at midday, before all, or not at all.
Arthur speaks the succession oath before all
Arthur names Gawain heir under exile-witnessed oath, forcing Mordred to swear or refuse at the wall, and the charter either holds or breaks publicly.
Lancelot and Bedivere carry the oath to Mordred
The torn seal goes through the wall with the exile judges, turning succession into a negotiation where both agreement and refusal have visible cost.
Percival and the Lady of the Lake take the road
The court splits into those who hold the charter and those who follow the Grail, and the empty cup becomes a direction rather than a wound.

encounters.title: At dusk the charter is neither sealed nor abandoned: succession, wall refusal, a

text_script.value: At the last shrine hour the shard-basin showed three faces at once: the crown, the wall, and the road beyond the east door. Mordred held the draft like a dare and said that a peace which cannot see the wall was only a richer grave, while Arthur answered that a law which forgets the exiles was only a new throne for old fears. Lancelot pressed the torn seal into Arthur's hand and said a broken thing could still be carried whole, and the Lady of the Lake set the empty cup on the threshold and said the road did not need to be won, only followed. Morgan and Merlin listened as the dead were spoken to before the living swore, and Percival said the exiles were already walking, whether Camelot wished to watch them or not.
Arthur names Gawain heir before the dead
Gawain receives the succession by public oath, forcing Mordred's wall to swear to the charter or declare open refusal.
Arthur, Mordred, exiles, and road-watchers sign a conditional peace
Camelot survives as an exile-witnessed covenant rather than a crown alone, but succession must be renewed against both wall and road.
Percival and the Lady of the Lake take the empty cup outward
The court splits into those who hold Camelot and those who follow the Grail road, postponing succession until the road answers.

encounters.title: Before first light, Camelot faces three possible answers to the same oath: crown

text_script.value: At the last hour before dawn the shard-basin showed three faces at once: a crown, a wall, and a road. Arthur stood at the table while Guinevere asked who would be left to tend the exiles if the crown was kept, Mordred answered that a law without a wall was only a richer grave, and Lancelot said a torn seal could still be carried whole if someone was allowed to refuse it. Percival set the empty white cup on the threshold and named the road a direction rather than a destination, while Morgan reminded the court that every oath had one honest end and one bargain, and Merlin said the shrine was a question answered badly. Bedivere turned toward the east door and said the exiles were already walking, and Arthur answered that the oath would be spoken at first light, or the table would remain what it had become: an instrument of leaving.
Arthur speaks Gawain as heir under public oath
Gawain is named heir at first light, forcing Mordred to swear publicly or declare open refusal and ending Camelot as an uncontested crown.
Arthur and Mordred sign an exile-witnessed covenant
Camelot survives as an exile-witnessed covenant rather than a crown alone, but succession must be renewed against both wall and road.
Percival and the Lady of the Lake carry the empty cup outward
The court splits into those who hold the charter and those who follow the Grail road, postponing succession until the road answers.

encounters.title: At the dawn threshold, Camelot holds three open answers at once - a crown oath,

text_script.value: At the last candle hour the shrine bell had already fallen silent, and the three seals lay on the table like arguments waiting to be read. Arthur did not speak first; he let the empty cup catch the last blue light, then asked Gawain what he would carry if the crown had to choose between shield and road. Morgan laid a white hand over the basin's crack and answered that oaths were not ended by refusal but by being forced to remain honest, while Mordred said the exiles would not follow a law that only protected those already safe. By the time the east door yawned, Percival had lifted the cup toward the road, the Lady of the Lake had unbuckled her chain, and Merlin touched the table once, as if asking the dead to stay one breath longer.
Arthur names Gawain heir and binds the east road
Gawain can be crowned only by making the charter include the exiles and the road, turning Camelot into either a living republic or a defensive throne.
Percival and the Lady of the Lake carry the cup through the east door
The court splits between those who follow the Grail road and those who lock the shrine, pushing the realm toward exile, ruin, or a different kingdom.
Arthur, Mordred, and the exiles sign a witnessed covenant
Succession is postponed into an exile-witnessed compact that can survive as a mixed republic, be broken by rival claimants, or become the seed of a new order.

encounters.title: At the first-light threshold, Camelot stands at a final branching point: a law-b

text_script.value: First light touched the shard-basin and every seal on the table threw a shadow pointing a different way, as if the oath itself could not decide which future to face. Arthur asked the court once more what it would keep, and Lancelot answered that he would keep his refusal if it was the price of honesty, while Mordred said a crown that fed no one was a weapon wearing a robe. Guinevere set her hand on the crown and asked who would hold the widows if the seat were kept, Gawain said he would carry the wall if the road would carry the exiles, and Morgan warned that every answer had already been spoken somewhere, by someone who lost. Merlin closed his eyes, Percival raised the empty cup toward the eastern road, and the Lady of the Lake unbuckled her clasp, leaving the court to answer the question before the light arrived too fully.
Arthur speaks the crown oath and binds the exiles into it
Lancelot refuses the oath and Mordred declares the charter void
Percival and the Lady of the Lake carry the cup out of the east door

encounters.title: At the covenant threshold, Arthur, Guinevere, and Lancelot must each turn from p

text_script.value: Merlin spread his foresight like a thin sail over the table, and Arthur, for once, did not reach for his crown but for the thread. "A kingdom of shields is a kingdom of debts," he said; "what if the Round Table swore not to hold land but to answer for one another?" Guinevere rose with the empty white cup in her hands and answered that a shrine without a witness was only a beautiful theft, and would the knights sign that the cup belonged to the exiles as much as to the court? Lancelot stood at the threshold, the seal of his old service still cold against his chest, and said that he had spent his life choosing between the throne and the road, and could no longer say which he served. Merlin smiled and said the answer was not a choice but a covenant, and the question before them was who would speak it first.
Arthur proposes the civic covenant
Knights renounce private inheritance and swear to answer for widows, exiles, and the shrine, forcing Mordred's claim into public debate and ending uncontested crown rule.
Guinevere declares the Grail a covenant
The Grail becomes a public covenant guarded by all, binding the court to the exiles and forcing the court to decide whether the sacred object serves people or power.
Lancelot sets down the seal
Lancelot withdraws from seduction politics and offers his loyalty to the covenant instead of the throne, splitting the court between those who accept him and those who see it as weakness.

encounters.title: The covenant is no longer an abstract ideal; Arthur, Guinevere, Lancelot, Morgan

text_script.value: Outside the shrine, Percival lays a woven list of the widowed, banished, and half-named households whose fates the Round Table had silently promised to keep. Arthur sets the empty white cup not on a pedestal but on the threshold stone, and asks each knight to state what they would lose if the oath were kept. Morgan watches his face and asks whether a covenant can bind a crown, or only a courageous habit; Merlin answers that the magic is not in the vows but in the refusal to use them as chains. Lancelot reaches out to touch the seal at his chest, then folds his hand into the fold of his cloak instead, and the moment hangs as Merlin turns the room toward a second question: who will be answerable when the covenant fails?
Arthur binds the oath to failure

Arthur vows that any knight who breaks the covenant loses office before losing reputation, forcing the court to choose visible civic risk over private honor and turning succession into a matter of public accountability.
Guinevere opens the Grail to witnesses

Guinevere demands that exiles and ordinary households be allowed to bear witness to the Grail covenant, turning the sacred object into a public memory and inviting Morgan and Merlin to test whether magic can serve testimony without becoming coercion.
Lancelot ties his oath to the exiles

Lancelot ties his own withdrawal to the road rather than the throne, separating his loyalty from Arthur's power and forcing the court to answer whether loyalty may be given to people, a shrine, or both.
