encounters.title: The court is deciding whether the Grail covenant becomes a public succession rit

text_script.value: At first light, Percival reads the names again while the Grail cools from a relic into a question, and Arthur stops arranging the throne and begins arranging the court. 'If the oath cannot answer the empty chair,' he says, 'then the Round Table is only a fine way to say no one owns the door.' Merlin shows three roads in the air: one to the crown, one to the exile roads, one to a civic peace no one has fully survived yet. Morgan asks what magic is for if not to make witnessing survivable, and Lancelot, his seal unreadable in the new light, answers that a covenant which cannot follow people past Camelot is not a gift but a cage wearing courtesy.
Arthur opens the succession to public judgment
Arthur makes the next rule an answerable office rather than a crown, forcing Mordred's claim and the court's loyalty to be tested before witnesses.
Guinevere sends the Grail outward as testimony
Guinevere lets widows, exiles, and half-named households witness the covenant, turning the Grail into a shared road instead of a court treasure.
Merlin and Morgan set the price of magic
Merlin and Morgan turn foresight into a limit: magic may reveal and witness, but no oath may be compelled without consent, forcing the court to accept uncertainty.

encounters.title: The court is moving toward a constitutional peace in which Arthur bounds knightl

text_script.value: At dusk the court stops arguing over a throne and begins arguing over a habitable order. Arthur sets the unmarked bowl on the threshold and asks every knight to name the privilege he or she would surrender before Merlin reads the compact aloud; Guinevere takes the empty civic chair beside him, pledges the Grail to widows, exiles, and half-named households, and tells Mordred that his name may remain if his claim can be judged by witnesses. Lancelot sets his sword inside the shrine, closes his hand around the sealed seal rather than the crown, and says that withdrawal is not an insult but a covenant that will not demand worship. Merlin hears the old magic cool into arithmeticâ€”promises, losses, deadlinesâ€”while Morgan asks what happens to those who cannot consent, and the court leans toward a peace that would rather be answerable than beloved.
Arthur binds privilege
Arthur names what every knight loses if the covenant fails and forces a visible public judgment rather than a private honor pledge.
Guinevere charters the Grail
Guinevere opens the covenant to widows, exiles, and half-named households so the Grail answers a road rather than a court.
Mordred is asked to speak
Mordred is forced to state his claim before witnesses, testing whether the peace can absorb legitimacy without erasing his grief.

encounters.title: The court is moving from a private peace toward a public covenant in which Mordr

text_script.value: At the second bell, Mordred rises with his claim folded like a torn charter and says the peace will fail if his name is buried instead of answered. Arthur reads the line aloud and asks the court to state what it will surrender before it asks Mordred to give anything up; Guinevere sets the empty civic chair at the threshold, Lancelot lays his seal beside the ledger rather than on any crown, and Morgan turns the old magic into a list of prices that cannot be demanded by force. Merlin folds the three roads into one visible covenant, while Percival lifts the Grail-bowl, Bedivere marks who may speak, and the Lady of the Lake keeps the outer road lit for those who are not yet inside it.
Mordred answers under witness
Mordred must state his claim and what he will accept, turning legitimacy into a public bargain rather than a throne dispute.
Every order names its loss
The court makes each knight, shrine-keeper, and guardian name the privilege or fear it gives up, making the covenant answerable instead of merely honorable.
Open the outer road
Guinevere and the Lady of the Lake let widows, exiles, and half-named households join the covenant before Camelot is safe enough to close its gates.

encounters.title: The court is moving from private pledges toward a public, dated covenant in whic

text_script.value: At the third bell the court stops speaking in court titles and starts speaking in debts. Mordred unfolds a folded claim and says plainly: if the peace answers only the living who can name themselves, then it is a rich man's treaty. Arthur asks every witness to name what he can prove and what he cannot, while Guinevere keeps the empty civic chair open for whoever arrives after the bell. Lancelot does not hide his sword; he lays it on the ledger as a reminder that his peace will be a non-use, not a victory. Merlin turns the old magic into a dated sentence, Morgan asks who pays when the peace cannot save everyone, and the Lady of the Lake opens the outer road by hand, not by decree.
Mordred answers under oath
Mordred must state his claim, his fear, and what he can accept, forcing the peace to absorb his legitimacy without pretending his grief is a defect.
Set a visible deadline
Merlin converts the magic into fixed terms, prices, and consequences so the covenant can be judged later rather than recited forever.
Let the outer road in
Guinevere and the Lady of the Lake admit widows, exiles, and half-named households as witnesses before Camelot can close its gates.

encounters.title: The court is swearing a dated, public covenant at the Grail shrine in which Mord

text_script.value: The oath is taken where the Grail bowl sits, not in the hall. Mordred reads his claim aloud from a folded strip â€” not a crown but a share in the road, a place where his family's debts are answerable â€” and Arthur answers by naming the first privilege he will surrender: the right to choose his own successor. Merlin sets the dated terms into the old magic, Morgan names the prices that cannot be bought, Lancelot lays his sword flat beside the ledger, and the Lady of the Lake opens the outer road by hand while widows and exiles file in to witness the words rather than to be blessed by them.
Seal the dated covenant
Merlin converts the oath into fixed terms, deadline, and named consequences, so the peace can be judged later rather than recited forever.
Guard the Grail as covenant
Custody of the bowl is split among named witnesses and shrine-keepers so no single claimant, crown, or magic holds the sacred object alone.
Let the road witness
Widows, exiles, and half-named households inside the outer road are given a named place in the covenant and a right to record the court's promises.

encounters.title: The dated covenant is being read aloud in public, with Arthur's privileges surre

text_script.value: At dawn the covenant stops being a promise and becomes a set of clocks. Merlin reads the dated terms aloud while knights say what they surrender: Arthur gives up choice of his successor, Percival gives up the right of judgment at court, and Lancelotâ€”his sword already lying flat on the ledgerâ€”declares he will not use love as a weapon of power. Morgan asks what happens to those the covenant cannot save, and Guinevere, standing at the outer road instead of the dais, answers that the covenant must hold their names, not their favor. The Lady of the Lake opens the gate-road by hand, and Mordred, for the first time, reads his oath aloud as witness rather than claimant.
Record the surrenders
Bedivere and the road-witnesses write each surrender into the ledger in public, making privilege measurable and revisable instead of recited forever.
Make Guinevere the civic witness
Guinevere accepts the road's civic roleâ€”recorder and first answererâ€”rather than crown-companion, shifting the peace's weight toward the outer road.
Give Mordred a named witness seat
Mordred gains a fixed, named place in the covenant as witness, forcing the peace to hold his legitimate claim without pretending his grief is a defect.

encounters.title: The dated covenant is recorded in magic but awaits enforcement by people: Guinev

text_script.value: Merlin touches the dated terms with a thumb and the shrine's low light shifts, but the words will not hold until someone pays the price of writing them down. Morgan names it plainly: the magic will record the covenant, not enforce it, and enforcement will be done by people. Mordred reads aloud the family debts the covenant promises to answer, and Guinevere rises to the road side and says she will answer first â€” not as Arthur's queen but as the one who owes the outer road. Arthur, gripping his surrendered privilege as a dead weight, asks what remains of him if he can no longer choose his successor, and Lancelot, sword still flat on the ledger, tells him it is everything that is already spoken aloud. The Lady of the Lake steps to the road's end and turns the gate-road's light toward the witnesses rather than toward the shrine.
Make people enforce it
The court designates named witnesses and shrine-keepers to check the covenant's terms at fixed intervals, shifting power from the Grail bowl to those who answer the road.
Put Mordred's debts in the record
The family debts Mordred read aloud are written into the covenant as dated obligations, giving him a binding stake that cannot be bargained away.
Open Arthur's succession to the road
Arthur formally relinquishes choosing his successor and offers the succession question to the road-witnesses and the court together, making the peace's answer public.

encounters.title: The covenant is humming with magic but pending human enforcement: Mordred's fami

text_script.value: The court gathers on the shrine dais as Merlin lays his hand over the Grail and the bowl answers with a low hum rather than a light. Mordred has read the family debts aloud and now stands silent, listening for the court to say whether they believe his claim or are merely recording it. Guinevere takes his sleeve and says the plain thing: the covenant will hold what it can carry, and it cannot carry everything, so it must carry the debts it can. Lancelot turns his flat sword toward the outer road and says the court is done choosing; the court must only hear. Morgan lifts her staff and asks whether the covenant is a wall or a road, and Merlin answers that it is both: the Grail is a promise kept, not a weapon kept.
Seat the road-witnesses
Widows, exiles, and road-keepers are given a named place at the covenant's edge, shifting legitimacy out of the court and into the community it serves.
Seal the Grail as covenant
The Grail is defined as the covenant itself, guarded by those who answer the road, so its light can only widen the promise rather than defend the court.
Hold the succession reckoning
Arthur opens the succession question to the whole table and the road-witnesses, making the peace's next answer public, contested, and unchosen by him alone.

encounters.title: The road-witnesses hold the gate-road at dawn, Guinevere has pledged civic witne

text_script.value: Dawn finds the outer road lit with lanterns and the road-witnesses standing in a ring beyond the shrine gate rather than at the dais, shoulders set as if daring the court to refuse them a seat. Merlin lifts the Grail and its light narrows to a single steady beam that rests on the gate-road instead of the shrine, and he says plainly that the promise is not to be defended but to be kept. Guinevere steps to the ring and speaks first: she will be no queen of the road, only its witness, and she names one by one the widows, exiles, and road-keepers she can answer for. Morgan lowers her staff and asks what the covenant cannot carry, and Arthur answers that it cannot carry what people refuse to carry, then asks the ring aloud what they ask of Camelot. Lancelot is already walking to the edge of the light, leaving the court behind.
Name the witnesses at the gate
Guinevere and Merlin read the named witnesses aloud before the court, turning the covenant from a court ceremony into a public act of civic accountability.
Carry the Grail to the road's edge
The Grail is lowered from the shrine and set at the gate-road itself, so the promise lives outside the shrine wall and must be maintained by whoever holds it.
Speak the succession question aloud
Arthur addresses the ring and the table together and asks what Camelot becomes when the succession question no longer belongs to him, forcing the court to answer before the witnesses.

encounters.title: The succession question has been put to the community, Mordred has offered accep

text_script.value: Arthur steps from the dais and walks into the road-light, and asks the ring aloud: what Camelot becomes when the succession question no longer belongs to one man. The witnesses answer in a low unison, each naming a debt they carry, and Mordred does not speak until Lancelot says the court has no right to choose for those who cannot vote. Mordred then sets his sword point-down on the covenant stone and says he will accept whatever the court can honestly give him, not what it flatters itself to give him. Merlin lifts his hand toward the Grail and says the old magic does not predict the ending but only its rhythm, and the rhythm is quiet. Morgan notes that a quiet peace is only quiet because it has not yet been tested, and the Grail hums a note lower than before.
Hold the public reckoning
The court reads the debts aloud together and forces each member to say what they will carry, making the succession answer a public act of burden rather than a throne decision.
Test the Grail against the debts
The Grail is asked to judge whether the covenant can carry the recorded debts, and its response either widens the promise or exposes the limit of what it can hold.
Let Lancelot withdraw from the choosing
Lancelot steps back from the dais and the court is left to choose without him, forcing Arthur and Guinevere to carry the covenant's meaning into the open.

encounters.title: The debts are read aloud and answered as carried, Mordred has laid down claim in

text_script.value: The court reads the debts aloud in order, and each name lands heavier than the last, until the ring of witnesses finally answers as one: 'We carry it.' Mordred sets his sword where the road meets the shrine and says the claim he came with is smaller than the debt he can now see, and Arthur, who has carried the crown alone, finds he can no longer say who will hold it after him. Lancelot steps down from the court's edge and asks the witnesses what he is to them now, and Guinevere answers before anyone else can: he is a debt the covenant refuses to collect. Morgan smiles without pleasure and asks what the Grail answers when the court stops asking what it should be.
Ask the Grail what it holds
Merlin lifts the Grail and asks it plainly what it holds when no court defines it, and its answer becomes the covenant's first line.
Let Lancelot answer for himself
Lancelot names his own place in the covenant and the court must accept it as civic fact rather than romantic exception.
Let Morgan test the peace
Morgan asks what would break the covenant if it were tested, and the court must either answer honestly or admit it has not looked.

encounters.title: The court is being converted from succession drama into civic covenant: Lancelot

text_script.value: Merlin lowers the Grail until its hum is barely above the road, and it answers not with a name but a rhythm: not heir, but witness. Arthur asks who may hold the crown when the crown is the least of it, and Guinevere—already answering as civic witness rather than queen's companion—says the crown may be held by whoever can carry the oath that no one is chosen for belonging. Lancelot strips the bright helm from his head and answers that he will be one sworn witness among others, not a beautiful exception, while Mordred accepts the keeper's keys but refuses any promise that peace will last. Morgan adds that a peace never tested is only a waiting room, and Percival asks what the Grail says of the widows and exiles outside the shrine.
Write the civic articles
Arthur and Guinevere turn the rhythm into articles: crown as covenant, limited knightly privilege, Guinevere's civic role, and the Grail held as covenant rather than trophy.
Send the covenant beyond the shrine
Percival and Bedivere carry the promise toward widows and exiles, forcing the court to show whether the peace survives outside the walls.
Let Morgan challenge it
Morgan demands proof that the covenant can fail, and the court must either answer honestly or admit it has not looked.

encounters.title: The civic articles are written, Lancelot has withdrawn from seduction politics,

text_script.value: The articles are laid on the long table as ink is still wet, and Arthur writes the first line himself: no one holds Camelot by birth, by blood, or by love. Guinevere adds her clause in her own hand, that the crown is a caretaking and not a title, and Lancelot, helm already gone, speaks plainly that the romance he once carried is a relic now, and he will not carry it past the threshold of the shrine. Merlin reads the Grail's answer aloud: covenant. Mordred posts the keys where the shrine door opens and says the peace will be judged where it is least flattering. Morgan smiles at the charter and asks what happens on the road beyond the walls when the knights are gone.
Send the covenant outward
Percival and Bedivere carry the articles beyond the gates toward widows and exiles, and the court must answer whether the peace still holds when no knights are watching.
Let Morgan test the covenant
Morgan names a flaw in the articles and demands the court answer it in the open, turning the peace into an argument rather than an agreement.
Settle the succession openly
Arthur, Guinevere, and Lancelot draft an open succession pact, ending the succession drama and forcing each of them to state publicly who holds the crown when Arthur no longer does.

encounters.title: The civic covenant is ready to leave Camelot, but its fate now depends on whethe

text_script.value: At the outer gate the sealed articles rest on a stone shelf while Percival, cloak trailing mud, is shown the last rule before dawn: the covenant must be read aloud to those who have no voice in court. Mordred holds the shrine keys openly and tells him the peace will be judged by whether the road answers; Morgan drifts close to make him hand over the seal, and Lancelot breaks her silence by naming her a test, not a threat. Arthur asks what the Grail says when there are no witnesses, and Guinevere answers that it will say whatever Percival repeats when the court is far enough away to be innocent. Bedivere sets the charter under Percival's arm and says the shrine will be open after sunrise, whether or not the road is kind.
Send Percival into the road
Percival leads Bedivere and the covenant toward widows and exiles, forcing Camelot to accept that the peace may be judged by strangers rather than by the Round Table.
Answer Morgan in the open
The court must publicly answer Morgan's demand for proof that the covenant can fail, forcing Lancelot, Arthur, and Guinevere to expose what they fear about the peace.
Hold a dawn return
Merlin sets a dawn deadline for the road test, turning Camelot into a place that listens for failure instead of hiding behind the Grail's glow.

encounters.title: Camelot now faces a dawn-tested choice: carry the covenant outward, expose its f

text_script.value: The dawn horn did not free Camelot; it made the road outside the gates look newly born. Percival shrugged off mud before the court and said the widows and exiles had not praised the covenant, they had tested it: bread was counted, names were spoken, and the guest-list was longer than the court's map. Mordred set the shrine keys on the threshold and told him no relic may live unwatched, while Morgan asked what would remain if the road refused to answer. Guinevere answered that an ordinary promise is harder to kill than a glory, and Merlin read the Grail's reply in a low voice: not for Camelot, but for whoever can keep a promise when no crowd is clapping.
Send the covenant deeper
Percival and Bedivere carry the charter beyond the gates toward the exile roads, and Camelot must answer whether peace can be witnessed by strangers.
Answer Morgan publicly
Arthur, Guinevere, and Lancelot must name the covenant's failure point in the open, making the peace into a shared argument instead of a flattering ritual.
Make the shrine public custody
Mordred, Merlin, and the Lady of the Lake convert the Grail from sacred symbol into a public charge, forcing Camelot to defend ordinary people as a duty.

encounters.title: Camelot is now deciding whether the Grail remains a private miracle, a public co

text_script.value: The council did not wait for permission to argue; it came out of the gatehouse with mud still on its boots and a question written over Arthur's throne: what kind of kingdom will the Grail keep when the road decides first. Arthur set aside the sword-hilt and said, if the peace is a door, let the hinges face the widows, not the hearth of glory. Guinevere named the empty seat of Keeper of the Commons, Lancelot folded his charm away and declared that a promise kept in public beats a passion kept in secret, while Merlin read the Grail as a covenant rather than a crown. Morgan leaned close to ask what the oath would do when it hurt someone, Mordred answered that the keys would stay openly visible, and Percival said the road had already heard the first answer.
Open the keys
Mordred and the Lady of the Lake place the Grail under public oath beside widows, exiles, and oath-breakers, forcing Arthur to defend custody instead of prestige.
Name the cost
Arthur, Guinevere, and Lancelot must choose which privileges they will surrender, making loyalty, love, duty, and law collide in the open.
Send proof outward
Percival and Bedivere take the covenant into the exile roads before sunrise, and Camelot must answer what failure will mean to ordinary people.

encounters.title: Camelot has moved from private custody to public covenant, but the road outside

text_script.value: Dawn broke over a shrine door left open for widows, exiles, and oath-breakers, and Camelot no longer looked like a palace guarded by glory. Arthur set the sword-hilt on the threshold beside bread, ink, and the Grail's uncovered bowl; Guinevere called the seat of Keeper of the Commons a public office, not a courtesy; Lancelot closed his hand around the charm and said that beauty had no right to judge a promise. Merlin heard the Grail answer in a low civic tune: not sacred above all, but witnessed below all, so that an ordinary hand could break it and a stranger could carry it. Morgan asked what if the oath protected one side more than another, while Mordred declared that the keys would remain on the open altar until the road outside answered; Percival reported bread counted and names spoken, and Bedivere found the exiles had brought their own questions for the court to answer.
Hold the road test
Percival and Bedivere return with hard evidence of who the covenant serves, forcing Arthur to accept both praise and public failure.
Surrender a privilege
Arthur, Guinevere, and Lancelot each name one right they will trade for the covenant, turning personal loyalties into law.
Ward the Grail openly
Merlin, Mordred, and the Lady of the Lake convert the Grail into a covenant under witnesses, ending any claim that it stands above ordinary custody.

encounters.title: The road test shows the covenant works in some villages but fails quietly for wi

text_script.value: The returns from the road came in before the bells, mud and ink together: Percival emptied his satchel of village tallies, Bedivere laid out the letters he had carried, and the Grail sat on the altar not as a relic but as a scale that kept tilting. Arthur listened while Percival read that three villages had taken the covenant, one had refused it as theft of its own custom, and one widow's household had accepted it and then lost its grain-debt because no one at court had checked the books. Morgan asked what the oath would be worth to the refusing village; Mordred answered that refusal was a right, not a failure; Merlin muted the Grail's civic tune and said it would not bless a treaty that only worked for the proud; Guinevere lifted the second Keeper's seat to the table and said the office was not a reward; and Lancelot set his hand flat on the charm so no one could accuse him of hiding a private interest. The question left on the table was whether the peace was a promise or a habit — and who would keep it if keeping it meant losing what it protected.
Audit the covenant
Guinevere, Percival, and Bedivere demand a public ledger of every village's debt, acceptance, and refusal, and Arthur must defend the Grail's oath or hollow it out.
Pay the cost now
Arthur, Lancelot, and Guinevere each surrender one privilege openly, making the covenant a real civic bargain at the price of Camelot's honor.
Leave the road open
Mordred, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake send a witness caravan to the refusing village, risking the covenant's stability to show that refusal is answered with presence, not force.

encounters.title: The court has accepted that the covenant must be witnessed, audited, and costly,

text_script.value: By the second bell, the ledger had broken Camelot's comfort: Percival tapped the debt lines with a worn stub, Bedivere read the refusals without flinching, and the Grail on the altar hummed less like a treasure than like a rhythm a village could learn. Arthur pushed back the sword-hilt and said that a peace which only dazzled the proud was no peace at all, while Lancelot set the charm down among knives and seals and refused to call beauty a judge of promises. Merlin muted the magic until it could be witnessed rather than ruled, Morgan asked what the oath would do to a thief who kept a widow fed, and the Lady of the Lake closed her cloak over the covenant rather than over a secret.
Seat the Commons
Guinevere accepts the civic office openly and Arthur surrenders the highest knightly privilege, moving the council toward a covenant that survives both victory and loss.
Make Lancelot a witness
Lancelot trades his private claim for a public oath, ending seduction politics but risking the Grail's peace if the others treat the oath as flattery.
Test the Grail
Merlin, Morgan, Mordred and the Lady of the Lake open the covenant to a night test, forcing the court to reveal whether the Grail can be guarded without being feared.

encounters.title: Camelot is ready to bind the covenant into a public office, but the peace now de

text_script.value: At the third bell the covenant table was not an altar anymore: it held wax seals, village tallies, and one open book where the Grail had waited. Guinevere stood in the Keeper's seat and said that the office belonged to whoever could make it survive a winter; Lancelot pressed his own hand flat to the oath and refused to call love a private key; Mordred demanded that his name be written beside the refusal, not only beside the victory. Merlin listened for the covenant to be seen, not heard, while the Lady of the Lake held the Grail as a witness who could be asked a question and still leave the room.
Bind the witness seal
Lancelot and Guinevere seal the peace in front of village witnesses, making the covenant lawful but forcing Camelot to accept that love and duty can no longer be separated.
Open the Grail audit
Merlin and Morgan let the commons test the Grail's covenant, turning the relic from a shrine into a guarded public instrument whose failure would be visible.
Place Mordred in the table
Mordred is seated with Arthur and Guinevere, so the succession question is settled by argument and office rather than by a promised duel.

encounters.title: Camelot is governed as a modest, enduring realm: Arthur accepts limits, Guinever

text_script.value:
At first light the Round was no longer a ring of swords but a circle of desks, bread, and witnessed promises. Arthur laid his crown beside the law-book rather than on his head and told the court that the king would now stand on common ground with every serf at the gate; Guinevere took the keeper's chair, not as queen's decoration but as the person who would answer for who was fed; Lancelot set his lance against the table and said his love was no longer a charter for anything, and would be, if he were spared, the oath-keeper who kept the covenant honest. The Grail rested in a plain case on the altar, and Merlin, watching it, called it not a prize but a promise that had been given to anyone who would hold it in good faith. Mordred nodded once at Arthur's humility, and the Lady of the Lake pressed her palm to the seal, and the covenant closed like a door that only opened inward.

Camelot did not become a perfect kingdom; it became a governable one. Arthur kept the throne but gave up its shine, Guinevere held the civic office with both hands, Lancelot chose service over secret union, Mordred sat inside the peace rather than beyond it, and the Grail was kept as a covenant of peace rather than a trophy of power. The court was not flawless, and ordinary life outside it was not even, but it was honest: oaths were witnessed, refusals were written, failures were admitted, and the Round was governed by promises that could still be broken and remade. In that quiet, unglamorous light, Camelot survived as a small and enduring realm, and the story of the Grail continued not as a prize to be guarded but as a duty to be kept.

encounters.title: Camelot has begun to fracture into households: the oath is refused, Gawain and M

text_script.value: The seventh candle guttered as Arthur rose to speak the Round Table oath aloud in the great hall, but Lancelot laid his hand flat upon the broken seal and said that love owed him more than any charter ever could. Gawain answered that a feud between kin was no longer a private grievance but a crack in the stone, and Mordred replied that the exiles would follow the stronger name, not the elder one. Morgan, standing at the threshold with her white cloak, let the silence stretch until it split the hall, then murmured that two oaths could be kept if one agreed which one would be forgiven first.
Arthur re-speaks the oath and demands every household swear or leave
Camelot becomes a court of forced compliance: those who refuse form a second household outside the hall, and the Round Table is broken into warring factions under one roof.
Lancelot publicly withdraws from the oath and takes his household with him
The pact collapses into two visible households - those who keep the crown oath and those who keep a private love-oath - and succession is left to be claimed by households rather than by law.
Morgan brokers a hidden double pact between Gawain, Mordred, and Lancelot
A private, double-faced bargain stabilizes the hall in appearance while quietly rewriting the Round Table's terms, leaving legitimacy to depend on secrets rather than oaths.

encounters.title: Camelot is dividing into named households around a broken table, with Merlin con

text_script.value: Candle smoke curled around the cracked charter while Merlin redrew the succession in ash and asked who would feed the exiles if the Round Table could not. Guinevere argued that the dead oath deserved burial rather than resurrection, and Gawain answered that loyalty split like frost on a lake, not all at once. Morgan smiled from the colonnade and said that every bargain was a small throne, and the one forgiven last would sit longest.
Arthur declares succession publicly, binding the crown to household pledges
The crown survives as a spoken law, but each household must now beg for bread and legitimacy before the exiles, tightening the feud between Gawain and Mordred.
Gawain and Mordred make the feud open before the court
The hall turns into a hostage of names, banners and oath-shards, and Arthur must choose between visible order and private reconciliation.
Morgan brokers a hidden double pact for Gawain, Mordred and Lancelot
The court appears stable, but legitimacy shifts from open oath to secret favor, leaving Merlin and the Lady of the Lake to decide whether the pact can survive exposure.

encounters.title: The Round Table is now a public split of four households, with the Grail placed

text_script.value: Merlin chalked the broken seal into four columns at the hall's center and made the exiles set their pledges beneath each. Arthur said the table could break but not be remade by pretending it had not, while Morgan answered that broken things often survived by being given new names. Mordred pulled three oath-shards from the table and called the exiles to choose which name would feed them, and Lancelot looked at Guinevere until she put her hand over the candle instead of speaking. The Lady of the Lake set the Grail on the fallen seal and said that it would not choose between the banners, but only answer who could face the question of what it was for.
Arthur binds the exiles into four pledges beneath the columns
Camelot gains visible law again, but bread and legitimacy are now divided by household, and Gawain and Mordred fight over which pledge deserves the crown.
Morgan forces the double pact into the open at the Grail
The hidden bargain cannot be denied, the court becomes either the pact's witnesses or its enemy, and Arthur must publicly choose between saving the crown and protecting the oath.
Percival and the Lady of the Lake carry the Grail out of the hall
The relic becomes an exile and a test, drawing households outside the charter and leaving the broken pact exposed to whatever the exiles do next.

encounters.title: The double pact is now public, the exiles are refusing a tidy settlement, and Ar

text_script.value: Morgan tore the hidden bargain across the Grail's silver rim and made every household read its own debt in loud letters: bread, names, shame, oath, or mercy. Gawain answered that a table did not feed people by being perfect, and Mordred answered that a crown did not survive by asking for forgiveness. Arthur held the broken seal in his bare hand while the exiles kept stepping forward until even Merlin stopped naming conditions and simply watched the light change. The Lady of the Lake said the relic would answer the question of what it had been made for, and the hall heard the same word in every household: not power, not love, but a promise kept when keeping it cost something.
Arthur binds the four households beneath one common shrine
Camelot gains a fragile common covenant, but legitimacy is now a rotating claim among households, and the exiles must choose between bread and political exile.
Mordred declares the pact void and takes the oath-shards
The broken pact becomes an open succession crisis, turning the Round Table into contested land, temple, and feud at once.
Lancelot, Guinevere and the exiles step outside the charter
The court loses its ritual shelter but gains an unofficial community that may carry law and faith beyond Camelot.

encounters.title: The pact is openly broken, exiles are leaving for the woods beyond the wall, the

text_script.value: Mordred's shards still lay in the rift, and the households had begun to count bread, swords and exile instead of oaths. Arthur tried to gather the pledges before sunset and Mordred answered that no pledge could hold a table already broken, so the exiles left one by one for the woods beyond the wall. Lancelot knelt with Guinevere's hand in his and asked whether a promise kept in shame could still be law, while Morgan, standing on the seal, said the law had always belonged to the loudest winner. Percival carried the Grail toward the gates and the Lady of the Lake set the broken seal against the door so that no one could pass unless they named what they had left behind.
Gawain stands with Arthur against Mordred's crown claim
Camelot becomes a contested succession within the hall, forcing the households to fight over legitimacy while the exiles wait outside the wall.
Lancelot and Guinevere leave with the exiles to build a new charter
The court loses its ritual shelter but gains an unofficial community that can carry law, love and faith beyond Camelot.
Merlin binds or breaks the old magic openly
Morgan's hidden power is exposed, forcing Arthur and Mordred to choose between the crown's future and the survival of the oath.

encounters.title: The gate now separates those who will still name what they left behind from thos

text_script.value: The Lady of the Lake set the broken seal against the gate and forced every traveler to name one thing they carried out of Camelot: a child's name, a debt, a shame, a sword, a broken promise. Mordred read the shards as a ledger and called the Round Table a ruined toll-house; Gawain said a table was not saved by crowns but by who still fed the hungry. Arthur answered that the oath could not be revived by force, so it had to be rebuilt around the exiles, while Morgan laughed on the seal and told Merlin to choose whether the old magic would serve a living household or a dead one. Percival held the Grail close to the threshold, and the hall felt the difference between a relic watched over and a relic asked to carry meaning.
Arthur rebuilds the oath around the exiles
Camelot becomes a smaller, unstable commonwealth of households that can still protect the weak, but it loses the legitimacy of a unified royal court.
Mordred claims the oath-shards as law
The shards become hostages in a household struggle, forcing Arthur, Gawain and the loyalists to defend legitimacy against a crown built from broken fragments.
Merlin names Morgan's old compact
Morgan's hidden bargain becomes public, exposing whether Merlin, Arthur and the exiles can survive the magic that built Camelot or must break it.

encounters.title: The broken court is split between exiles who still name their debts, a contested

text_script.value: At the threshold, the named exiles crouched by small fires while inside the hall the loyal swords were already being counted as bread, ashes and exile. Arthur asked for a truce of three bells; Mordred answered that a truce was a debt owed by the living; Morgan murmured that the crown was being kept by the few who feared being erased. Merlin, half-turned from the old seal, said the compact had never promised equality, only that all would keep one another honest, and Percival carried the Grail toward the gate as if the relic could decide who was allowed to leave.
Arthur stakes the threshold for named households
Camelot loosens from a single court into named households with separate sworn circles, trading crown legitimacy for protection of the weak.
Gawain and Arthur hold the shards
Mordred's claim becomes a civil feud, forcing loyalists and exiles to choose sides while the gate can no longer be an honest threshold.
Merlin breaks or binds the old compact
Morgan's bargain is exposed at the seal, forcing Arthur and Mordred to decide whether the crown survives by honest law or by magic that answers no one.

encounters.title: The court is no longer one body but a chain of small sworn fires and a contested

text_script.value: By the hinge of the hall, the exiles lit a second chain of small fires while Mordred carried the broken seal toward the dais and called it a charter no one could refuse. Guinevere set her wedding oath down beside a hooded child's bundle, and Lancelot answered not with a sword but with a question: what would the Round Table keep if it could no longer ask every debt be one debt? Morgan traced the faint sigil beneath the seal and smiled, saying the old magic had not broken; it had only started keeping accounts. Percival held the Grail at arm's length, not to bless the argument but to see whether it could still be innocent of politics.
Arthur turns the shards into household pledges
Camelot loosens into separate sworn households that protect the weak but surrender a single royal seal and court legitimacy.
Lancelot names one oath he can no longer keep
Lancelot's public choice splits the court into those defending the table and those defending his divided love, hardening feuds rather than ending them.
Merlin opens Morgan's hidden compact
The compact becomes public, forcing Arthur and Mordred to decide whether to expose, break, or remake a bargain that holds both crowns together.

encounters.title: The court must now choose between fragmented households that protect the weak, s

text_script.value: At the hinge of midnight, the broken compact lay open under the Grail like a map of a country that had died twice. Mordred laid the shards on the table and called them a census; Arthur named the widows, exiles and oath-keepers whose names were missing from it. Morgan said the old magic had not fallen, it had changed hands, and Merlin answered that a bargain could be rewritten only if someone was willing to say what it had cost. Percival raised the Grail, not as a crown but as a witness, and the hall fell silent enough to hear the gate-fires outside answer one by one.
Arthur grants named household charters
Camelot becomes several sworn hearths with shared burdens but no single seal, so the weak are safer while succession loses unity.
Guinevere and Lancelot make sanctuary for the child
The Round Table is split between protectors of the table and defenders of shelter, forcing the gate to choose between law and rescue.
Merlin reads Morgan's compact aloud
Morgan's bargain becomes public fact, forcing Arthur and Mordred to expose, break or remake the magic that holds both claims together.

encounters.title: Morgan's compact is public, the child is sheltered by Guinevere and Lancelot, an

text_script.value: Merlin unrolled the sigil across the broken table and let every candle gutter as the old magic caught the light, and when silence stretched, Morgan said: "You did not lose the compact. You only read it aloud for the first time." Mordred did not kneel; he put his charter beside the grail and named the fires outside Camelot as his own oath-keepers, and Lancelot answered him not with a sword but with a question about what the table was for when the table itself had to choose sides. Guinevere rose, laid the child's bundle on the seal of the court, and told the hall that the house of the Round Table now held a hostage: whoever held the child held the law. Outside the gates the answering fires burned one by one, and none of them agreed on whose name to carry.
Arthur makes the compact public and calls for a single ruling
Arthur forces the court to choose one oath under light, so the Round Table either survives as a sworn republic of debts or divides into households that can no longer share a crown.
Guinevere and Lancelot make the child the hinge of every oath
The oath follows the child's safety rather than the crown, so ordinary households protect the weak while succession and the old magic lose the single seal.
Merlin and Morgan try to rewrite the compact with named debts
The old magic is rewritten under public eyes, but only by making every oath-breaker visible, so Morgan gains influence over the terms and Mordred must either submit or challenge them.

encounters.title: The Round Table is visibly split into oath-households, the child is sheltered by

text_script.value: The hall had become three rooms wearing one roof. Arthur chalked the charters on the table's broken rim and called each household by its oath, while Guinevere kept the child wrapped in a blanket woven from gold thread and said, 'A law that cannot carry a small life is not a law, only a sword.' Lancelot set his cloak over the child's bedroll and looked at the grail as though it were an empty chair, not a crown. Mordred placed his oath-banner against the wall, not as conquest but as evidence, and Morgan leaned close to Merlin and murmured, 'Then let the ledger speak; it already has a name for you.' Outside, the gate-fires burned in three colors, and no two agreed on the word for safety.
Arthur accepts a limited throne held under household oaths
Camelot survives as a coalition of hearths and charters, but succession is no longer sacred to one crown and Mordred may join or refuse under the same terms.
Guinevere and Lancelot carry the child beyond the gate into border sanctuary
The child and its protectors leave the throne hall, forcing Arthur, Mordred, Morgan and Merlin to fight over custody of the law itself while ordinary households gain privacy.
Merlin and Morgan carve Morgan's compact into a public ledger of debts
The old magic becomes visible as a binding inventory of promises, giving Morgan real authority but forcing every claimant to declare what was promised, betrayed or still owed.

encounters.title: The court is now visibly fragmented into oath-households, the child is protected

text_script.value: The negotiation failed over the last unmarked charter: Arthur offered a shared crown if every household would swear beneath it, but Mordred said, 'Then a hearth is a charter too,' and Gawain answered that the law had already become a list of exceptions. Guinevere kept the child wrapped tight in a gold-lined cloak and told the hall that safety could not be weighed against legitimacy. Morgan opened the ledger and made every betrayal visible, while Merlin watched the names crawl like moths over the seal. By dusk the Round Table had not fallen; it had simply become three tables, and the gates burned in colors that refused to match.
Arthur accepts three hearths sharing one bridge-ward
Camelot survives as a weak coalition of oaths instead of a single court, giving ordinary households breathing room while leaving succession unsecured.
Guinevere and Lancelot carry the child to a border sanctuary
The child and its protectors leave the throne hall, forcing the rest of the court to choose between custody, law, and visible loyalty.
Morgan and Merlin finish the ledger while excluding sworn debts
The old magic becomes public power, but unrecorded promises become dangerous claims and the households stop trusting the table as a place of law.

encounters.title: The Round Table is now three oath-hearths sharing one roof, the child is unresol

text_script.value: By candle-thin dawn the hall had stopped being a hall and become three hearths that no longer spoke the same sentence. Percival read the unnamed charters aloud until Gawain laid a hand on the page and asked whether a law could be carried by a child who would one day grow up in a different king; Guinevere answered from beside the bedroll that safety was not a statute but a weight, and that some laws were only swords. Morgan traced the row in Merlin's ledger where every promise wore a different color and murmured, 'Then ask who the debt belongs to, not who the crown does.' Mordred did not raise his banner; he set his oath-token beside it, face up, as if the only question left were whether anyone would still answer it.
Arthur binds the hearths into three oath-wardships under one bridge-ward
The court gains an uneasy coalition of households instead of a single crown, leaving succession to be argued by whoever controls the bridge-ward.
Lancelot and Guinevere carry the child beyond the gate to border sanctuary
The child and its protectors leave the throne hall, forcing Arthur, Mordred and the magic-holders to choose between custody, law and exile while ordinary households gain privacy.
Morgan forces every household to declare one promise kept and one broken before the ledger closes
The old compact becomes a public inventory of guilt, giving Morgan real authority while making every claimant answerable to the hearths.

encounters.title: The Round Table is now three households with the child between custody and exile

text_script.value: Dawn found the hall still split into three hearths, but no longer silent. Mordred walked to the middle with the broken charter folded beneath his cloak and said, 'Then let the king say what he is,' and Arthur, too tired to lie, answered, 'A bridge without a road.' Lady of the Lake leaned over the ledger and named each promise aloud until Guinevere stopped her with a hand on her shoulder, whispering that some sins could not be read aloud without being born twice. Percival lifted the child toward the door and asked whether the road beyond the gate was a border or a boundary, and Morgan answered that it was whatever the living chose to build there. By mid-morning the oath-tokens had been carried out of the hall and into three kitchens, where the court learned whether a promise could survive without a crown above it.
Guinevere and Lancelot carry the child across the gate to the border sanctuary
The child and its protectors leave the court, leaving Arthur, Mordred and the magic-holders to answer for custody while ordinary households lose the last visible reason to stay together.
Morgan declares every sworn debt now answerable to the ledger, not to the crown
The households must pay, pledge, or break openly, turning Camelot into a contest of visible obligations and forcing Arthur to choose between rule and accountability.
Gawain and Percival split the child's custody between the three oath-hearths
The court becomes a bargained household instead of a throne, giving the ordinary households real stake while leaving succession and safety suspended.

encounters.title: The court is divided into three households around a broken Round Table, with the

text_script.value: The three kitchens had not merged into a court; they had become rival weather systems with the same roof. Mordred set his oath-token on the gap where the Round Table had once been continuous and said, 'If a promise cannot hold one roof, show me where I was to put it.' Arthur looked at the child, then at the three fires, and answered, 'In a road that can survive its own light.' Morgan opened the ledger and let one page slip past the others, showing the debts as a ladder of broken stepping-stones; Gawain named a child, a widow, a beggar, and an exile as the four things the old table had promised to hold. By dusk the question was no longer whether Camelot would survive, but whether survival could be chosen before succession was named.
Arthur and Merlin bind the three hearths to a rotating bridge-ward instead of a single crown
Camelot survives as a witness-held household rather than a monarchy, but succession becomes a contested rotation and Morgan gains practical leverage.
Lancelot and Guinevere open the border gate while Gawain and Percival keep the inner gate for exiles and widows
The court splits into sanctuary and court, giving ordinary people privacy but making the claim to the crown impossible to defend without bloodshed.
Morgan forces each household to surrender one kept promise and one broken one before the ledger closes
Morgan wins uneasy authority over the court, while Arthur and Mordred are both publicly answerable to debts they can no longer ignore.

encounters.title: The court is now a three-hearth bargain in a broken hall: the child is suspended

text_script.value: The three kitchens had fused into three weather systems, and at noon the broken Round Table became a negotiation under a canopy of smoke and moonlight. Morgan opened the ledger and said, 'Let the gate say what it is before the gate says otherwise,' while Arthur answered, 'Then we witness it, and let the witnessing be enough.' Gawain insisted that the inner threshold must not be held by one hand, Guinevere and Lancelot answered that the border could be a refuge without becoming a wall, and Percival asked whether the child would live by a crown or by a road. Mordred closed the charter over the child's custody and said, 'Then carry my name too,' and Bedivere carried three tokens toward the three doors, each token already marked by a debt or a loss.
Arthur, Merlin and Mordred bind the three hearths to a witness-road rotation
Camelot survives as a witnessed household rather than a monarchy, succession stays suspended, and Morgan gains practical leverage without gaining a throne.
Lancelot and Guinevere hold the border sanctuary while Gawain and Percival keep the inner gate
Ordinary exiles and widows gain shelter but the claim to the crown becomes violently unavailable to the unified court.
Morgan calls every oath before the public debt-court and demands pay, pledge or break
Morgan wins real authority, Arthur and Mordred become publicly answerable to household losses, and the succession moves from promise into wager.

encounters.title: The broken Round Table has become three guarded hearths around an unpaid oath: t

text_script.value: At grey dawn the three fires answered one another rather than the hall, and Morgan set Mordred's oath-token between Arthur and the child, saying, 'An oath is either a road or a ledger line; choose which it is to become.' Arthur answered, 'Then we do not crown it; we carry it past the gap,' while Lady of the Lake lifted the grail-cloth and showed that the water had no loyalty to any one fire. Gawain and Percival barred the inner threshold, Lancelot and Guinevere argued for a sanctuary that was not a wall, Mordred demanded that his claim be counted as a debt rather than a shame, and Merlin glimpsed the old magic beginning to choose its own side.
Arthur, Merlin and Bedivere carry the oath as a rotating witness-ward instead of a crown
Camelot survives as a rotating witness-road, Mordred must either accept a share of the road or leave it, and Morgan gains real leverage without becoming sovereign.
Lancelot and Guinevere open the border sanctuary while Gawain and Percival keep the inner law
Ordinary exiles and widows gain shelter and privacy, but the crown becomes undefendable without blood, exile or a new myth of legitimacy.
Morgan forces every hearth to answer one kept promise and one broken one before the ledger closes
Morgan becomes the court's working power, Arthur and Mordred are both publicly answerable to household losses, and succession moves from oath into wager.

encounters.title: Camelot is now three law-hearths around a suspended child and succession: the bo

text_script.value: At dusk the broken oath had stopped sitting in one hall and now hung in three ovens, each hearth answering a different law. Morgan set the open ledger between Mordred's child-token and Arthur's crown-chain and said, 'An oath must become either shelter or sentence; do not ask it to be both.' Gawain answered that a road held by one hand was only a siege with better manners, while the Lady of the Lake lifted a water-cloth and said, 'The water will not bless a wall that turns its back on those outside it.' Percival pressed the court to choose before the last fire made its sound, and Lancelot stood at the border steps with the exiles behind him and the crown before him, unable to make either shape whole.
Arthur and Percival bind the hearths into a rotating witness-road
Camelot survives as a witnessed household rather than a single monarchy, Mordred must accept a share of the road or leave it, and Morgan gains leverage without sovereignty.
Lancelot, Guinevere and the Lady of the Lake open the border sanctuary
Ordinary exiles and widows gain shelter and a right to be seen, but the crown becomes harder to defend without violence, exile, or a new myth of legitimacy.
Morgan forces every hearth to pledge one kept promise and one broken promise
The court becomes publicly answerable to household losses, Morgan becomes the working power of the broken Round Table, and succession moves from oath into a formal wager.

encounters.title: Camelot is now a contested witness-ward: a suspended child and succession sit be

text_script.value: At candle-thin dusk the oath lay open under three cold relic-lights while Mordred lifted his blood-token and said, 'Count it a debt, not a stain; I will carry the interest.' Morgan set the ledger's edge against the child's chair and told the court that a road which excluded the exiles was a wall wearing a shrine's clothes, while Gawain answered that a law which could not be sworn was only a mood. Arthur laid the crown-chain on the table and asked every hearth to name one promise it would keep and one it would surrender before the grail-cloth closed over the child.
Arthur, Merlin and Bedivere bind the hearths into a rotating witness-road
Camelot survives as a witnessed household rather than a single monarchy, Mordred must share the road or lose its protection, and Morgan keeps leverage without becoming its sovereign.
Lancelot, Guinevere and the Lady of the Lake open the border sanctuary
Widows and exiles gain shelter and a right to be seen inside the walls, but the crown becomes harder to defend without violence, exile or a new myth of legitimacy.
Morgan forces one kept and one broken promise from every hearth
The court becomes publicly answerable to household losses, Morgan becomes the working power of the broken Round Table, and succession moves from oath into a public wager.

encounters.title: Camelot now stands as three contending hearths around a suspended child and a di

text_script.value: At the last hour before the grail-cloth could close, the oath broke into three spoken vows instead of one sentence. Morgan held the ledger open as if Camelot were an account she could still balance, while Mordred set his blood-token on the floor and said, 'If this table has no oath, let it have witnesses or let it have witnesses’ doors.' Gawain warned that every household about to leave would take a piece of the law with it, and the Lady of the Lake answered that a wall cannot save those still outside it. Arthur pressed the court to choose what would be kept when the compact no longer held: shelter, succession, or the right of exiles to be heard.
Arthur and Percival make the hearths swear a rotating witness-road
Camelot survives as a shared road with rotating arbitration, Mordred is forced to accept a real share or surrender it, and Morgan loses sovereignty while keeping leverage.
Lancelot and Guinevere keep the border sanctuary open
Widows, exiles and children gain a public right to be seen inside the walls, but the crown becomes easier to attack, narrate, and displace.
Morgan forces one kept and one broken promise to be spoken aloud
The Round Table becomes publicly answerable to household losses, Morgan gains working power without a crown, and succession moves into a formal wager over memory, land and the child.

encounters.title: Camelot is now a three-hearth compact under pressure: the child waits beneath th

text_script.value: By the fourth bell, the Round Table had split into three hearths pushed into one circle, each edge still warm with its own candles. Arthur set the succession question into the grail-cloth's fold and called for a third path; Guinevere answered by naming widows already outside the gate, and Lancelot, torn between the oath and the road, asked whether loyalty could be divided without becoming a lie. Mordred answered that he would not be made a guest in his own bloodline, while Morgan wrote one word beside his name and showed Arthur the half-erased line: the pact was no longer a sentence, only a payment schedule.
Arthur, Merlin and Bedivere swear the rotating witness-road
Camelot survives as a rotating witness-road, Mordred must accept a real share or lose the compact's protection, and Morgan keeps leverage without becoming sovereign.
Lancelot, Guinevere and the Lady of the Lake ratify the sanctuary
Widows, exiles and children gain a public right to be seen and sheltered, but the crown becomes smaller, harder to defend and more easily narrated as tyranny.
Morgan forces every hearth to speak kept and broken promises
The Round Table breaks publicly into competing households, Arthur rules only as first hearth, and succession becomes a public wager over memory, land and the child.

encounters.title: Camelot ends as fractured households around a closed grail-threshold, with Lance

text_script.value:
At the twelfth bell the Round Table ceased to be one sentence and became three fires speaking over one broken floor. Arthur offered the oath as mercy, Morgan answered with the ledger, and Lancelot rose from the seat beside Guinevere with his hands empty: 'I will not eat the peace I cannot defend,' he said, and walked beyond the border light. Mordred laid his blood-token on the ash, Merlin watched the relic-lights tilt, and Morgan closed the ledger over the last kept promise as Camelot broke into separate households rather than a single doomed kingdom.

The Broken Pact closes Camelot as a court that cannot become either a just republic or a single doomed kingdom. Arthur does not win by refusing mercy; he loses by being unable to bind mercy to law. Lancelot walks away with loyalty kept as an empty oath, Guinevere holds the names of the excluded, Mordred inherits a claim that is more blood than authority, and Morgan remains the one who knows precisely what was owed and what cannot be paid. Merlin can still see the relic, but the relic no longer rules a table. Morgan may keep leverage, Mordred may keep a throne-claim, and the Lady of the Lake may still give passage, yet the Round Table has become three hearths, an unanswered border, and a broken promise no longer powerful enough to hold the future.

encounters.title: Excalibur is loose in Camelot, with Arthur, Gawain, Lancelot, Mordred and the el

text_script.value: In a torch-darkened relic hall, Excalibur had been drawn from its mooring and left lying across two sword-rests, its bright edge forked by a fine crack. Arthur demanded that every claimant put one hand on the blade, while Mordred simply closed his fingers around the hilt and said the crown belonged to the hand that could be seen to hold it. Lancelot, unbuckling his chain, answered that a sword could be guarded but never owned, and Morgan murmured that the blade remembered an oath broken long before this court. Bedivere saw the sheath split open along its seam, and the Lady of the Lake drew a ribbon of salt across the table edge to mark where the table stopped being a meeting and became a battlefield.
Gawain seals Excalibur under the crown
Gawain binds the sword to the heir-oath, forces Mordred to declare public refusal, and turns Camelot into either a guarded republic or a defensive throne.
Lancelot carries Excalibur beyond the oath-ring
Lancelot takes the blade toward his household, starting a claimant-faction and forcing Arthur to choose between open oath, theft-like recovery, or civil fracture.
Morgan and Merlin loosen the old binding
The blade answers to claimants rather than the table, so oaths split into three visibly hostile allegiances and the shrine loses its single authority.

encounters.title: Excalibur now sits among torn charters in a Camelot already split into guarded,

text_script.value: By the second bell after midnight the shrine court had stopped looking like a court: three torch-groups burned in separate arches, Mordred's banner dripping red over the lower gate, Lancelot's household lamps in the exiles' walk, and Arthur's gray standard no longer touching the grail-stone. Excalibur lay on a cushion of torn charters, its bright edge notched where Merlin's binding had been forced open; Guinevere, gripping Gawain's sleeve, told the elders that a blade is not a covenant, while Morgan answered that neither is a covenant until somebody is willing to be seen breaking it. Percival swept the oath-ring's shards into a row, Bedivere read the crack like a boundary line, and the Lady of the Lake said that the first real kingdom would be the one that made the broken thing useful again.
Arthur closes the shrine as law
Arthur declares the shrine a closed civic space, forcing Mordred to choose public breach or betrayal and splitting Camelot into guarded law versus sworn claim.
Lancelot carries Excalibur to the exiles
Lancelot plants the sword among widows and outsiders, turning oath-keeping into patronage and forcing Arthur to defend legitimacy against those outside the Round Table.
Morgan breaks the old binding
Morgan lets the relic answer three allegiances, hardening oaths into rival feudal charters and stripping the Round Table of its common language.

encounters.title: Excalibur now hangs over a fractured Camelot where a civic-guarded oath, an exil

text_script.value: At the third bell the relic-hall had three weathers at once: Arthur's gray banner dim over the grail-stone, Mordred's red pennant snapping on the lower gate, and Lancelot's exile lamps already moving down the road beyond the walls. Excalibur lay across the broken oath-ring with its crack running like a violet seam, while Gawain held up the torn charter and said the oath could be renewed if the heirs swore before the same broken table, and Lancelot answered that a blade broken by law was not a law but a door. Morgan leaned over the table and told the court to let the sword ask three questions instead of answer one, Mordred declared the fenced ward his claimant kingdom, and the Lady of the Lake answered that a shrine cannot hold the blade until it stops pretending to be the only court. Merlin set three threads of pale magic over the hilt, and Percival walked the seam of the crack as if reading a border that had not yet learned its name.
Gawain swears a ward-and-exile common oath
Gawain opens the exiles' walk to a renewed common oath, making Camelot a guarded civic kingdom but forcing Mordred to fight the fence, not only the throne.
Lancelot carries Excalibur into the exile road
Lancelot plants the blade among widows and outsiders, converting oath-keeping into patronage and making Arthur choose between restoring the shrine or accepting a sworn claimant.
Morgan and Merlin set the sword to three allegiances
The old binding splits into three answering threads, stripping the shrine of single authority and turning oaths into rival feudal charters that can be sealed, stolen, or broken.

encounters.title: Excalibur now sits under live claimants, three oath-languages and an unresolved

text_script.value: By the fourth bell the shrine-court no longer had one gate: Mordred's red cord was stretched across the lower steps, Lancelot's widow lamps waited at the exile road, and Arthur's gray sigil sat unanswered over the grail-stone. Guinevere said, 'Do not let a blade become the only father we can still name,' while Mordred answered, 'Then make the father of the law something we can swear to, or else break it honestly.' Merlin let a thin thread of gold and silver cross the broken hilt, Morgan watched it hesitate, and Percival counted the shards of the oath-ring aloud until every household in Camelot had heard its own name in the crack.
Arthur grants claimant status, not kingship
Camelot becomes a court of fenced oaths rather than a single crown: Mordred is admitted to counsel and guarded wards, while Arthur must answer for legitimacy instead of rule alone.
Lancelot carries Excalibur to the exile road
The sword is installed among widows, outsiders and sworn-not-yet-full-members, forcing Arthur to defend a shrine he cannot keep as private property.
Morgan and Merlin let Excalibur answer three charters
The relic splits into contestable jurisdictions, turning succession into feudal bargains that can be sealed, stolen or renounced before witnesses.

encounters.title: Excalibur is now a three-lamp contested relic whose seam is widening, forcing Ca

text_script.value: At the fifth bell the relic-hall had three gates open at once, and Excalibur lay across the oath-ring with the violet seam already widening under the weight of three lamps: Arthur's gray, Mordred's red, Lancelot's pale road-light. Percival read the marks on the blade as if they were a charter being written by its own break, while Lady of the Lake refused to lift the hilt until all claimants could stand close enough to hear it. 'A sword should make room for the law, not swallow it,' Guinevere said, and Gawain answered that room would have to be built by fence, road, and witness or else never arrive. Merlin's threads trembled above the hilt, Morgan watched them decide whether to bind or split, and Mordred set his pennant against the lower steps rather than across the grail-stone.
Gawain swears the witness-oath
Camelot becomes a fenced court of sworn witnesses: Mordred must accept counsel and wards, be exiled, or answer as an armed claimant.
Lancelot gives the blade a road
The relic moves toward widows and outsiders as patronage, and Arthur must choose between defending the shrine as private law or enlarging the kingdom by promise.
Morgan and Merlin cut one binding thread
The binding splits into open jurisdictions, making succession a contestable feudal charter that can be sealed, stolen, or renounced before witnesses.

encounters.title: Excalibur now answers three charters at once, its violet seam widening, with the

text_script.value: At the sixth bell the seam in Excalibur widened enough for a fingertip of violet light to show, and the three lamps no longer burned at the same height: Arthur's gray guttered, Mordred's red burned steady, Lancelot's road-light leaned toward the door. Merlin pressed two fingers to the broken hilt and said the old word, but the word would not settle, and Morgan added a second, colder one that made the sword answer both questions at once. 'A blade cannot be a father to three houses,' Guinevere said. 'Then it must be a charter, or it is nothing,' Mordred answered, and Gawain shouted for the witnesses to count aloud before the light on the blade drowned their voices. Bedivere spoke the first names in the exile-roll, and Lady of the Lake set her circlet on the floor between the three lamps so that no one would pretend the shrine was free of them.
Arthur splits the sword into three co-guardians

Camelot becomes a fenced council of equal oaths: Mordred keeps the red lamp as armed ward, Lancelot keeps the road, Arthur keeps the grail-stone, and succession is decided by charter votes rather than inheritance.
Lancelot carries Excalibur to the exile road
The relic leaves the shrine and enters the exile-road charter: Arthur must either follow it out or defend a shrine he can no longer claim as his own.
Morgan and Merlin read the three charters and bind them with a third oath

The binding is rewritten as a third law that can hold the relic only while every claimant keeps a live oath to the exile-roll, turning the sword into a public instrument that can be sworn, broken, or refused.

encounters.title: Excalibur is a three-claim instrument with a severed thread, an uneven lamp-set,

text_script.value: At the seventh bell the sword answered before anyone touched it: gray, red, and road-light struck the oath-ring together, and a single violet line snapped through the seam like a stitch pulled from a charter. Mordred named himself keeper of the red lamp and gave no answer to Arthur's challenge, while Lancelot placed a foot on the exile-roll and said, 'The road is not waiting for your mercy.' Gawain demanded one witness for each claimant, Lady of the Lake set her circlet on the oath-ring until oaths could be counted, and Merlin's threads trembled around the blade until Morgan cut one thin thread loose, leaving the sword suspended between law and road. Percival read the names twice, Bedivere refused to strike the first name from the exile-roll, and Guinevere watched Mordred's pennant slide from the lower steps toward the grail-stone.
Gawain builds a counted witness-fence
Camelot becomes a fenced court of counted oaths: Mordred must accept counsel and wards, answer as an armed claimant, or have his claim recorded as exile and road.
Lancelot carries the road-lamp to the exile road
The relic moves toward the exiles as patronage, forcing Arthur to choose between defending the shrine as private law and promising the road to widows, exiles, and outsiders.
Morgan binds the severed thread into a feudal charter
The sword becomes a public feudal charter with three jurisdictions, making succession contestable before witnesses and capable of being sealed, stolen, or renounced.

encounters.title: The seam is open, Mordred is on the grail-stone, Lancelot is at the gate with th

text_script.value: At the eighth bell the seam in Excalibur opened past a fingertip: violet light ran down the oath-ring and the three lamps stopped guttering in rhythm. Mordred crossed beneath Gawain's counted fence and laid one glove on the grail-stone while Lancelot swung the road-lamp to the gate and said, 'The exiles will hear whether Camelot feeds them or watches them walk.' Merlin caught the blade's trembling voice; Morgan answered it with a second, colder voice, and Guinevere answered both with the plainest question: 'Who eats tonight if this charter breaks?' Bedivere refused to strike the first name from the exile-roll, and the circlet fell from the oath-ring to the floor as the sword hummed once, three times.
Arthur forces a witnessed three-part split
Camelot becomes a publicly witnessed three-jurisdiction charter: Mordred gains a guarded claim, the exile-road is promised entry, and the grail-stone is left open to oath-breaking.
Lancelot opens the exile road
The shrine becomes a road court: widows and exiles may enter the gate, but Mordred gathers armed followers to block them and test whether Camelot feeds or merely watches.
Morgan binds the seam into a feudal charter
The sword is recast as a feudal instrument with witnesses, road-wardens, and exile rights, but magic now judges succession rather than leaving it to free oaths.

encounters.title: Excalibur is a three-voice instrument; Mordred is entangled with the grail-stone

text_script.value: At the ninth bell the sword did not stop ringing; it forked into three voices, and each voice cast a different shadow across the floor. Mordred kept one knee on the grail-stone and the other on the exile-roll, saying, 'The throne is only bread until someone feeds it,' while Lancelot held the road-lamp high enough to show a line of widows and lame riders still outside the gate. Gawain called for one named witness for every claim; Bedivere would not strike the first name, and Lady of the Lake set the circlet on the seam and refused to choose which of the three should hold it. Morgan cut the last thin thread to fall, Merlin caught the falling light, and Guinevere asked the only question the hall could not answer: which oath would keep the gate open at tomorrow's supper?
Arthur witnesses a three-claim covenant
The hall records Mordred as an armed claimant, Lancelot as road-warden, and the Lady as relic-keeper; Excalibur can be lawful, stolen, or renounced, but no one may hold it alone.
Lancelot opens the road to widows and exiles
Widows, exiles, and named oath-breakers enter the shrine under the road-lamp; Mordred may block them, test mercy, or force Arthur to defend both the gate and the sword.
Morgan and Merlin bind the last thread
A sealed feudal charter forms in the blade: succession is judged by visible oaths, but magic now rules whether the charter can be forged, stolen, or renewed.

encounters.title: At the tenth bell the seam is split into three colors, Mordred holds the exile-r

text_script.value: At the tenth bell the fallen thread keeps striking the floor like a bell-clapper, and the grail-stone answers with a second seam. Mordred puts his glove on the exile-roll and tells the widows waiting at the gate, 'Come inside and see which oath buys you bread,' while Lancelot shifts the road-lamp toward the crown and Merlin catches the last violet thread against his chest. Morgan answers by cutting the circlet free; Guinevere asks whether an open road can still be an oath, and Bedivere finally marks the first exile-name beside the seal.
Arthur witnesses a three-seat fracture

Camelot becomes a publicly witnessed three-seat charter: Mordred takes an armed claim, Lancelot swears as road-warden, the Lady keeps the grail, and Excalibur no longer grants one ruler sole legitimacy.
Lancelot opens the exile road
Widows and named exiles enter under the road-lamp; Mordred may seal the gate with armed followers and force Arthur to defend both the sword and the meal being promised outside it.
Morgan and Merlin bind the last thread
The charter is magic-bound as a feudal compact: oath-breakers can be forged, stolen, or renewed, but succession is judged by the seam rather than by free choice alone.

encounters.title: The exile-roll is torn and burning with names, Mordred has moved the grail-stone

text_script.value: At the eleventh bell the exile-roll tore along its stitched edge, and every widow-name on it caught fire at once. Mordred slid the grail-stone halfway into the gateway and called out, 'Let the road prove the sword: whoever feeds the smallest table holds the king?' Lancelot set the road-lamp on the threshold and answered past him, 'The road is already owed; bring your claim through the gate or do not let us speak of it.' Morgan snapped the last binding-thread free, Merlin caught its violet light against his chest, and the three voices in Excalibur sharpened from tones into signatures: steel, bread, and wax.
Arthur witnesses three signatures
The hall records three lawful seats rather than one king: Mordred keeps an armed claim, Lancelot swears as road-warden, and the Lady keeps the grail, with Excalibur held only by shared seal.
Lancelot swears the gate before the blade
Widows, exiles, and named oath-breakers enter under the road-lamp; Mordred may seal the gate with armed followers and force Arthur to defend the meal promised outside the shrine.
Morgan and Merlin loose the last thread
The charter becomes a tearing, magic-fed feudal compact: it can be forged, stolen, or renewed by touch, and succession is judged by the seam rather than by a single oath.

encounters.title: The torn roll is burning as currency, Mordred has fixed the grail-stone across t

text_script.value: At the twelfth bell the torn exile-roll flares once more, but its names begin to read like currencies: bread, wage, blood. Mordred sets the grail-stone across the gateway and tells Arthur, 'Call heirs over the threshold before the seam lets you sleep.' Lancelot answers with the road-lamp, 'No heir may cross until a widow is named and fed,' and Morgan slices the last violet thread; Merlin catches it against his chest as the three signatures of Excalibur—steel, bread, wax—burn through Camelot like a charter in three colors. Percival, bearing a lame exile and the child he is owed to shelter, waits for Arthur's nod; Gawain keeps the shields from leaning on the gate.
Arthur witnesses a three-seat charter
Arthur records a public charter of three seats—armed claim, road-warden, grail-keeping—so Mordred must either march under an open sky or carry the claim out of Camelot.
Lancelot opens the gate to widows

Widows, exiles, and named oath-breakers enter beneath the road-lamp; Mordred seals the gate with armed followers and forces Arthur to defend the meal promised outside the shrine rather than only the crown.
Morgan and Merlin bind the portable seam
Morgan and Merlin fold the torn binding into a portable feudal compact that can be carried, stolen, or renewed by touch, making the first refusal forge Excalibur's next wielder.
