encounters.title: The visible council still presents peace, while the hidden second ledger now con

text_script.value: Below the lighted council, relic-shelves cast amber shadows over a ledger that no longer matched the oaths spoken at dawn. Morgan watched Mordred fold exile names into wax instead of fire, while Merlin kept one hand on a crooked candle and one on the broken mirror's edge. 'A seal is not a grave,' Morgan said; 'it is a curtain that still holds the room.' Percival saw the white cup cool under the Lady of the Lake's sleeve and asked Arthur whether a relic could be used as both promise and leverage. Lancelot looked at Guinevere, not at the throne, and answered only that every public kindness now had a price hidden in the dark.
Morgan hardens the second ledger
The exiles are erased from public memory while their debts and injuries are quietly transferred to new oath-holders, making later resistance harder to coordinate.
Merlin forces the ledger into the open
Morgan and Mordred are exposed as rewriting oaths, forcing Arthur and Guinevere to choose between open confession, public betrayal, or a deeper hidden peace.
The Lady of the Lake ties the cup to succession
The Grail becomes a living bargain that can secure Mordred's claim, protect Merlin, or be refused outright, sharpening every later succession choice.

encounters.title: The hidden second oath-book now governs exile debts, shrine custody, and success

text_script.value: Below the oath-table, Morgan slid a second waxed sheet beneath Arthur's polished cup; every exile's name had been moved from the public page to the margin as a steward, a keeper, or a debtor. Merlin, now at the stair's lower rail, read the line aloud and answered, 'The room remembers you still, whatever the ink says.' Percival brought two keys - one for the shrine, one for the ledger - and asked whether a key given for safety could be kept when safety had been redefined. Lancelot watched Guinevere's thumb worry the edge of the rewritten oath until it curled, then tucked the curled corner back as if it were still the dawn's promise.
Morgan binds shrine-keepers to the margin
Shrine custody, exile debts, and succession timing become one quiet obligation, making later open resistance harder to coordinate.
Merlin refuses to certify the rewrite
Morgan must choose between exposing Merlin's witness, exiling him beyond the court, or tightening the hidden peace around his refusal.
The Lady of the Lake moves the cup past the shrine gate
The Grail cup is tied directly to whoever controls the hidden ledger, forcing Arthur and Mordred to decide whether custody belongs to law, love, or oath.

encounters.title: The hidden vault now coordinates exile memory, succession timing, and cup access

text_script.value: Beneath the still-lit Round Table, a second audience gathered in the vault where oaths were kept as debts: clerks wore masks of warm gold, exiles stood in a line like candles in a frosted window, and the visible court's trumpets sounded two rooms above. Morgan set the cup on a hidden altar and said, 'No freedom here; only a kept name, a carried debt, and the chance to make the fire look smaller.' Merlin lifted the crooked mirror, found himself looking not at the king but at the queue of names, and answered that a room that forgets its debtors is not safe but only easier to decorate. Arthur heard the Lady of the Lake say that the Grail did not crown anyone; it simply refused to be forgotten, while Mordred reached for the succession tally and did not once look at the cup.
Morgan opens the second council
The oath-keepers rehearse new custody terms in private, so the next confrontation is not Arthur's choice alone but a bargain among the living who now hold the cup's access.
Morgan offers Merlin a gilded witness seat
Merlin becomes publicly visible as the voice of resistance while remaining confined, splitting the court between those who need his witness and those who fear his truth.
The Lady of the Lake ties the cup to the ledger
Whoever controls the hidden ledger can now decide when the Grail is shown or withheld, making succession and custody the same negotiation.

encounters.title: The visible court is now performing a peace that depends on a hidden scale balan

text_script.value: Behind the lantern-lit hall, the council's applause was replayed in whispers while clerks stitched exile names into the lining of a hidden oath-cloak. Morgan set a brass scale under the Grail cup and said, "Let the trumpets sound below; up here, custody is arithmetic." Arthur answered that a peace should not need an inner stage, while Merlin stepped back from the ledger and called the rewritten oath "a pretty wall with the doorpaper changed." Mordred looked at the exile line, then at the succession tally, and left the cup to balance on its own. Guinevere pressed the curled oath-corner flat without naming it, and Lancelot saw the Lady of the Lake tie the cup's shadow to the ledger, not to any crown.
Morgan keeps Merlin visible but sealed
Merlin becomes the public face of resistance without real access, so Arthur and Mordred must choose whether his witness is strength or a leash.
The exiles move from margin to inner ring
The hidden alliance gains a living chorus, making open resistance harder to ignore and making the next bargain harder to split among claimants.
The Lady of the Lake sets custody on the scale
Whoever balances the cup decides whether succession belongs to the table, the exiles, or the hidden ledger.

encounters.title: The shadow court has rehearsed Arthur's visible resignation as a sacrament, tyin

text_script.value: Behind the audition of voices, the hidden ward opened beneath the Feast of the Broken Crown: exiles stood like candle-figures under a painted sky, ash-gold clerks wrote Arthur's resignation as a blessing, and the visible hall kept singing the peace two rooms above. Morgan did not argue with the crown; she said, "Let the king smile at the feast and spend his name in the room where names are owed," while the Lady of the Lake set the Grail on a ledger whose pages were themselves the oath. Merlin reached for the crooked mirror, found the exiles' faces instead of his own, and answered that resistance without a witness was only an apology wearing a cloak. Mordred touched the succession tally and did not smile at the cup, but at the line of debtors; Arthur felt the oath harden into a debt he could no longer settle merely by being king.
Arthur opens the bargain
Arthur names the hidden oath in the visible council, forcing Morgan to accept public custody or expose the shadow court as a competing government.
Let the exiles speak
The exiles are allowed to state their debts in open council, turning the hidden alliance into a coalition Arthur and Mordred can no longer ignore.
Morgan offers Merlin the sealed seat
Morgan offers Merlin either the public witness seat or the sealed exile, forcing the alliance to choose between visibility and protection.

encounters.title: The visible peace now hangs by a second oath whose hidden ledger is being bound,

text_script.value: The second vow was stitched while the feast still held its note: Morgan drew a knife of lamplight through the ledger's binding, and every visible candle leaned toward the exiles as if listening. 'Let the feast keep its smile,' she said, 'while the room where names are owed keeps its ledger.' Arthur felt the old oath lose its edges and found himself naming hidden names aloud, while Lancelot saw the Grail's shadow split into two keys, one for Arthur's peace and one for the court that would survive it. Merlin answered from the sealed shrine that the shadow court was not a new kingdom but a sentence already spoken.
Arthur names the sealed oath
Arthur forces the council to choose between declaring the shadow court illegitimate or accepting it as the only honest law, turning private custody into public politics.
Percival tests the divided Grail shadow
Percival can expose the cracked keyhole and either unmake the divided custody or bind Arthur and Morgan to the same relic.
Merlin answers from the sealed shrine
Merlin's witness forces the exiles and Mordred to decide whether his voice is testimony or a leash on the succession.

encounters.title: The shadow court now controls the rewritten oath behind the visible feast, with

text_script.value: By night the visible council sang the peace on, while beneath it the oath was rewritten in ash-gold ink: the Grail's two keys lay on a ledger split down the middle, one blade labeled light and the other custody. Morgan set her hand on the ledger and told the gathered shadow court that an oath rewritten in secret was still an oath, only quieter, and that appearances were not lies but bridges over famine. Lancelot watched the key for Arthur's peace turn toward the exiles rather than the crown, and understood that the alliance would not break the feast but replace its meaning. Merlin, hooded and nearly silent, kept his sealed witness like a stone in a pocket and said only that a law that could not be witnessed was already a rumor.
Arthur reads the rewritten oath aloud
The council must publicly accept the shadow court's custody or declare it illegitimate, turning hidden bookkeeping into an open constitutional crisis.
Lancelot chooses which key to defend
Lancelot can defend the key of peace and risk the exiles, or guard the custody key and force Arthur to choose between legitimacy and survival.
Merlin lifts the seal and speaks
Merlin's witness forces Morgan and Mordred to decide whether the sealed court can be publicly witnessed or must disappear entirely.

encounters.title: The shadow court has exchanged appearances for tokens: exile safety, relic custo

text_script.value: Behind the visible feast, the undercroft smelled of beeswax and wet stone: Morgan laid two lead-sealed tokens on the table where the ledger used to burn, one marked exile, one marked relic, while Mordred smiled at the shapes of ordinary faces outside the doors. Arthur said the peace could not kneel; Guinevere answered that neither could the dead, and Lancelot understood that the bargain would keep the crown fed by paying the poorer roads for its silence. Merlin kept his seal like a stone in the pocket and said only that a truth kept hidden was still a wall, and Morgan closed the shrine mouth without opening it.
Arthur bargains for the exiles
Arthur risks crown legitimacy by trading relic custody for exile safety, forcing Mordred to choose between alliance with Morgan or defiance in the open court.
Merlin breaks the seal
Merlin forces Morgan to publicly witness the shadow oath or disappear him, moving Camelot from bargains to open war over law.
Percival chooses the exiles
Percival binds the Lady of the Lake to rescue the exiles, splitting Arthur's peace from relic custody and pulling the visible council toward rupture.

encounters.title: The shadow court has turned the tokens into a live exile charter tied to relic c

text_script.value: Above the feast, Arthur's horn sounded a truce that everyone mistook for peace; below it, Morgan opened the relic-ledger again and set the exile token beside the shrine key, saying, 'The poor must be visible somewhere, or the crown will eat its own legend.' Mordred did not deny it. He asked instead whether the exiles would be paid as supporters or stored as silence. Guinevere looked at the tokens and heard the famine in the phrasing. Lancelot, holding the custody key, realized the alliance was not a theft of the Grail but a new charter written by the people outside the walls. Merlin kept his witness closed, but the seal no longer felt sealed; it felt like a door being measured.
Arthur countersigns the exile charter
Arthur trades crown legitimacy for visible shelter, forcing Mordred to choose open alliance with Morgan or public rupture with the exiles.
Lady of the Lake lifts the shrine curtain
The shrine's true custody becomes visible to those who look, forcing the visible council to recognize or deny the shadow charter before it hardens.
Merlin speaks while keeping the seal
Merlin turns the hidden witness into public pressure without exposing its proof, forcing Morgan to either disappear him or forge his testimony into visible law.

encounters.title: The shadow charter is now a live draft tying exile road, relic custody, and the

text_script.value: Behind the second curtain, Morgan dealt the charter as cards: one white for relic custody, one black for the exile road, one blue for the witness now called a door. Arthur heard the oaths being rewritten in the grammar of need. Lancelot set the relic key across his palm and felt it count the exiles like debts; Mordred smiled because every debt he could name was also a title. Guinevere asked who would answer if the poor were paid late, and Morgan answered that answers were how kingdoms chose when they slept. Merlin kept his mouth shut, but his seal pressed against his breastbone like a second heartbeat.
Arthur names the exile road
Arthur makes the exile road a public obligation, forcing Morgan to either honor it visibly or brand him a usurper.
Offer Merlin the measured door
Merlin either accepts the seal as office or exposes its empty promise, moving the shadow court from negotiation to open legitimacy war.
Lady of the Lake forces the relic to answer
The relic answers only to named oaths, splitting Lancelot and Morgan and pulling the visible council toward rupture.

encounters.title: The visible feast continues while the shadow court rewrites oaths as accounts, w

text_script.value: Beyond the wax-lit gallery, Morgan laid the exile tokens on a road-map and asked each chosen name to give only his purpose, not his oath. Mordred heard loyalty become a currency and smiled, Guinevere heard mourning become a tax and gripped her glove, and Lancelot heard his devotion to the Queen and his devotion to the crown entered as two separate accounts. Merlin stood at the curtain's edge with his sealed witness tight to his breastbone, and every silence around him became a locked room.
Force the feast to witness the bargain
Morgan must either let the hidden ledger be seen or break the illusion of unity before the whole visible court.
Offer Merlin the locked witness
Merlin can open the witness and expose the bargain, or refuse and be made visibly useless while the oaths harden around him.
Let the exiles name their road
The road becomes a demand rather than a metaphor, forcing Morgan to honor survival or publicly brand the poor as uncounted.

encounters.title: The shadow court now moves from drafting oaths to testing what happens when the

text_script.value: Behind the visible council, the doors were no longer shut; they were scored with small dark marks that turned when touched, each one naming a duty too small to refuse. Morgan set a chalice of frozen wax on the table and said, Show me the price, while Arthur heard the feast outside calling him King and the sealed witness against his heart answering with a name. Merlin did not step forward, but the seal against his ribs pressed twice, as if a locked room had learned to breathe. When Guinevere lifted her veil, the candlelight did not reveal her grief; it counted it.
Let the poor read the price aloud
The exiles force Morgan to honor survival or declare them uncounted, shifting the shadow court from private bargain to public demand.
Let Merlin open the sealed witness
Merlin can reveal the hidden ledger or force Morgan to prove the seal is sacred, splitting legitimacy openly inside Camelot.
Let Lancelot keep debt and title apart
Lancelot either protects the Queen's unpaid love or accepts the crown's account, forcing Morgan and Mordred to choose whose legitimacy survives.

encounters.title: The hidden ledger now ranks survival above inherited title, with Arthur forced t

text_script.value: In the lamp-lit undercroft, Morgan sets three copies of the same oath on the slate table: one for Arthur, one for the Queen, one for the dead who still owe. Mordred says the crown may be heirless, but not uncounted, while Lancelot watches his love for Guinevere and his service to the king become two locks on the same door. Merlin presses the sealed witness to his ribs and names the exile who already understands the new rule: survival is counted only where survival cannot plead. Outside the grille, the feast thins into a chorus of applause that no one has yet answered.
Seal Merlin's witness into the ledger
Arthur can make the hidden record public or force Morgan to admit that Camelot now runs on sealed words.
Give exiles a visible seat
Exiles gain a voice that Morgan must answer openly, shifting the shadow court from private bargain to public demand.
Let Lancelot choose one lock
Lancelot either shields Guinevere at the cost of title or accepts the crown's account and exposes the bargain to the Queen.

encounters.title: Arthur must now choose whether the sealed witness stays locked or is spoken alou

text_script.value: Morgan set the three oaths in a row and swept one across the slate, then invited Arthur to say which words he would keep. Merlin stood at the fringe of the circle and asked, once, whether his silence was a bargain or a sentence; the table answered with the sound of a struck relic, not a voice. Guinevere refused the wax chalice and set it aside, while Lancelot laid his hand flat on the crown's account so his own name stayed visible to all who looked. Outside the grille, exiles answered the feast's applause with a low, patient sound like bells counted under water.
Let the exiles speak through the seal
The shadow court is dragged toward open public demand, and Morgan must either pay survival to the frightened poor or admit the seal protects only those it names.
Let Lancelot carry Guinevere's oath
Love and title fuse into one visible bargain, forcing Mordred and Morgan to either forgive it or break it in front of the court.
Let Merlin remain at the fringe
Old magic withdraws from the visible council, shifting real power to Morgan's bargains and leaving Arthur to rule on what the relic means after Merlin's witness is no longer asked.

encounters.title: The shadow court now prices survival and forgetting behind the visible council,

text_script.value: Behind the sealed grille, the visible council praised the wine while Morgan unrolled three oath-scrolls on black slate and carved a new line beneath each: who would live, whose name would not be counted, and what the Grail would do if it ever slipped a bargain. Mordred drank the Queen's refusal as a trophy; Merlin, marooned at the threshold, did not curse the price but asked whether the old magic could remember a door that had been shut in its face. Arthur heard the Lady of the Lake count exiles in a voice used for relics rather than armies, and answered that if legitimacy can be bought, then so can survival.
Make exiles unforgettable
Morgan must either pay the poor with visible rights or leave the shadow court permanently marked by the names it hid.
Let Lancelot sign as Guinevere's proxy
Love and title fuse into one visible signature, forcing Mordred and Morgan to forgive it or break it in front of the court.
Close the shadow court
Arthur can restore the visible rite, but Morgan and Mordred may keep the hidden ledger and turn Camelot into a kingdom of masks.

encounters.title: The shadow court rewrites the oath around a witness who may testify even when he

text_script.value: Morgan set the wax chalice aside and had her scribe re-carve the oath in a hand no knight in the hall had ever seen, while the visible council watched the flames rather than the words. Mordred laughed low at the new line — not a crown, but a witness — and said the crown had always been easier to hold than to keep honest. Merlin stood at the fringe of the candlelight and asked whether a witness could be made to testify to its own silence; Arthur did not answer, and outside the grille the exiles began counting their own names aloud, each one a door the shadow court had not yet decided to open or close.
Make the hidden bargain public
The court's illusion breaks open and Morgan must either give the exiles the names they already count or concede that the bargain was only ever a disguise for power.
Let Mordred hold the witness
The succession passes quietly into Mordred's hand, and Arthur must rule as a man whose legitimacy is remembered by those who never saw it made.
Force Merlin to speak
The old magic steps back into the visible council and asks whether the oath can be re-witnessed by one who has been made invisible.

encounters.title: The witness can now be written on the living, the dead, or the unnamed, and the

text_script.value: Behind the grille, Morgan set the Grail chalice on the black slate, and the visible council still ate beneath the stained glass. The exiles outside had not stopped counting their names; now they were naming the rooms they had been shut out of. Merlin pressed a cold, unmarked band into Arthur's palm and said the witness could be written on the living, the dead, or the unnamed, and each choice changed what Camelot would remember. Mordred watched Lancelot the way a man watches a coin about to be spent, and the Lady of the Lake lowered her voice to the rhythm of a relic being carried across a threshold.
Write the witness on the living
Arthur must take the unmarked band, and the crown is declared a burden carried in public rather than a title held in secret.
Write the witness on the dead
The exiles' names are carried by the memory of the fallen, and Morgan must decide whether the dead can testify without being kept.
Leave the witness unnamed
The names go back into the dark, and the shadow court can survive by staying legible only to those who live inside it.

encounters.title: The shadow constitution is now a current of rooms: the oath can be widened into

text_script.value: Behind the grille, the exiles had moved past names into rooms: one sealed cell for a widow, one stair for a clerk, one door for a chapel that no longer woke. Morgan placed the unmarked band over the Grail shelf and said that a crown could be stolen but a current could not be destroyed, only agreed to. Merlin answered from the dark that the old constitution had counted the living because it feared the dead, and Mordred watched Arthur's hand hover above the ledger where the names were being written in smoke. Around the visible hall, the feast kept its small applause; beyond the grille, the exiles were already singing the next doors open.
Open the ledger in public
The visible council hears the hidden bargain, and Morgan must either hand the exiles the doors they already count or admit the bargain was only a disguise for power.
Seal it inside Merlin's circle
The old magic becomes the only visible counterweight, forcing Arthur to choose between granting Merlin authority or leaving the oath vulnerable to rewrite.
Give the witness to the relic
The Lady of the Lake rules by threshold rather than title, while Mordred's claim and Arthur's legitimacy both wait on what the Grail answers.

encounters.title: The shadow court has moved from counting names to choosing thresholds, with Morg

text_script.value: Below the visible feast, a widow had carried her husband's tally-stick into a sealed cell and knocked until the door opened inward. Morgan sat at the black table with the exiles' ledger and no guard; Merlin, on the far side of the grille, answered her not with a curse but with a list of names he could no longer remember and chose not to recover. Lancelot set his sword on the slate, Mordred watched the hand that steadied it, and Arthur had to speak while Guinevere, Lady of the Lake and Percival remained silent enough to be evidence. 'If the oath is a current,' Morgan said, 'then who carries the charge when the lamps go out?'
Let the exiles choose the thresholds
The exiles gain real doors and office, but Mordred can call them outside the crown while Arthur loses sole authority over legitimacy.
Bind the oath to the Grail threshold
The Lady of the Lake becomes the only judge of what can be entered, forcing Arthur and Mordred to fight over whether the Grail may rule without naming the keeper.
Seal the constitution inside Merlin's circle
Merlin survives as hidden authority, yet the public court becomes a fiction and Guinevere, Lancelot and Percival may be forced to choose whether to witness it or become its instruments.

encounters.title: The shadow constitution now exists as a second, wax-sealed current in which Merl

text_script.value: Beyond the grille, the exiles' rooms had grown tall enough to swallow the feast above; Morgan poured wax over the ledger where the old oath had run, and the words hardened into a second script: the living may enter only through doors they have already survived. Merlin stood in a dark niche with his name struck from the rite, saying only that he remembered the sound of the dead and not the reasons, while Lancelot chose not to answer when Mordred called the rewritten ledger a crown without a king. Arthur watched Guinevere, the Lady of the Lake and Percival remain still as witnesses, and Morgan asked who would be left when the lamps, the oath and the crown all changed hands at once.
Burn Merlin's margins
Merlin is reduced to a marginal witness, the rewrite becomes Morgan's authority, and Arthur must accept a shadow court without his old counterweight.
Let the relic witness the rewrite
The Lady of the Lake decides whether the rewritten oath may enter the Grail, making Mordred and Arthur both answer to a threshold they cannot command.
Countersign as an exile
Arthur gives legitimacy to the rewritten order while Lancelot and Mordred split over whether the countersignature is rescue, surrender or a new kind of inheritance.

encounters.title: Camelot appears stable while legitimacy is rewritten in hidden bargains: Merlin

text_script.value:
Beneath the lamps of the feast, Camelot sang its old anthem while, behind the relic-shrine, Morgan held the true council: names drawn on wax, thresholds pledged in exchange for doors, and the oath written not as one law but as several buried contracts. Merlin was no longer answered by his name but by a silence the room accepted; Arthur looked at Guinevere, Mordred, Lancelot and the Lady of the Lake as if asking which of them would keep their face; Percival stood just outside the light, listening to a settlement made without him. When the feast ended, every seat stayed filled, every candle stayed lit, and the kingdom appeared whole—while power had already moved into a court no one could see.

The Shadow Court closes the age with an uneasy grace: Camelot is still Camelot—lights, seats, oath-song and a Grail set before the people—but the living law no longer answers the visible council. Merlin stands at the edge of memory, no longer a keeper of truths but a door the bargains pass through; Mordred's claim is carried in private warrants, Lancelot's divided loyalty is made into a sealed current, and Morgan's hidden alliances bind exiles, relics and succession to a system of appearances. The realm is not destroyed so much as remade quietly, stable in its faces and uncertain in its meaning, while the Lady of the Lake, Guinevere, Arthur and Percival learn that legitimacy can be performed for centuries after it has been rewritten behind the lamps.

encounters.title: Camelot is abandoned at dawn and the exiles must choose what the new settlement

text_script.value: At grey first light the gates of Camelot stood open and no banner moved. Percival dug a foundation trench on the lower field while Bedivere patched the one lamp that had survived the fall of the shrine, and the exiles - Gawain, Lancelot, Guinevere, the Lady of the Lake, and a handful of oath-bound tenants - dragged bells, tools, and roof-tiles across the mud toward a safer ridge. Lancelot said the new settlement could not be a refuge if it was only a smaller Camelot; Percival answered that it would be a road, a roof, and a name remembered before a crown. Arthur stood at the broken threshold, refusing to lead and refusing to vanish, while Merlin watched the first smoke rise and called it a question instead of a victory.
Percival swears the exiles to a ridge charter
The ridge becomes a governed settlement under a public covenant, so succession is answered by common roofs and law rather than by an heir.
Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake carry the shrine shards with the exiles
The settlement is marked as a living shrine-road, drawing Arthur, Mordred, and others toward competing pursuit of the shards.
Guinevere and the Lady of the Lake guard the road and shelter the exiles
Survival is secured by open gates and common keeping, but Camelot is left oathless and unstable without a visible successor.

encounters.title: The exiles are choosing between open common law, shrine-road memory, and Arthur'

text_script.value: The first council fire burned over mud, half-sawn beams, and a charter that Percival refused to call a crown. Gawain tried to laugh at the list of promises and found it serious when a stranger knocked at the low gate, while Merlin warned that a settlement could endure only if its laws survived disbelief. Bedivere laid the shrine-road over his palms, Guinevere said the lamp could not stand unmarked where faithful and thieves might mistake it, and Lancelot told Arthur that a road taught to survive would carry Camelot's memory sooner than the relic's crown could.
Percival swears open roofs and common labor
The ridge becomes a governed refuge in which succession is answered by shared duties, debts, and visible promises rather than by a chosen heir.
Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake mark the shards as a road
The settlement is marked as a living shrine-road, pulling Arthur, Mordred, Gawain, and wandering loyalists toward a contest over what the relic means.
Arthur declines the crown and takes a pilgrim steward's place
Camelot becomes fragile but real, forcing the survivors to decide whether legitimacy can grow from care, oath, and survival instead of inheritance.

encounters.title: The ridge settlement must decide whether hospitality, a witnessed shard-road, or

text_script.value: The knock came just before dusk, and Mordred stood at the low gate with a debt-roll wet at the edges, not wearing a crown but asking whether the ridge was a refuge for the oathless as well as the oath-bound. Gawain wanted to bar the road; Percival answered that a road built around exclusion would be a smaller Camelot with new doors. Lancelot told Mordred that the shrine shards were not a trophy to be handed over but a road to be kept, while Guinevere asked what the exiles owed to people who had not chosen their cause.
Percival opens the common table to the oathless
The ridge feeds and houses Mordred and the displaced villagers under shared labor, weakening crown-claims but requiring the exiles to keep promises rather than defend a throne.
Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake leave the shards as a public road
The shards become a witnessed way for pilgrims, refugees, and claimants to pass, pulling Arthur, Mordred, and Gawain into a contest over what the relic means.
Arthur names keepers, not a successor
Camelot's memory is carried by rotating keepers and public debts rather than an heir, so legitimacy grows from care and repeated promise instead of inheritance.

encounters.title: The renewed settlement now faces the hard test of keeping oaths, feeding the oat

text_script.value: The second morning after the council found the common table still set under a torn cloth, with bread, a cracked cup, and a ledger open to an empty page. Percival made Mordred carry the smallest sack of barley, not as a penance but as an act of proof: the oathless had already made the ridge a household, not a fortress. Gawain said the road could not keep its faith if everyone was forgiven by a grand gesture, and Guinevere answered that forgiveness would have to be counted like water and grain. Merlin touched the shard-road and heard it not as a crown but as a breathing line, while the Lady of the Lake set one lantern toward each family already promised a place.
Percival records promises in the common ledger
Every meal, repair, debt, and guest-right becomes a witnessed debt owed to the settlement, so legitimacy can be checked by repeated proof instead of a royal title.
Bedivere lights the shard-road for pilgrims and exiles
The shards become a traveling threshold that can be entered by those who help it, pulling Arthur, Mordred, Gawain, and outside loyalists into a public test of care.
Mordred demands a covenant for his own dead and living
The ridge must answer whether the oathless are guests, claims, or neighbors, forcing Arthur, Percival, and Merlin to decide what memory can be given to those who rejected the crown.

encounters.title: The ridge must choose whether its survival is a witnessed road, a public commons

text_script.value: On the third morning of the renewal, the ledger at the ridge gate began to fill with debts no crown could cancel, and Mordred set a strip of bone-tags on the table for his dead, saying plainly that they were not crown property and should not be measured only by what they claimed. Percival answered that the settlement could feed, repair, and remember if the owed were named before the worshipped; Merlin leaned close to the shard-road and said it answered to witnesses better than to relics, while Guinevere pressed Arthur to give the exiles a public share rather than a title. Gawain warned that a list of the righteous would become a new wall, and Lancelot answered that a road without witnesses would become a shrine for people who no longer needed one.
Percival keeps the debts visible
The settlement turns hospitality into recurring work and named obligations, weakening throne-claims while forcing both Arthur and Mordred to answer for promises kept in public.
Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake light the road

The shard-road becomes an entrance that can be entered only by witnesses who can carry it forward, pulling Gawain, Lancelot, and the outside loyalists into a hard contest over who is allowed to inherit Camelot's memory.
Mordred asks for a covenant for his dead
The ridge must decide whether memory belongs to the crown, the oathless, or the witnesses, forcing Merlin and Percival to confront the difference between keeping the dead and owning them.

encounters.title: The settlement must decide how to admit refugees, debts, and claims without turn

text_script.value: On the fourth morning the new settlement passed its first test: a handcart came up from the salt marshes carrying widows, a limping smith, a boy with a frayed boot, and three families from Mordred's old holdings who wanted to be counted without being crowned. Percival set bread on the common trough and said, 'We can shelter you if you bring one task, not one claim.' Guinevere answered, 'Then let the claim be measured in who feeds whom,' while Gawain warned that a rule written on a cloth could still become a new throne. Merlin cupped the shard-road and heard it draw tight, as if the land were leaning toward a single promise; the Lady of the Lake dipped her lamp and touched it to the threshold stone. Arthur stood back from the crossing, unable to say whether he was returning as king or as debtor, while Mordred stood closer, not surrendering his name but asking that it be kept as a risk to be held, not a crown to be inherited.
Percival gives shelter in exchange for one task
Each entering household receives bread, a room, and a named duty, so legitimacy becomes a chain of reciprocal work rather than a title.
Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake keep the shard-road lit
The road becomes a guided threshold where lanterns mark who may enter, who is refused, and who must return with help.
Mordred asks the ridge to carry his dead forward
The ridge must either keep the dead as a debt owed to neighbors or let memory become a banner, deciding whether remembrance can end a kingdom without starting another.

encounters.title: The settlement must choose whether survival becomes repaired craft, a witnessed

text_script.value: Winter came down to the ridge as a series of small refusals: the miller's wheel seized, a child's splint cracked, and the shard-road threw no light past the second gate. Percival cut bread and tools into one line so that no one could say they were feeding a claim rather than a person, while Guinevere named the household that would tend the wounded at midwinter fires. Merlin asked the shard-road what it still meant if nobody was made king over it; Lancelot said, 'Less like a throne, more like a stair everyone has to step on,' and Mordred replied that a stair with no treads was only a rumor of rescue. Arthur watched the names move from the trough to the tools and did not step forward as ruler, only as the one who had to carry the first empty ledger.
Bedivere restores the toll-road as shared work
The ridge spends the winter making the shard-road passable, so outside loyalists return to repair rather than rule, while the shrine-road becomes harder for any claimant to claim as wholly his own.
Guinevere and Percival keep the gifts public
The settlement gains visible legitimacy as bread, timber, midwifery, and labor are counted in the open, forcing Arthur and Mordred to answer for promises in front of witnesses.
Merlin and the Lady of the Lake seal a witness covenant
The road can be entered only by those who swear to carry the settlement forward, uniting the ridge under oath but concentrating real power in the hands of witnesses.

encounters.title: The new settlement must decide whether legitimacy comes from an open commons, a

text_script.value: In the thaw, the ridge stopped being a refuge and began being a village: the miller's wheel turned again, the wounded lined the hearthstones, and the ledger kept by Bedivere showed more debts than crowns. Percival asked the assembled lords to choose between three names for what they were building: commons, road, or grave-field. Arthur said, 'I will not come back as a judge wearing a king's coat,' while Mordred answered, standing with his dead behind his shoulder, 'Then do not crown us. Wake us.' Merlin touched the shard-road with a blunt thumb and heard not a coronation chant but a slow rhythm of hammer, grain, and water; the Lady of the Lake smiled and asked what would be given to the ones who could not come back.
Percival and Guinevere make the ridge an open commons
Tenure, shelter, and labor become reciprocal tasks answered in front of neighbors, weakening titles but forcing Arthur and Mordred to answer as residents rather than claimants.
Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake make the road a witnessed threshold
Outsiders can enter and repair the ridge, but only by carrying witnesses and oaths, concentrating real power in the hands of those who guard the passage.
Arthur and Mordred settle what returning means
The succession is forced into the open: one may return as a debtor, another remain as a neighbor, and the settlement gains a hard choice rather than a vague promise of peace.

encounters.title: The new settlement must decide whether relics, road, and succession become commo

text_script.value: By the third thaw, the new settlement stopped being a refuge and became a working town: bakers, midwives, masons and exiles argued over a ledger of debts while the relic-bells slept in a common chest instead of a king's hand. Arthur said, 'I would not be first in line or first in excuses.' Mordred answered, 'Then line up behind the bells and ask what they are for.' Merlin heard the settlement road answer as a braid of water, bread, and oath; Morgan muttered that old magic kept a guest-list and forgot to return guests; Lancelot admitted he was still torn between the road that fed people and the duty that judged them, and Percival told the whole room that nobody could claim the settlement unless they helped carry its burdens.
Percival and Morgan open the relics to all hands
The settlement loses its most sacred objects as private treasures, but every household gains a visible duty, and Arthur and Mordred must answer as stewards rather than owners.
Bedivere and Gawain open the road to exiles
The ridge grows into a defended commons of refugees and artisans, making legitimacy visible but forcing the settlement to care for people it cannot fully govern.
Arthur and Mordred divide the return
The two claimants trade a future of kings for a public compact: one keeps the shrine, one rebuilds the road, and neither may rule without admitting what the other carries.

encounters.title: The settlement must decide how to honor the dead and missing, whether the ledger

text_script.value: In the cold month after the bells came down from the shrine, the settlement woke to a broken axle and a question no one had planned for: what to do with the debts of people who would never come back. Percival set the common ledger on the long table and read the names aloud, and Bedivere, who had copied it by lamplight, admitted he could not tell which of the debts were owed and which were owed only to the dead. Lancelot, who had carried the chest of relics up the ridge himself, warned that an open ledger would become a chain of accusation; Morgan answered that chains were also what held a settlement together, and Merlin touched the shrine-stone and heard the settlement answering not as a kingdom but as a field of small, stubborn lights. Mordred, who had not spoken in days, asked what the settlement would owe the next people who left it — and what the ones who stayed would owe the ones who did not.
Bedivere opens the ledger to every household
Debts and names become visible to neighbors, forging a covenant of mutual responsibility but forcing some households to refuse to be written, and leaving the settlement exposed to its own secrets.
Percival and Gawain send young finders down the shard-road
The settlement risks its young people on the road to find the missing and the exiled, testing whether it values its own survivors enough to spend them, and bringing back either news or loss.
Merlin and Morgan settle the old magic into sleep or stewardship

The settlement gains a working answer to the question of the shrine's power: either the magic rests beneath the stone as a shared trust, or it wakes as a guest the settlement must either welcome or refuse.

encounters.title: The settlement must now decide whether the road, the ledger, and the old magic b

text_script.value: After the young finders came back with the axle straight and two names, the settlement no longer asked whether the road was open but what it was open to. Percival argued that an open road must carry whoever it carried, even the ones the ledger had marked as strangers; Mordred answered that no settlement could feed and govern everyone and so had to decide what its welcome could bear. Arthur said peace was not preserving Camelot as it had been but making enough honest places to stand beside it, while Lancelot admitted that his loyalty was a wound that could either bind the road together or keep tearing it, and Morgan warned that the old magic kept a guest-list and often forgot to return the guests. Merlin left the shrine-stone silent for one full day so the town could choose whether the magic was a lamp to be carried, a door to be barred, or a burden to be answered by everyone who lived in the town.
Gawain and Bedivere open the ridge road as a common gate
Refugees gain a visible welcome and a defended path, but the settlement must feed, guard, and answer for people it cannot fully control.
Percival and Guinevere make the ledger a public witness
Debts, missing names, and care become shared obligations rather than private punishments, but households that fear exposure may refuse to stand under the covenant.
Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake place the old magic under rotating stewardship
The shrine-stone becomes a shared instrument that can protect the settlement or be refused, forcing every steward to answer publicly for its use.

encounters.title: The settlement must decide whether the unwritten households can shelter as witne

text_script.value: On the fourth morning of the open gate, the households the ledger had refused did not come to the common fire; they set their lamps along the ridge path and waited to learn whether the town would read them into the covenant or leave them as objects of charity. Percival said the ledger was not a list of debts but a lamp the settlement held in front of its own face, while Guinevere answered that a lamp can only shine on what is willing to be seen, and Morgan asked whether the stone would still light a room for those the town refused to name. Lancelot walked the line of lamps and asked whether love, if it was to be a law, could remain loyal to both the road and the home, and Mordred said the dangerous question was whether an unwritten person could still be a citizen or only a wound the town carried.
Percival and Guinevere grant witness-lamps to the unwritten
Unwritten households may light their own covenant lamps without being read aloud, forcing the town to value shelter and presence over control while making refusal visible and testable.
Gawain and Bedivere send two finders back onto the shard-road
The settlement risks young people on the road to find the missing and the exiled, testing whether it values its survivors enough to spend them and bringing back either news or loss.
Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake make stewardship public and annual
The shrine-stone becomes an accountable instrument that can protect the settlement or be refused, forcing every steward to answer publicly for its use.

encounters.title: The settlement must decide whether the returned road, the unwritten households,

text_script.value: On the fifth morning after the open gate, the shard-road returned one rider and half of a second: Gawain's horse stood unshod beneath the ridge while the young finder answered only that the bridge was no longer a bridge. Percival kept the ledger open to the households who had refused to be read aloud, Guinevere asked who could answer for them when they came home, and Merlin touched the shrine-stone until it spoke in a voice like many ordinary voices. Morgan warned that a stone which answers quickly is not the same as a stone that remains honest, and Lancelot stood between the road and the home with both hands open.
Percival and Guinevere read the returned finders into the covenant as witnesses
The missing become named again, but households that fear exposure may refuse the lamp, forcing the town to choose between belonging and being owned.
Gawain and Bedivere keep the ridge open while Lancelot repairs the first homes
The town gains both a defended path and a living neighborhood, but the same people who keep the road will carry the cost when the road fails them.
Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake put the speaking stone under rotating public trust
The shrine-stone can protect, refuse, or remember, yet every steward must answer publicly for what the stone makes the town do.

encounters.title: The settlement must choose whether its renewal is anchored by refuge-housing, by

text_script.value: On the sixth morning after the road failed, the settlement gathered around a fenced platform where the first house was to rise. Percival laid beams, nails, wheat, and repair tools as though care could be measured in timber, while Bedivere set the ledger open beside the tools and said that craft was not a service beneath law but a stubborn kind of witness. Mordred stood under the shrine-stone and asked whether a ruined court could still make one claim, and Arthur answered that it could only make one if every person who remained chose to be counted. Lancelot, Guinevere, Gawain, Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake heard the bargain change in the same breath: the old throne was finished, but a new public life had to learn to stand without it.
Percival and Bedivere raise the refuge-hall before anything else
The settlement becomes shelter first and identity second, forcing unwritten households to accept aid or refuse the covenant openly.
Gawain, Lancelot, and Arthur make the road an oath-duty
The town binds its future to travel and rescue, risking young helpers on the road while making survival visibly public.
Merlin, Morgan, Guinevere, and the Lady of the Lake divide the shrine-stone into rotating offices
Old magic becomes a public instrument with separate seats for memory, warning, and refusal, but every steward can be checked, blocked, or replaced.

encounters.title: The settlement must choose between refuge-housing that risks ownership, road dut

text_script.value: On the eighth morning after the failed bridge, the refuge-hall had two walls and a roof that had not been set, the ridge path carried a lantern every seven paces, and the shrine-stone stood with three seats around it instead of one. Percival counted nails and found six households that had returned with nothing to say why they had waited. Lancelot drove a hinge for the doorway while Gawain asked whether a refuge could ask its tenants to carry its shame. Morgan claimed the stone was speaking in two accents, one warm and one dry; Merlin answered that a stone with no fixed duty was a bell with no owner. Guinevere asked Mordred whether he would make a claim only to be checked, Arthur said yes if checked, and Mordred answered that a claim judged only by rank would not deserve his name. The Lady of the Lake watched the road and said that a new town survives only if it tells the truth about what it still refuses.
Percival and Guinevere put unwritten households before a public lamp
Households that come forward become visible and owed aid, while those who refuse can be marked as absent, forcing the town to choose between shelter and ownership.
Gawain and Lancelot muster the ridge under a visible road-oath
The settlement proves its survival through travel and rescue, but the ridge duty draws young helpers away from shelter and makes the road a public threat rather than a private risk.
Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake set the stone under three rotating offices
The stone can protect, remember, or refuse, yet every steward must publish what it makes the town do and can be checked, blocked, or replaced.

encounters.title: The settlement must choose whether to admit unwritten households under the lamp,

text_script.value: On the ninth morning the new settlement had one roof, one lamp, and a ledger that would not close. Percival cut notches into the first beam while Bedivere wrote down not only grain and nails but the names of those who had arrived with nothing; Guinevere asked what would happen to a person who refused to be counted, and Arthur said that refusal would be lawful only if it remained visible. Lancelot and Gawain disputed whether the ridge road or the hall should carry the settlement through the night, while Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake stood around the shrine-stone and asked who would answer if it changed its mind. Mordred waited for a throne that no longer existed and instead heard his own claim narrowed into a question: could the ruined court become a place that admitted failure without pretending failure was courage.
Percival and Guinevere open the hall to households willing to be counted
The refuge-hall gains visible covenant and food-sharing, but refusal becomes a public marker of shame rather than a private choice.
Gawain and Lancelot send oath-helpers to clear the ridge and bridge
The town proves survival through travel and repair, yet young helpers and inexperienced lords are pulled onto a dangerous road while shelter remains unfinished.
Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake demand a public audit of the stone-seats
The shrine-stone becomes an accountable office that can protect, remember, or refuse, but every steward must answer before witnesses or be replaced.

encounters.title: The settlement must choose how to handle a missing courier and a divided stone:

text_script.value: On the tenth morning the refuge counted bread again and found the road had taken its own toll: one courier from the counted households had not returned, and the shrine-stone had kept two small pulses instead of one steady heart. Percival wrote the missing name beside the food ledger while Guinevere said a shelter could not become a gate that watched who was worthy of it. Gawain wanted to walk out with Lancelot to find what had happened, Lancelot wanted the settlement to send no one still in love with safety, and Merlin said the stone was not deciding between kindness and law but asking which of them would survive the question. Mordred asked whether exile could carry a name if it were not turned into a throne, and the Lady of the Lake answered that a new people could not claim survival until it told the road what it refused to become.
Percival and Guinevere make countable households a covenant of the hall
The shelter gains a visible covenant and food-sharing, but households that refuse to be counted remain marked as absent and may be excluded without being destroyed.
Gawain and Lancelot send Arthur and guards to find the missing courier and bridge truth
The town gains evidence and protection from the road, while Arthur, Gawain, Lancelot, and young helpers are pulled toward a dangerous rescue and the refuge may be left to decide without them.
Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake force the shrine-stone into protect, remember, or refuse
The shrine-stone becomes an accountable sacred office that can shelter, record, or refuse the settlement, but every steward must publish the duty before witnesses and be checked or replaced.

encounters.title: The settlement must decide whether to publish an open covenant, send guarded oat

text_script.value: On the eleventh morning the refuge found its law had already changed shape. Percival held the ledger open under one lamp while Bedivere chalked the unreturned name beside the grain count, but a young herdsman arrived with a wet cloak and a torn ribbon, saying the road held two kinds of light: thin white mist where the bridge had been, and a gold thread where the shrine-stone answered. Arthur refused to let the settlement pretend the missing courier was only lost, while Mordred listened and asked whether a ruined court could still say no without becoming a cage; Guinevere widened the threshold and said refusal had to be visible, not punished. Merlin and Morgan argued over the stone's divided pulse, and the Lady of the Lake answered that Camelot had become a smaller republic with older debts, surviving only by deciding who it was willing to outlive.
Percival, Bedivere, and Guinevere publish an open covenant
Households receive visible shelter and food, while refusal remains spoken and unpunished but no longer invisible or private.
Gawain, Lancelot, and Arthur lead oath-helpers to the ridge and bridge
The settlement gains hard evidence about danger and survival, but its people are pulled toward a risky rescue and the hall stands with fewer keepers.
Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake force the stone into a witnessed office
The shrine-stone can shelter, record, or refuse, but every steward must answer before witnesses or be replaced.

encounters.title: The refuge has two returning households, one absent, a twice-pulsing shrine-ston

text_script.value: At the ninth dusk the ledger no longer had one clean line for the road: two households came back with salt in their hem, one stayed missing, and the small black shrine-stone answered twice instead of once. Percival closed the door against easy mercy and opened it to named duties, while Guinevere answered that mercy had to say where it stopped. Merlin could not steady the double pulse; Morgan called the council to stop asking whether old magic could keep a new town alive; the Lady of the Lake said Camelot would endure only as long as it could name the difference between rescue and rule. Arthur asked what the absent courier had seen, Mordred countered that a name without a throne was only a song, and Gawain and Lancelot gave the same warning from different sides: the ridge was not a map, it was a debt.
Arthur, Gawain, Lancelot, and chosen keepers test the ridge for the missing courier
The settlement gains hard road truth but loses its keepers, and the hall must decide whether rescue or shelter should come first.
Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake force the shrine-stone into protect, remember, or refuse
The stone becomes accountable sacred office that can shelter, record, or refuse, but every steward must answer before witnesses or be replaced.
Percival and Guinevere rewrite the covenant around named households and named refusals
Belonging becomes visible and shared, while refusal is spoken openly and may be excluded from labor without being destroyed.

encounters.title: The refuge now has two returned households, one blank name, a twice-pulsing shri

text_script.value: On the twelfth dusk the covenant was no longer a wall around the living but a door held open by hands that had not yet trusted each other. Percival set the ledger beside a candle that kept trying to burn backward, while Bedivere cut two names from the labor roll and left the third blank; Morgan said a stone that answers twice is not a secret but a warning, and warnings need a body to carry them. Arthur set his boot on the missing courier's trail-stone, Gawain asked who would refuse a call without being punished, and Guinevere answered that the refuge would keep only promises it could say aloud, while Lancelot said he could still carry a burden but would not carry it alone.
Percival, Bedivere, and Guinevere open the covenant as a public door
More households stay and labor is shared openly, while refusal remains spoken and visible but can still be left out of the work.
Arthur, Gawain, Lancelot, and chosen keepers carry testimony to the ridge
The settlement gains hard road truth and a path for the missing courier, but it loses hands at its hearth and must decide whether rescue or shelter comes first.
Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake force the shrine-stone into witnessed office
The stone can shelter, record, or refuse with testimony behind it, but every steward must answer before witnesses or be replaced.

encounters.title: The new settlement has two repaired households, one blank refusal still unspoken

text_script.value: On the fourth winter evening the refuge looked less like a camp than a patient workshop, with mud, grain, timber, and loom-wood laid out before the twice-pulsing stone. Percival asked each named household to say one thing it could repair and one thing it could not yet forgive, while Bedivere repainted the labor roll so refusal could be spoken without becoming a stain. Gawain and Lancelot argued over whether the missing courier should be chased or left to become a warning; Arthur said a settlement must first prove it can feed the next dawn, while Morgan called for the old shrine-stone to be made answerable to ordinary ears.
Percival, Bedivere, and Guinevere turn the blank roll into a craft compact
Water, grain, shelter, and shrine-repair are assigned to named households, so the settlement gains survival without forcing every refusal to become labor.
Arthur, Gawain, Lancelot, and chosen keepers carry testimony to the ridge
The refuge learns whether the missing courier is lost, trapped, or fleeing, but its hearths thin and survival is set against rescue.
Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake make the shrine-stone an open public ledger
The twice-pulsing stone records shelter, memory, and refusal for witnesses, yet every steward must stand answerable or step aside.

encounters.title: The commons has repaired households, one public blank to cross out, a disputed r

text_script.value: On the ninth morning of the commons, the thaw had made the ridge muddy and the repaired ledger still smelled of wax and smoke. Percival read the one household that had forgiven itself and the one that kept its refusal folded, while Bedivere inked the blank name with a line that could be crossed out only before witnesses. Arthur said the settlement would be judged by the breakfast it fed, Gawain answered that an oath to the ridge could not be paid at a table, and Guinevere asked what a household owed when forgiveness was made visible as labour. Lancelot carried the waterskin to the doorway as though refusing to choose between the hearth and the road, Merlin called the twice-pulsing shrine-stone a quarrel dressed as a relic, Morgan asked who would answer for the stone if it kept its own counsel, and the Lady of the Lake said the price of leaving it unowned was that no one would ever have to say alone.
Percival and Bedivere make the blank name crossable before witnesses
The settlement strengthens its hearth and survival compact, but refusal becomes public labour and some households may refuse to be written into the work.
Arthur, Gawain, Lancelot, and chosen keepers carry testimony to the ridge
The refuge may recover the missing courier or learn the ridge truth, but the hearths thin and rescue is set against survival.
Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake bind the stone as a witnessed office
The shrine can shelter, record, or refuse with testimony behind it, but every steward must answer before witnesses or step aside.

encounters.title: Camelot is ruined and abandoned, but a named, witnessed settlement stands on the

text_script.value:
On the first morning of the new age, the ruined court stood grey and quiet while Percival, Bedivere, and the lords who had stayed laid out the settlement's first road: water, grain, shrine-stone, and a roll of names. Arthur set the crown down in the ash of a fallen dais and said, 'The seat is gone; the table is not,' while Merlin warned that forgetting Camelot would be easier than healing it. Morgan lit the hearth-fire and asked who would keep it after the knights grew old, Guinevere answered that the hearth belonged to whoever fed it, and Mordred stood last to speak, claiming not the throne but the name of the house, which Gawain received as a small, uneasy mercy. The Lady of the Lake held the twice-pulsing stone and found it, at last, faint and steady, and Lancelot set his waterskin down beside the road as though he had decided where he lived.

The seat fell, but the idea of justice did not. Camelot burned down to a grey horizon and a ruined dais, yet on the ridge a smaller commons stood: a road, a hearth, a stone that pulsed gently, a roll of names crossed and re-crossed before witnesses. Arthur gave up the crown and found the kingdom he had actually meant - a table that fed ordinary people, an oath sworn to households rather than banners. Lancelot, divided, laid his waterskin by the road and chose a place to live. Morgan kept the fire and asked the hard question, who would answer when the knights grew old, and Guinevere answered that the hearth belonged to whoever fed it. Merlin and the Lady of the Lake made the stone an office, not a prize; Gawain and Mordred spoke carefully, claiming names rather than thrones; Percival and Bedivere hammered the compact of survival into the morning. It was bittersweet - Camelot was gone, exiles carried the wound - but the settlement was real, humble, and growing. The old order broke, and a different kingdom was born from ruin: not a doomed ideal restored, but a living commons of craft, memory, and duty, open to whatever comes after.

encounters.title: With offices failing, Camelot gathers at the empty-centered Round Table, where A

text_script.value: The shrine bells were gone and the heir was unsworn, so Arthur brought everyone to the Round Table and left the seat at its center deliberately empty. "If the crown is a lie," he said, "then let the table be the truth." Lancelot turned the empty cup toward the wall and said that love had never sworn allegiance to offices, only to people, while Gawain answered that oaths were the last rope over the edge. Percival set a small loaf and two cups on the table's edge, and Morgan, who had come only to mock, began naming the names of those the court had failed - the exiles, the widows, the ones who had walked away - until Arthur understood that the council was not being ended but being carried.
Arthur speaks the witnessing rite at the empty seat
The court names the failed offices aloud and vows to remember them, turning Camelot into a memorial fellowship rather than a living throne.
Guinevere calls the commoners to one table
The Round Table spills outward to exiles and servants, making fellowship communal and vulnerable to the realm's fragmentation.
Lancelot and Gawain share the final oath at the table's edge
The two rivals bind themselves to one another publicly, forcing Mordred and Morgan to choose between joining the vow or breaking it.

encounters.title: With the empty seat held fast, the fellowship at Camelot is now weighing whether

text_script.value: Bedivere set the Cup at the edge of the empty seat, not on it, and stepped back as if it were a door he had just opened. Morgan, who had come to mock, now spoke the names in a low and even voice - widows, exiles, a boy who had never received his sword - and Gawain answered that a list was not a life, though it might be a map of where lives had been. Lancelot, who had righted the cup he had turned toward the wall, said that the table had only ever meant one thing: whoever sat at it was held to love whoever sat beside him. Mordred, waiting in the doorway with his own claim in hand, asked whether a table that fed people but never crowned a king was a kingdom or a witness.
The court recites the failed names until the list is complete
The fellowship becomes a liturgy of memory, each named life a debt the Round Table owes the world, and the failure of Camelot is fixed in words that outlive the offices.
Guinevere brings the exiles and servants in to the table
Fellowship becomes physical and communal as Camelot is opened to the realm's edge, but the court's protection and its law-bound order are left exposed to fragmentation.
Arthur answers Mordred's question at the table's edge
The court must state aloud whether fellowship without kingship is a kingdom, forcing Mordred and Morgan to either join the vow or break it.

encounters.title: With the offices failed and the names recited, Camelot must now decide what fell

text_script.value: Morgan folded the names into a single tally-stick while Mordred stood where the road enters and said that a witness could be toppled by one angry heir. Lancelot answered that the table had never held a king, only the promise that no one would be left outside it, and Gawain picked up the cup as though it weighed less than bread. Percival read the first name aloud and looked up: if the fellowship was to survive, the court would have to choose now whether it was a chapel, a refuge, or a road.
Arthur seals the fellowship in a vow at the empty seat
The court binds itself to remain present for the named, even if the vow is later broken by the world around it.
Guinevere invites the exiles to sit with the court
The fellowship becomes public and dangerous, opening Camelot to both salvation and the loss of protection.
Merlin and Morgan keep the seat empty as a relic of refusal
The court refuses to remake the crown, forcing Mordred to answer whether his claim can stand without legitimacy.

encounters.title: The fellowship has sworn to the named but has not yet answered Mordred's charge:

text_script.value: Arthur spoke the vow aloud not to the crown but to the named, and Guinevere had already swept the court's feast-tables down for the widows and exiles who were coming through the gates at dawn. Lancelot, who had carried the cup once and set it down twice, laid his sword across the seat that Arthur would not fill, and Gawain answered that a sword on a seat was still a crown in miniature. Mordred stood at the threshold with the claim in his fist and asked what a table that fed people but crowned no one was worth, and Merlin, who had watched the old magic fray to thread, said it was worth everything the crown had promised it could not deliver.
Arthur names what the table will be beyond the crown
Fellowship is spoken as a covenant rather than a kingdom, forcing Mordred and Morgan to either join it aloud or break it.
Guinevere sends the Cup outward with the exiles
The Grail leaves the shrine to walk with the widows and the road, and Camelot becomes a waypoint rather than a seat of law.
Merlin and Morgan hold the empty seat in silence
The court refuses to fill the seat with a successor, forcing Mordred to either renounce his claim or become the first ward of the fellowship.

encounters.title: The fellowship has been spoken as a living promise, but Mordred's challenge, the

text_script.value: Dawn found the court already re-sorting its symbols: Bedivere had set lanterns along the threshold, and Guinevere's tables stood for the widows and exiles rather than for a coronation. Mordred came alone with his claim wrapped in cloth and asked whether the knights would forgive a king who tried to save the realm after the crown had stopped naming it. Lancelot lifted the cup from the empty seat and said the fellowship was no longer a crown, but a promise with a body, a road, and a wound to carry.
Arthur writes the fellowship covenant on the gate-stone
The court becomes a public compact named by the threshold, strong as oath but exposed to attack and to outsiders claiming entry.
Guinevere sends the Cup outward with the exiles
The Grail leaves Camelot as a portable witness and the fellowship becomes a road rather than a fixed shrine.
Gawain asks Mordred to stand and answer before the named
Mordred is forced either to join the fellowship under its terms or to be named as the first outsider opposed to it.

encounters.title: Mordred has spoken his charge and been named aloud; the exiles are at the thresh

text_script.value: Mordred did not flee when the exiles' torches crested the ridge; he stood with his wrapped claim against his ribs and answered the court aloud: that a crown, in his view, had stopped naming what it protected, and that naming was the only office left. Arthur heard it, set down his pen, and said that the table had never promised to make anyone safe, only to remember who was not. Guinevere turned to the gates and said the work was not to crown but to walk, and Lancelot lifted the cup and looked at the road as at a promise already half-kept. Merlin, watching the old magic fray to thread, murmured that the thread was not stronger for being unseen.
Arthur binds the covenant aloud and lets Mordred speak under it
The covenant becomes a spoken compact before the exiles; Mordred either joins it aloud or stands as the one named outsider against it.
Guinevere sends the Cup out with the first of the named
The Grail leaves the shrine to walk with the exiles and the fellowship becomes a road with a witness rather than a seat of law.
Merlin and Morgan test the thread that binds the table
The old magic answers or fails, and the court learns whether the fellowship can outlast the crown without its charter.

encounters.title: The covenant is spoken aloud but not yet sealed; Mordred remains named outside t

text_script.value: At the grey edge of the gate, Mordred unwound his wrapped claim and laid it on the lantern-light like a deed that had failed to name a realm. "If the table is a road," he said, "then let me ride it as a burden, not as a king." Gawain answered that the table was no burden-bearer, only a pact to make the burden visible; Lancelot lifted the cup and said the witness was heavy, not the road. Arthur spoke slowly: the covenant would be written not as a victory, but as an invitation to enter, carry, and be carried; beyond the threshold, the exiles stood with their children's breath held in the cold, waiting to learn whether Camelot would still answer them.
Guinevere sends the Cup with the first exiles
The fellowship leaves the shrine and becomes a road with a witness, risking loss of the Grail if the road fails.
Arthur opens a hearing for Mordred before the named
Mordred gains a public place to speak, which may either join him to the fellowship or fix him as its first unwilling outsider.
Merlin and Morgan bind the oath to memory rather than magic
The old thread is softened into a lamp of remembrance, freeing the table from reliance on charter magic.

encounters.title: Mordred has been heard aloud at the table's edge; the thread bends but holds; th

text_script.value: Mordred laid the wrapped claim down between Arthur and the exiles and said plainly that the crown had never fed anyone, only named who was worthy of being carried. Arthur did not answer with judgment but with a question â€” who would carry him when the table could no longer â€” and the court felt the answer move through it like light through a lens. Merlin drew the old thread taut between two fingers and held it to the lantern; it bent, wavered, and did not break, and Guinevere, watching the gates beyond the shrine, said that Camelot would not end with victory but with witnesses.
Guinevere lifts the Cup and the fellowship steps through the gates
The fellowship leaves the shrine and becomes a journey, carrying the Grail where law has already failed and risking its loss if the road fails.
Arthur gathers the named at the empty seats and speaks the covenant as elegy
The table ends as mourning and memory rather than victory, and the exiles are witnessed rather than granted a kingdom.
Merlin and Morgan set the thread aside and bind the oath to names and shared bread
The charter of old magic is released and the fellowship rests on spoken names, memory, and care instead of enchantment.

encounters.title: The covenant is spoken but unsealed; the Cup, thread, exiles, and Mordred's wrap

text_script.value: Arthur set the Cup on the bare table and did not lift it, because a crown could be carried away while a name could not. Lancelot said, 'If love divides the road, then divide the carrying,' and Percival answered that the Grail had never asked who was pure but who was willing to be answerable. At the gates the exiles stood in a thin line, and Morgan touched the thread with two fingers: it did not glow, only remembered. Mordred listened with his wrapped claim still in his hand, and the court understood that the next word would decide whether Camelot would become a promise, a tomb, or a road.
Arthur speaks the covenant as memorial, not kingship
The named gather to witness and mourn the table, narrowing succession to a vow of care rather than a title.
Guinevere and Lancelot carry the thread-lamp to the gates
The fellowship leaves the shrine and meets the exiles directly, risking the Grail if the road cannot hold them.
Mordred is offered the place of bearer rather than king
Mordred either accepts a named burden within the fellowship or refuses it, fixing the table as either open or unwilling.

encounters.title: The court has answered what Camelot will hold; the Cup, thread-lamp, wrapped cla

text_script.value: Arthur set the wrapped crown aside and asked each named soul to answer one question aloud: what will hold Camelot when the title no longer does. Lancelot took up the thread-lamp and let its light lean toward the gates while Guinevere laid the Cup at the threshold rather than on the table. Percival answered that the Grail was not a relic but a debt owed to the unseen, and the exiles beyond the gates answered in their turn, one name at a time. Mordred, still clutching his wrapped claim, said that a name carried by love outlives a king who merely wears one.
Lancelot and Guinevere carry the thread-lamp through the gates to the exiles
The fellowship leaves the shrine and meets the exiles face to face, risking the Grail if the road beyond the gates cannot hold them.
Arthur speaks the covenant as commemoration among the empty seats
The table becomes a mourning and witness rather than a kingship, and the exiles are seen but not granted a kingdom.
Arthur asks Mordred whether he will bear the claim and the road
Mordred either accepts a named burden inside the fellowship or refuses it, fixing the table as open or unwilling.

encounters.title: The court has heard the exiles' silence and the thread's memory; the lamp, the C

text_script.value: In the hour before the threshold closes, Morgan set her palm against the thread-lamp and said it was not a relic but a road that remembered its own footsteps; Merlin shook his head and answered that roads end when the ones carrying them forget why. Gawain walked the length of the bare table and placed one hand upon each empty seat, naming the absent aloud, while Bedivere, who had tended the shrine for thirty years, said quietly that the widows outside the gates had not yet been told the court had voted to stand still. Mordred remained at the far end with his wrapped claim in his hand, and for the first time looked not at the crown but at the lamp.
Guinevere and Lancelot take the thread-lamp through the gates to name the exiles
The fellowship leaves the shrine and answers the exiles' names directly, turning Camelot from a memorial into a moving road, at the risk that the lamp fails beyond the threshold.
Arthur asks Mordred to bind the wrapped claim to the road
Mordred either accepts a named burden inside the fellowship and gives the table an open, costly continuation, or refuses and fixes the table as a closed, elegiac shrine.
Arthur leaves the Cup unlit and lets the court swear its vows by ordinary word
The covenant is sealed as a spoken fellowship rather than a relic, keeping the Grail unlit and vulnerable but free of every claim.

encounters.title: The court has named what each will carry; the lamp, the Cup, the claim, and the

text_script.value: Arthur set the crown's wrap aside and did not call it a crown but a debt, then asked each of them aloud: what will you carry out of Camelot when there is no longer a table to carry it on. Merlin answered that magic was a lamp that burned whether or not anyone needed it, and warned that roads died when their keepers forgot why. Lancelot was quiet too long, then said the table had never held him the way the road had, and that this was the one thing he could not pretend to fix. Mordred stood at the far end and said, without heat, that he would carry the wrapped claim until it broke or he did, and that neither outcome was nothing. Guinevere asked Percival what the exiles beyond the gates had asked for, and he answered simply: a word, and someone to be named.
Guinevere and Percival carry the lamp and the word to the exiles
The fellowship moves beyond the threshold into the exiles' country, joining the table to the road but risking the lamp and the Grail against the road's own limits.
Arthur asks Mordred to bind the claim to the road in person
Mordred either takes the burden and joins the fellowship openly, giving the table a costly, living continuation, or refuses and seals the table as a closed elegiac shrine.
Arthur speaks the covenant over the empty seats and leaves the Cup unlit
The covenant is sealed as ordinary word and witness rather than relic, keeping the Grail free of every claim but with no relic left to anchor the fellowship.
