encounters.title: Arthur is effectively gone; Camelot remains divided among preserving his absence

text_script.value:
At the final bell Arthur did not rise, fall, or die dramatically; he thinned like a seal pressed into fog until the court could no longer feel his weight behind the throne. Guinevere asked what they were keeping, and Merlin answered that the oath had survived its king, while Mordred answered that the oath was useless until it fed someone. Lancelot set the seal on the threshold: 'A claim that cannot shelter the living is a costume for a ghost.' Lady of the Lake answered, 'Then let the ghost go where the need goes,' and the Round Table split into those who would remember Arthur, those who would replace him, and those who would carry the emptiness outward as a doorway.

Arthur is gone not as a corpse but as a condition: a ring of absent weight that no throne can fully hold and no successor can simply take back. Camelot divides into inheritance and reinvention, between those who keep the ghost as an oath, those who rebuild his absence as an order, and those who send the seal outward to meet need. The court survives unevenly: widows still ask for bread, laws still harden or soften, and the seal no longer proves who is king but forces everyone to decide what a king was for. In the end Camelot is not restored to Arthur, nor cleanly replaced by him; it becomes a haunting kingdom of choices, where the ghost of Arthur is not a title but a test that every heir must answer by feeding the living, refusing office, or opening the door.

encounters.title: The Grail remains an unreadable lamp over a split shrine while Arthur, Mordred,

text_script.value: Under a moon split in two, Percival held the lamp low while Bedivere re-read the same scrap of parchment until the word 'grail' became three different roads. Morgan leaned close and said the misreading was not an accident but a covenant test: whoever read the cup first would have to say whether it asked to be kept, followed, or lost. Merlin answered that silence was already a ruling, and Lancelot, unwilling to be the one who named it, turned his face from the lamp toward the road. Arthur asked the court to speak only what the exiles could hear, and Mordred answered with the first clear sentence of the night: the seal would not be forged, only misunderstood honestly.
Percival, Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake carry the lamp outward unnamed
The court follows a road that refuses to explain itself, so the shrine stays open as a question and succession is postponed beyond Camelot.
The court reads the evidence aloud before widows, exiles and rival claimants
The misreading is forced into public contest, making Arthur and Mordred negotiate under witness rather than crown the answer by force.
Arthur seals the shrine and postpones the oath to an exile-witnessed council
The Grail is not recovered, the table remains unresolved, and Camelot may endure as a guarded question rather than a trophy.

encounters.title: The Grail remains an unresolved lamp over a split shrine while Arthur, Mordred,

text_script.value: At the shrine's eastern edge, the lamp flickered into three shadows where the road had been, and no one stepped into any of them. Merlin said, 'A Grail is not a prize that answers when pointed; it is a question that moves when a court stops asking.' Lancelot turned to the exiles' banners and said, 'If I choose the road, I may become the last witness to a mercy; if I choose the seal, I may become its first liar.' Mordred answered quietly, 'Then the seal should not be offered as safety, only as an honest question about who is allowed to bear it.' Arthur made the court set down crowns, vows and hopes until each side named the ordinary person it feared losing.
Percival and Lady of the Lake walk the three shadowed roads alone at dawn
The court receives three partial answers instead of one crowned truth, forcing Arthur and Mordred to govern by sworn listening rather than by recovery.
Arthur reads the oath aloud to widows, exiles, heirs and claimants
Succession is no longer a private contest but a civic ceremony, with Lancelot and Mordred compelled to name what they would risk for those outside Camelot.
Merlin and Morgan attempt a covenant-test that does not name the Grail
The old magic presses harder on the court's conscience, revealing whether power can survive as vowed care or collapses into claim.

encounters.title: The court remains unresolved and exile-witnessed: the Grail stays a non-answer o

text_script.value: Dawn found the shrine unsealed but un-illumined, its cup-shaped shadow empty while the exiles waited beyond the threshold with their blankets and broken bells. Arthur asked each claimant to name the one person outside Camelot whose life the answer would protect or betray; Mordred named a widowed carter, Lancelot named the child who might never see a crown, and Guinevere said that love was useless unless it could be refused without killing the covenant. Merlin answered that naming the prize would make the shrine into a temple, while Morgan insisted magic could keep an empty seat warm but not fill it; Percival told the small true story of a lamp carried by a bride who refused to turn it toward the road. Bedivere read the scrap once more and heard it become three promises, not one proof, and Gawain demanded that the court speak in sentences the exiles could repeat.
Percival, Bedivere and Lady of the Lake carry an unnamed lamp outward by stages
Succession is postponed, but Camelot becomes a moving relay of witnesses and the road, not the shrine, sets the calendar.
Arthur stakes the oath to named protection for widows, exiles and heirs
The Round Table is not crowned but made answerable, forcing Lancelot and Mordred to defend the same small life publicly.
Morgan and Merlin hold the covenant test without recovering or naming the Grail
The old magic becomes a test of care rather than conquest, leaving Camelot open to ruin or just survival.

encounters.title: The oath has been spoken and witnessed but not sealed: Camelot is answerable to

text_script.value: The exiles answered the spoken oath not with applause but with a ledger: blankets counted, bells mended, a child carried past the shrine on a father's shoulders. Kay mocked the word 'succession' until Arthur asked who would actually answer for a widow's roof, and the laughter thinned. Lancelot admitted he could swear to the exiles and still break the oath to the road he loved, and Mordred answered that a king who cannot name what he would lose is not a ruler but a rumor. Merlin held the covenant-test open and felt the court's attention sharpen into three thin beams, while Morgan warned that any light chosen would shine longer on the one who held it; the lamp stayed empty, and the empty cup seemed to listen.
Gawain and Kay lead the witnesses beyond the threshold to count the exiles' needs
The Round Table leaves the shrine and becomes a traveling ward, with the Grail's absence carried rather than recovered.
Morgan and Merlin bind the oath to a non-naming light and let it fail or hold
The court's care is either proven and made durable or exposed as posturing, with the lamp deciding nothing but revealing the liars.
Arthur sets down the crown and asks each claimant to swear to the widows' roofs first
Succession is suspended in favor of a public covenant, and Camelot survives as an open experiment rather than a throne.

encounters.title: The court is split between public debt, magical refusal, and succession-as-quest

text_script.value: Beyond the shrine, Kay chalked the exiles' debts on a gate-stone while Gawain read them aloud; Lancelot asked why love should be a claim, Mordred answered that a promise unnamed was only a story, and Arthur said the covenant must answer before it could decide what it was. The Lady of the Lake came back carrying not a cup but a wet ribbon that the wind pulled toward the road, and Merlin warned that holding it would make the shrine a throne while Morgan said refusal must be tested, not romanticized. Guinevere said the real wound was not the empty cup but the fear of being answered by people who no longer owed the court anything, and Percival swore he would keep one small sentenceâ€”'come home, or do not lie to us'â€”until someone acted on it.
Kay posts the exiles' debts and Arthur must fund or answer them
The court gains real power over roofs and bells but loses the luxury of a sacred answer.
Merlin and Morgan ask the covenant to survive one failed act
The covenant either stands when it nearly breaks or is exposed as a performance.
Arthur returns the crown question each season instead of naming an heir
Succession becomes a recurring public practice, and the Round Table remains answerable rather than owned.

encounters.title: The covenant is public but unsealed: the exiles' needs are named, the light has

text_script.value: At the gate-stone the chalked debts were read in the order the exiles had chosen: roof, bell, child, oath. Lancelot put a hand over the empty cup and said a promise seen was no promise kept; Mordred answered that a crown which could not refuse was only a crowd with a banner. Merlin let the covenant light fail once and find the liars, while Morgan kept the ribbon taut and refused to call its tug the Grail. Guinevere walked the line of exiles and asked whether love, law, or the missing cup should be allowed to answer first.
Arthur and Gawain carry the debt-list into the exiles' hamlet
Camelot gains outside accountability and proof or refusal, but loses the aura of sacred permanence.
Merlin and Morgan hold the empty cup through one more failed act
The covenant either survives as practiced choice or collapses into exposed posturing.
Kay and Bedivere leave one chair unnamed and convene the Table only when someone acts
The Round Table becomes a recurring public experiment instead of a throne, temple, or crowned relic.

encounters.title: The covenant still half-fails, the exiles' debts remain public but unmet, the Gr

text_script.value: At the half-lit gate-stone, Bedivere laid the ribbon beside the chalked debts and asked the court to decide what an unanswered answer could become. Lancelot held Percival's sentence in his fist and said love felt like evidence when it refused to arrive; Merlin said silence was only a choice if someone kept listening; Morgan answered that listening was the cheapest magic in the world; Mordred countered that nobody had left the court to carry the question into rooms that might refuse it. Arthur looked at Gawain, Kay, and the Lady of the Lake, then told them the Round Table would keep one unnamed chair until someone acted rather than until someone admired.
Arthur and Gawain carry the debt-list into the exiles' hamlet
The court gains outside proof or refusal and weakens its aura of sacred permanence.
Kay and Bedivere let one unnamed chair receive a named obligation
The Round Table becomes a practical covenant for whoever can be sent, helped, or held accountable.
Merlin, Morgan, and the Lady of the Lake read the ribbon's tug instead of hunting the empty cup
The court chooses whether to pursue a trace, refuse it, or remain honestly unresolved.

encounters.title: The debt-list is spoken at the hamlet edge, the cup remains absent, the ribbon p

text_script.value: At the edge of the widows' road, Kay marked the empty chair with a threshold stone and asked each exile to name the debt they were willing to carry. Lancelot, carrying Percival's refusal like a small stone, found no cup waiting; only a ribbon snagged on a gatepost and pulling toward the dark after the chapel. Merlin's failed light turned the chalked words half-legible, while Morgan said the tug was not proof of the Grail but proof that something was being refused, and Mordred countered that a court which could not refuse would soon be only a procession of its own promises.
Let the hamlet set its own terms before help arrives
The court gains outside accountability and may be turned away, but the Grail trace stays unresolved.
Merlin, Morgan and the Lady of the Lake follow the ribbon's tug
The court risks a misread in pursuit of a trace rather than a trophy, shifting the Round Table from witness to probe.
Arthur, Gawain and Kay leave the chair unnamed and public
The Round Table becomes an ongoing experiment in refusal, keeping the Grail unresolved and the covenant fragile.

encounters.title: The debts are public at the hamlet gate, the cup remains absent, the ribbon pull

text_script.value: At the hamlet's edge the chalked debts dimmed under a lamp no one trusted, and the ribbon lay across the threshold like a hair pulled from a wound. Arthur said, 'Do not bring me a verdict; bring me the terms.' Gawain answered that the list was already a verdict written in other people's doors, and Kay copied the terms in the mud where refusal could be seen. Merlin traced the ribbon's tug and found it headed not for a cup but for a dark seam where the road changed its name; Morgan said a seam might mean escape or only a better place to hide, while Mordred asked whether a court that could be refused was still a court. Lancelot held Percival's refusal against his ribs, Guinevere kept the unnamed chair open by the gate, and the Lady of the Lake set her hand on the seam and felt it answer like an ear rather than a vessel.
Let the hamlet speak its terms before any help enters
The court gains outside accountability and may be turned away, but the Grail trace stays unresolved.
Merlin, Morgan and the Lady of the Lake enter the seam to read it
The court risks a misread toward a trace rather than a relic, shifting the Round Table from witness to probe.
Arthur, Gawain and Kay leave the chair unsealed at the gate
The Round Table remains an open question, forcing every later answer to declare what refusal costs.

encounters.title: The debt-list now names a second widow and an unexplained heel-track, the lanter

text_script.value: In the changed name of the road, the chalked debts left goose tracks in the mud and one pair of heels that belonged to no court. Arthur put his palm to the seam and felt it answer like a held breath; Gawain named the widow who had come back with bread, Kay wrote the price aloud instead of the password, and Lancelot, still holding Percival's refusal, said, 'If the Grail wants us, let it have the leaving as well as the coming.' Merlin lit a pale lantern that showed only mud and one darker notch; Morgan answered that a light unable to hold a path was still better than a path that only wanted to be followed; Mordred said the Round Table was not a chair but a claim, and a claim proved only once could not govern a border; the Lady of the Lake read the seam as an ear and heard a low syllable that might be stay, go, or give back, while Percival and Bedivere carried the empty cup past the threshold without setting it down.
Let the border decide who passes
The court accepts outside accountability and may be turned away, while the Grail trace stays unresolved and the covenant weakens or renews by public refusal.
Merlin, Morgan and the Lady of the Lake read the seam while the court guards the threshold
The court risks a misread toward a trace rather than a relic, shifting the Round Table from witness to probe with the border exposed.
Leave the empty chair at the threshold as a standing refusal test
The Round Table remains an open question, forcing every later answer to declare what refusal costs before the Grail can be returned or lost.

encounters.title: The empty chair now holds a live question rather than a trophy, the darker notch

text_script.value: By the second bell the threshold had become a negotiation: two widows stood outside the chalked line, the heel-track led past them toward the seam, and the empty chair rocked once as if consulted. Arthur set his sword across the seat and said, 'A chair is not a verdict. Put the question in it.' Guinevere answered that love had already been asked, and the answer had been late; Mordred replied that late answers were how borders learned to divide; Merlin held the lantern low and showed the mud, and the darker notch had grown longer, as if listening. Morgan said the seam was not swallowing the road but tuning it, and asked whether the Round Table could survive being asked questions it could not answer; Lancelot said he carried Percival's refusal the way a shield carries a wound, and that the wound was evidence; Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake carried the empty cup toward the seam, not to enter it but to leave a trace of refusal behind them.
Require the widows' terms aloud before anything enters or leaves
The court gains outside accountability and may be turned away, but the trace is made visible to those who live outside it.
Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake leave the empty cup at the threshold
The Round Table becomes a witness to refusal, and the seam responds to the absence of the relic rather than its presence.
Leave the chair empty and unsealed as a standing question
The Round Table stays an open question, and every later answer must state what refusal costs before the Grail can be returned or lost.

encounters.title: The widows' terms are now public, the empty cup is left at the threshold rather

text_script.value: At the chalked line the two widows named their terms before any cup or crown could be moved: bread, a public name, and the right to be counted outside as well as inside. Arthur asked what the Round Table owed before the Grail answered, and Guinevere said vows were for those outside the seam as much as for those who could still gather around it. Merlin lifted the lantern and the darker notch lengthened toward the threshold; Morgan called it a door that could not yet be trusted to open; Lancelot kept Percival's refusal visible and said a shield that cannot show its wound is only decoration; Mordred answered that an oath with no one outside it was a trophy, not a law. Kay wrote the terms and the unanswered notch on the same strip, Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake set the empty cup down at the border rather than within it, and Gawain held the chalk line open while the seam kept making its low, unreadable reply.
Enter the widows' terms into the Round Table's oath-list
Camelot gains a wider, public accountability, but the oath may become weaker as its rules now bind those who cannot receive the relic.
Keep the cup outside the seam and unreturned
The Grail trace remains unresolved while the border becomes a threshold of refusal rather than a shrine gate.
Ask the court to name one duty it will perform without the Grail
The Round Table moves from relic claim toward civic promise, forcing Arthur, Lancelot and Mordred to define loyalty beyond the cup.

encounters.title: The Round Table now holds a public, limited oath to bread, names, and non-exclus

text_script.value: Dawn brought the two widows and their knotted cord of promises to the chalked threshold while the notch waited at the center of the court like a small locked door. Arthur asked what the Round Table could keep when the Grail would not answer, and Guinevere answered that the first vow was already broken: to feed, name, and not abandon those standing outside the line. Merlin narrowed the dark seam with one thought, then chose to leave the gap open; Morgan said the old magic had learned to ask smaller, more local questions; Mordred insisted that any oath excluding the poor was already a trophy in disguise. Kay struck a false mark through the oath that promised return, Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake kept the empty cup low against the border, and Gawain read the widows' terms aloud until the room could hear them as law, not decoration.
Enter the widows' terms into the Round Table's oath-list
The court becomes answerable to those outside the seam, but some relic claims are weakened because the oath now binds those who cannot receive the Grail.
Make the threshold a civic gate for exiles and witnesses
The court must decide whether the seam is a danger to be sealed, a refuge to be opened, or a question to be governed.
Require Arthur, Lancelot, and Mordred to swear one non-relic duty each
Loyalty is redefined around the promise to keep the outside alive, forcing the heirs of the Round Table to choose between crown, love, and accountability.

encounters.title: The court has begun swearing terms outside the relic, but the notch still listen

text_script.value: At day's end, with the notch risen to shoulder height and the cup at the border answering in a voice no one could place, the court held its own small accounting. Mordred said an oath that bound only the inside was a cage wearing a throne, and Arthur answered that the cage would be built around those outside it. Lancelot set his hand on the threshold and said he would keep the door open, not the gate; Guinevere countered that love, like bread, was not a relic to be kept in a box; Merlin read the notch as listening rather than opening, while Morgan asked what the court would do if the Grail answered with a question instead of a gift. Gawain read the widows' names aloud, Kay wrote the day's terms on a strip of vellum, Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake kept the empty cup low against the border, and Percival stood at the edge of the light and would not step past it.
Seat the widows at the Round Table's edge
The outside becomes partially inside, forcing Arthur, Lancelot and Mordred to answer to those not yet trusted with the cup, and the court's claim is tested rather than confirmed.
Keep the seam sealed and witness it nightly
The border holds and the Grail question is deferred, but the Round Table remains untested and its claim to govern the outside weakens quietly.
Let Morgan and Percival try to hear the notch's question
Magic and faith are tested directly against the seam, the Grail stays unresolved, and the court's authority is challenged from within the notch itself.

encounters.title: The widows now occupy the threshold of the Round Table and the notch has begun a

text_script.value: On the third morning the widows sat on straw stools at the Round Table's edge and told the court what the notch had cost them, and the court had to answer in the open air rather than in the shrine. Mordred said that a throne that feasted only its owners was a graveyard built in advance, and Arthur, for the first time, put his hand flat on the table's rim and did not move it. Merlin held the seam open a finger's width and heard something answer that was not words and was not quite silence, and Morgan whispered that the old magic had begun to ask questions in the widows' own dialect. Lancelot stood nearest the border and admitted that he could not decide which of the two things he kept — the kingdom or the cup — he loved more, and Percival answered simply that love was the one thing that did not fit inside a law. Gawain read the widows' names aloud again, and Kay wrote them where everyone could see, while Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake set the empty cup between the court and the seam so that no one could mistake it for a treasure.
Let the widows draft the next clause of the law
The court becomes a rule-maker answerable to those it excludes, but the Grail question deepens as the notch tests the wording.
Leave the empty cup at the threshold unclaimed
The Round Table refuses to enshrine the Grail as a trophy, forcing Lancelot and Mordred to choose a different kind of loyalty.
Walk the seam line with the widows and the guard
The border is crossed into shared territory, testing whether Camelot can govern without retreating behind the notch.

encounters.title: The widows' clause is spoken into the seam, the notch answers with frost and sym

text_script.value: On the fourth evening, the widows did not ask to be admitted; they brought a single written clause and read it into the open air while Arthur, Lancelot and Mordred stood behind the table like a jury without a verdict. When Percival answered the seam with his own name, the notch answered not with words but with a rising line of frost that moved from the court toward the widows' doorway, and Morgan said the old magic had begun to feel sympathy. Lancelot put his hand over the cup but did not lift it; Guinevere traced the clause until the letters trembled, and Merlin kept one finger upon the notch so the court could hear it answer. Gawain, Kay, Bedivere and the Lady of the Lake kept the seam from swallowing the table's edge, and the Round Table remained open to the question of whether it could hold those outside as well as inside.
Seal the clause into the seam
The court is forced to accept the widows' terms as binding, while the notch deepens its answer and the Grail remains unresolved.
Set the cup beyond the Round Table's rim
The shrine is refused as a trophy, stripping Lancelot and Mordred of an easy claim and forcing a different oath to be chosen.
Let Morgan and Percival call the seam to answer once more
The border gives a partial, unstable answer to the succession question, making legitimacy, love and law collide openly.

encounters.title: The seam has forked with light-shapes of a cup, a key, and a name, forcing Camel

text_script.value: The frost line did not retreat; it forked toward the widows' threshold, and each branch carried a small shape — a cup, a key, a name — written in light rather than letters. Morgan leaned close and said the old magic was not asking whether the court should keep the Grail; it was asking what a Grail could be for a people who had no shrine. Arthur answered by walking to the rim and touching the empty cup with two fingers, the way one touches a sleeping child, and said that a cup is only a cup until someone chooses to be loyal to it. Lancelot, for the first time without evasion, said he would spend his life trying to find a shape for loyalty that did not end in a claim, and Mordred countered that Lancelot's shape might become a second throne. Gawain proposed that the court rule by witness rather than by object: each oath spoken aloud, witnessed by those it hurt, and the seam answered in kind. Kay wrote the proposals on a single leaf, and the Lady of the Lake carried the empty cup out beyond the border stones to see what it felt like to be seen by those outside.
Make every oath public before the hurt
The Round Table becomes a court of witnesses rather than relics, but the notch answers by showing that the hurt may outlast the oath.
Carry the cup back into the notch
The Grail is returned to the seam, forcing the court to argue about what is kept and what is given away.
Ask the seam what the key shape means
The border reveals a partial answer about access to the Round Table, splitting Arthur's peace from Mordred's claim.

encounters.title: The empty cup remains visible beyond the border while three unresolved claims -

text_script.value: At first grey light the cup stayed beyond the border stones, small and unlit, while the frost no longer moved in one line but forked toward three directions: the widows' door, the empty throne, and the guest-seat where Guinevere refused to sit. Lancelot said aloud that love could not be entered on a ledger, and Mordred answered that silence was also an inheritance. Arthur stood at the rim and asked the court to name the hurt it was asking the Round Table to carry; Morgan watched the frost and said the old magic would feel it before it could argue. Percival read the clause twice, Kay marked the pauses, Bedivere carried the empty bench out, and the Lady of the Lake kept the cup visible to those outside while refusing to let it be touched as a trophy.
Make each claimant speak before the hurt
The court trades ceremony for testimony, and the seam replies by showing that some harms cannot be answered by any seat.
Ask Merlin what the key shape admits
The border reveals access rather than succession, separating Arthur's peace from Mordred's claim without settling either.
Keep the cup outside and refuse it as an emblem
Camelot becomes a court of daily care and spoken oaths, but the Grail remains unseen and the throne stays an open question.

encounters.title: The court must choose what the Round Table refuses to become while the frost hol

text_script.value: At dawn the frost had thinned into three thin strands, and each strand carried one of the three unsettled claims: the widows' door still open to no one, the empty throne still empty, and Guinevere's guest-seat still waiting. Lancelot knelt beside the outer strand and admitted aloud that he did not yet know whether his life was a debt or a road, and Mordred said that a debt unpaid was a road that belonged to whoever found it first. Merlin reached toward the strand nearest the throne and found it cold, not empty, and Morgan answered that the old magic was not refusing the throne; it was refusing to be the only thing in it. Kay read aloud the two names no one had answered, Bedivere set the empty cup back on the border stone so it would be seen and not fought over, and Percival said plainly that the Grail meant nothing to him except that it had already been stolen once from those who needed it most. Arthur watched the three strands thin and thinner, and asked the court not to decide the Round Table but to decide what it would refuse to become.
Declare the throne a door, not a seat
Arthur stakes the court on access rather than succession, and the seam answers by hardening Mordred's claim into something harder to refuse.
Read the unanswered names aloud and speak to them
The Round Table becomes a hearing for the hurt, and the seam shows that hearing cannot heal everything but can keep the harm from being hidden.
Follow the strand toward the key and ask what it admits
Merlin and Morgan cross the border, splitting Arthur's peace from Mordred's claim but forcing the court to decide what is lost if the key is opened.

encounters.title: The frost line now runs from the Round Table to the empty cup beyond the border,

text_script.value: By dusk the three frost strands had braided into one pale line running past the border stones toward the empty cup, and every voice rose at once: Lancelot said he would walk it, Mordred answered that walking it was already a claim, and Guinevere asked whether the Grail could be refused without being lost. Arthur answered that refusal was its own form of custody, and Gawain asked whether the court could still be sworn to a thing it could not see; Kay said oaths were made for things not yet seen, and Morgan answered that they were also made for things that might never arrive. Percival stood beside the line and said that the widows' door was still open, that the court's answer to the border had already been given once by whoever chose to knock. Bedivere carried the empty cup toward the line and stopped at the frost; the Lady of the Lake stood at its edge and would not step past it, not because the cup was forbidden but because she would not carry anything as a trophy. Merlin watched the line and said that the old magic was not refusing the Round Table; it was refusing to be the only thing holding it up.
Walk the frost line together
The court splits between those who step across and those who keep the border, and the seam answers by showing that the Grail cannot be carried as a trophy.
Refuse the line and keep the door open
Camelot becomes a court of care rather than emblem, the Grail stays unseen, and the throne remains an unanswered question.
Speak the two unanswered names aloud
The court becomes a hearing for the hurt, and the seam answers by showing that hearing cannot heal everything but can keep the harm from being hidden.

encounters.title: The frost cord now leads from the Round Table to an unseen cup beyond the border

text_script.value: At the far end of the frost cord, the cup did not shine brighter; it seemed to listen. Arthur asked whether the Round Table would be a ring of oaths, a wall against Mordred's claim, or a doorway that stayed unfinished. Mordred answered that an unfinished ring was a weak one; Lancelot said a finished one would only be a stronger lock. Guinevere set her folded seat beside the empty cup and said that waiting had to remain a choice someone still made. Merlin held one hand over the cord and felt it asking for a name, while Morgan said the old magic kept not by touching but by refusing to be mistaken for destiny. Percival stood nearest the border, saying the widows' door was already open to whoever could knock without wanting to take something.
Send one witness to the border marker
A chosen witness crosses to the first marker and returns changed, forcing the court to decide whether witnessing is duty or trophy-seeking.
Leave seat, throne and cup visible but unmarked
Camelot becomes a practice of return rather than a monument, with the throne and Grail left deliberately unresolved.
Make the two unanswered names a public hearing
The court splits Arthur's peace from Mordred's claim while forcing every oath to name its cost before it can be kept.

encounters.title: Camelot remains open: the Grail is never seen, the Round Table is an ethics rath

text_script.value:
By the last candle, the frost did not divide the court; it asked each of them to stay answerable to the door. Mordred said a claim dies when it cannot be kept, Lancelot said witness is safer than possession, and Arthur answered that the Round Table would be a ring of questions that refused to close, not a lock around the Grail. Percival knocked twice at the widows' threshold, Guinevere left the seat empty, Morgan touched the old magic once and let it return to the dark, and Merlin saw no temple rise in the empty cup—only a court deciding what it would carry home.

The Grail never appears in the expected form. It does not descend, blaze, bless, or crown; it simply refuses to be owned, and in that refusal it disciplines the court. Arthur does not become a conqueror of the holy, Mordred does not become its master, and Lancelot does not turn witness into possession. The Round Table survives as an ethics rather than a monument: an open circle where love, duty, law, and memory are kept visible without being made into a trophy. Camelot remains neither a doomed ideal nor a finished temple, but a living question—what a just court owes those who are not yet safe—while the widows' door stays open, the sacred cup stays unseen, and the central mystery remains an obligation rather than an answer.
